10	
11	**SHIPPED + HARDWARE-VERIFIED 2026-10-11.** `ask set bob's first meal to 7:30`
12	and `ask set bob's dinner to 19:15` both landed, and `status.md` read back
13	`- scheduled meals: 07:30 12:30 19:15` — two separate agent turns, both
14	persisted to flash. Four agent-driven writes have now landed in total
15	(07:30 / 13:00 / 19:15 / 18:45). Firmware `9242daf64d1c9744f9d1ec917bf13d69`
16	(1563648 B) is the complete one; `3ad206ae3c0992c6da8ebacec20d0bf3`
17	(1563536 B) is the earlier build that wrote correctly but reported an error.
18	This is the path that replaces on-device voice for meal scheduling, which is
19	hardware-blocked (see [[velapaw-mic-capture]]).
20	
21	## The three pieces
22	
23	1. **`velapaw_meal_set_by_name(name, slot, minute)`** in
24	   `apps/examples/velapaw/identity/identity.c`. Pet ids are array indices that
25	   renumber on delete (`identity.h:52`), so a **name is the only stable handle**
26	   an agent or dialog can hold. It normalises both sides — lower-case, strip
27	   leading whitespace, trim trailing non-alphanumerics — because the enrolled
28	   pet on this board is literally `bob,` with a comma from the on-screen
29	   keyboard. The model sent `"pet": "bob"` and it matched; the normaliser
30	   earned its place on the first real call. Returns 0 / -1 bad args / -2 no
31	   such pet / -3 ambiguous / -4 rejected, else the save rc. It **copies all
32	   three slots** before writing one, because `velapaw_identity_update()` writes
33	   every slot it is handed; passing 0 for portion/limit means "leave alone".
34	2. **`vp_status_write()` publishes the meal times** as
35	   `- scheduled meals: HH:MM HH:MM HH:MM` (or `off`). This is why there is
36	   **no `get_meal_schedule` tool** — the agent already reaches `status.md`
37	   through `read_file`, so reading costs zero schema budget. That budget was
38	   hard-won (36→16 tools; see
39	   [[velapaw-ai-agent-integration-progress]]), and the write tool took it to 17
40	   builtin / Tools JSON 5245 B, still comfortable.
41	   **2026-10-13 (fix9): `status.md` is now also rewritten after every agent,
42	   Edit or voice-dialog change and pet delete.** Before, it refreshed only at
43	   boot and after a feed, so the agent read back times it had just changed —
44	   see [[velapaw-agent-on-lcd]].
45	3. **`set_meal_schedule`** in `packages/ai_agent/src/tools/tool_meal.c`.
46	   Declares `velapaw_meal_set_by_name` by hand with `extern` rather than
47	   including `identity.h` — same FLAT image so it links, and the header would
48	   drag in the app's whole include path. Accepts `pet`/`pet_name`/`name`,
49	   `slot`/`meal`, and either `"HH:MM"` or separate `hour`/`minute`. Its success
50	   string **states the Model-B gate explicitly** ("dispenses it only when %s is
51	   recognised at the bowl at or after that time"), or the model promises the
52	   owner food appears on the clock alone, which is false.
53	
54	## THE TRAP: `Local tool shortcut: skip LLM round`
55	
56	`agent_loop.c` ~1230 short-circuits the turn when a round has exactly one
57	"local" tool call: it hands the raw tool output to the user as the final reply
58	and never does another LLM round. **That structurally kills every two-step
59	plan.** First run of the new tool: the model correctly called `read_file` on
60	`status.md` to find the pet name, the shortcut fired, the owner got a raw
61	status dump, and the meal was never set — `iters=1 tools=1`, `status=ok`. It
62	looks like a successful turn.
63	
64	The fix was already half-written in the file: an `is_instruction_read` escape
65	hatch exists for exactly this reason (skill files, `AGENT_HEARTBEAT_FILE`), and
66	`list_dir` had already been pulled out of the local set for the same bug with
67	the same symptom. Added `strstr(path, "/velapaw/")` to that condition —
68	everything in `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/` (`status.md`, `feed_log.md`,
69	`history.bin`) is **data to reason over, never a finished answer**. Correct
70	trace afterwards is `iters=2 tools=2` with a `set_meal_schedule` step, and
71	`[agent] Skill file read — no shortcut` in the log. **Read that trace line
72	before believing a turn worked** — `status=ok iters=1` is the failure mode.
73	
74	Deliberately did NOT "fix" this by rewriting the tool description to make the
75	model skip the read. Read-then-write is the correct behaviour (right name,
76	current times) and must not depend on the model choosing to skip a step.
77	
78	## SOLVED: the HTTP 400 invalid unicode code point was a use-after-free
79	
80	Every successful write used to end with the owner seeing `Sorry, I encountered
81	an error`, because the round *after* `set_meal_schedule` returned was rejected
82	with `[llm] API error 400: … messages[N].content: invalid unicode code point`.
83	The write was already on flash, so a working action reported failure.
84	
85	**Root cause, in `tool_meal.c`:** `cJSON_Delete(root)` ran while `const char
86	*pet` still pointed **into** that tree, and all six `switch` branches format
87	`pet` afterwards. The success string therefore carried raw freed-heap bytes at
88	the `%s`, and DeepSeek rejected the whole request. Fix is three lines — copy
89	the name into a `char petbuf[64]` and repoint `pet` at the copy **before** the
90	delete; reassigning `pet` covers all six branches without renaming anything.
91	Verified 2026-10-11 on firmware `9242daf64d1c9744f9d1ec917bf13d69`
92	(1563648 B): `result: 151 bytes`, no sanitiser warning, `status=ok iters=3
93	tools=2` in 5 s, real owner-facing reply.
94	
95	**The byte arithmetic was the signal all along.** The log said `result: 163
96	bytes`; hand-counting the format string twice gave 151. I trusted the count and
97	hunted an encoder bug instead of asking why the gap existed. `"Meal 2 for "` is
98	11 bytes and the diagnostic reported only 13 valid — corruption began exactly
99	at the `%s`, which names the variable.
100	
101	**Two theories falsified on the way — do not re-derive either.** (1) History
102	truncation: first failure at column 8230 against `hist=8192` looked conclusive;
103	`session_clear_all` reproduced it at column 4536 in a 10286-byte body.
104	(2) A stale over-read of `tool_output`: `cJSON_AddStringToObject` passes bytes
105	through verbatim and takes its own `strlen`, and `agent_tool_exec_streamed`
106	(`static inline` in `src/core/agent_mem.h:278`) is a clean malloc/execute/
107	memcpy with no appending — the message holds exactly our NUL-terminated bytes.
108	Also wrong: re-indexing `messages[N]` onto the assistant message. `msg[0]
109	role=user` proves the **system prompt is not in the messages array**.
110	
111	**Kept as defence:** `utf8_valid_prefix()` + `add_clean_string()` in
112	`agent_loop.c` now sanitise all four content sites (assistant `content` and
113	`reasoning_content`, single- and parallel-tool results), logging `[agent]
114	UTF-8: trimmed N of M byte(s) from "<key>"`. That warning is what localised
115	this bug; a malformed string no longer hard-fails a turn. The companion
116	`msg[N] role=… len=… utf8ok=…` dump (the 25-line `DIAGNOSTIC (velapaw
117	2026-10-11)` block) was **removed 2026-10-13**: `agent_loop.c` `c1c8ebf1…` →
118	`1474c400505aa4e472d7a77bf3bbe73e`, image `0e51e11b5c61786c966ebe072015f04a`
119	(1,564,608 B, fix10 + this only), gates `grep -ac "utf8ok="` = 0 and
120	`grep -ac "UTF-8: trimmed"` = 1. Flashed on COM3 and hardware-verified
121	2026-10-13: `ask change bob's dinner to 18:20` → `END status=ok iters=3
122	tools=2` in 5 s, saved to flash, and no `msg[N]` lines printed. About 10 min
123	later, `ask set bob's launch to 12` (a typo and a bare hour) set slot 2 to
124	12:00. It took the same 3 iterations, 2 tools and 5 s, after the agent
125	reconnected on its own (`Pooled connection stale, reconnecting`). Rollback:
126	the fix10 golden's `app-sources.tar.gz` has the old `agent_loop.c`.
127	
128	## Verification discipline that worked
129	
130	- `grep -ac "set_meal_schedule" nuttx/nuttx.bin` + `grep -ac "scheduled meals"`
131	  + `nm nuttx/nuttx | grep -E "velapaw_meal_set_by_name|tool_meal_set_execute"`
132	  as flash gates.
133	- `cat /data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md` **before** any LLM call proves the
134	  VelaPaw half independently of the agent.
135	- The agent's reply text is never the discriminator — only `status.md` is. The
136	  model will happily narrate a write it never performed.
137	- `cat` does not exist at the `vela>` prompt; `quit` back to `nsh>` first.
138	- There is **no direct tool-invoke command** in the agent CLI (`help` lists
139	  none), so tool verification always costs an LLM round trip.
140	- **An ask that hangs after `REQ written` is the USB network, not this
141	  tool** — the CDC-NCM TX wedge, fixed by fix10 on 2026-10-13; see
142	  [[velapaw-ncm-tx-wedge]].
143

11	**Improvement item 8, SHIPPED 2026-10-13.** The user's goal: judges should see
12	the agent on the LCD instead of in a terminal — "watch the feeder change",
13	not "read the terminal".
14	
15	**Why:** this is the demo's centrepiece for the defense.
16	**How to apply:** demo with fresh sentences (see the cache note), judge success
17	by the `set_meal_schedule` trace line or `status.md`, never by the reply text,
18	and expect the toast within about a second of `ask`.
19	
20	## What is on the screen (item-8 patch, 6 files)
21	
22	Rollback copy: `~/velapaw-golden/pre-item8-agent-lcd/`.
23	
24	- **Toast under the bell for every `ask`:** "You: <question>" → "Agent
25	  working… N s" counting up → the reply. It stays 30 s; a tap dismisses it.
26	- **Heartbeat:** an all-clear is a green toast for 10 s. A warning is a red
27	  toast that stays, turns the bell red and is listed in the bell panel until
28	  the next all-clear. A *failed* heartbeat shows nothing, so a dead network at
29	  the offline defense doesn't clutter the screen.
30	- **Live My Pets:** an identity generation counter makes the card redraw on
31	  whatever tab is showing. An open Edit dialog picks up the change too, so
32	  pressing Save can't write the old time back. Before this, My Pets only
33	  redrew when you entered the tab.
34	- Bilingual; the Chinese strings use only glyphs already in the font subset
35	  ([[velapaw-i18n]]).
36	
37	## fix9 — why "the toast works but the times don't change"
38	
39	6 files: `store.h`, `store_stub.c`, `identity.c`, `ui_lvgl.c`,
40	`tool_registry.c`, `nsh_commands.c`. Rollback:
41	`~/velapaw-golden/pre-fix9-status-refresh/`. Image
42	`148bf5d5eff85947a89e00eaafd538c3`.
43	
44	- `status.md` is the agent's only source of meal times, and it was rewritten
45	  only at boot and after a feed — one turn after moving breakfast, the agent
46	  read the old time back. It is now also rewritten after an agent change, an
47	  Edit or voice-dialog save, and a pet delete.
48	- The model answered "Done" without calling `set_meal_schedule`. The tool
49	  description now says a meal changes only when the tool succeeds.
50	- `ask` text carried raw backspace/arrow-key bytes from the terminal; they are
51	  now applied or dropped before the message is sent.
52	- **Still open, not in fix9. SEEN ON HARDWARE 2026-10-13:** sending
53	  `ask change bob's dinner to 18:20` twice in a row gave `Cache hit, skipping
54	  LLM call` and `END status=ok iters=1 tools=0 … elapsed=0s`. It replayed
55	  "Done — … 18:20" without calling `set_meal_schedule`. That time it was
56	  harmless, since the meal already was 18:20. After an Edit-dialog change it
57	  would be a false "Done".
58	- **How the cache works** (`src/llm/llm_cache.c` and `include/llm/llm_cache.h`;
59	  values read from the D: checkout, which is upstream code we never modified):
60	  - It is RAM-only, with 8 slots.
61	  - Entries expire after 300 s, but **every hit re-stores the entry and
62	    restarts the 300 s**.
63	  - The key is a djb2 hash of the prompt's first 64 characters, with no string
64	    compare. Long asks that differ only after character 64 therefore collide.
65	  - The store is at `agent_loop.c` `send_reply:` (~line 1451). It is gated
66	    only on `LLM_COMPLEXITY_SIMPLE` and the non-heartbeat `cacheable` flag.
67	- **Fix** = add `&& trace.total_tool_calls == 0` to that store condition. That
68	  counter is what the END line prints as `tools=`. Not applied yet. Until then,
69	  use a fresh sentence, wait 5 minutes, or restart `ai_agent`.
70	
71	## Status
72	
73	Confirmed on hardware: the ask toast; My Pets updating live 12:00 → 12:30 with

1 English | 中文 2 3 # VelaPaw —— 端侧 AI 多宠智能喂食器 4 5 **队伍：** CircuitForge（`contest2026_043`） · **赛道：** AI 硬件产品创新 6 **平台：** openVela（NuttX），运行于 Waveshare **ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5-C** 7 **代码仓库：** [github.com/open-vela/contest2026_043_CircuitForge](https://github.com/open-vela/contest2026_043_CircuitForge) —— 源码已提交至大赛专属分支 **`dev-ai-contest-2026`** 8 9 --- 10 11 ## 演示视频 12 13 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7cf3a67b-49a3-45f4-a800-5e8f92b570e9 14 15 16 17 18 ▶ 如果上方的嵌入视频无法加载，可以[直接下载](VelaPaw_Demo.mp4)（93MB，MP4）。建议您下载视频以获得更好的画质。 19 20 --- 21 22 ## 一、作品简介 23 24 **VelaPaw 是一款智能宠物喂食器：它能识别出正站在食盆前的是*哪一只*宠物，并只投喂这只宠物当前应吃的那一餐——而所有 AI 全部在设备端本地运行。无需云端、无需手机、无需账号。** 25 26 在多宠家庭里，普通的定时喂食器分不清是哪只猫，结果往往是最贪吃的那只把大家的粮都吃了，定量管理根本无从谈起。VelaPaw 用和人一样的方式解决它：先"看"一眼动物、认出是谁，再只投喂它自己的那份口粮，并按它自己的时间表。由于摄像头、神经网络、时钟和投料机构全部自成一体，它在断网时照常工作，也绝不会把家里的画面上传到任何地方。 27 28 **核心亮点** 29 30 - 🐾 **逐只宠物识别** —— 端侧 INT8 神经网络凭面部识别每一只已登记的宠物，无需项圈或标签。 31 - 🍽️ **识别门控投喂** —— 只有当"识别到正确的宠物在食盆前"**且**"它的某一餐已到时间且未被跳过"时才投喂，且每餐每天至多一次。每一餐都可单独设置**跳过（skip-meal）**开关。 32 - 🗣️ **语音设置时间表** —— 投喂时间也可以直接说出来：由端侧关键词识别模型驱动的 MEAL→HOUR→CONFIRM 语音对话，可免触摸设置某只宠物的投喂时间。**没有唤醒词** —— 需先在编辑宠物页面点击开始，再用语音依次回答。VelaPaw 不含常驻语音唤醒功能，因此大赛"参赛须知与规则"中关于统一唤醒词的要求不适用于本项目。 33 - ⚖️ **份量与每日上限** —— 每只宠物可设定克数份量，并有每日投喂硬上限。 34 - 🩺 **健康监测** —— 第二个端侧网络估计体况（偏瘦 / 理想 / 偏胖），进食历史分析还会发出**食欲骤降告警**，这是疾病的早期信号。 35 - 🤖 **会主动开口的端侧 AI Agent** —— 板上运行 openVela `ai_agent` 框架，并加载自定义 Skill 读取*真实*的喂食记录。它按定时**自行推送**提醒：当某只宠物越过预警阈值时自动触发，无人值守、无需有人守在控制台前。设备不出声，就说明一切正常。详见[第四节](#四端侧-ai-agent唯一需要联网的部分)。 36 - 🕑 **真实计时** —— 硬件实时时钟（RTC）让投喂时间表在断电后依然准确。 37 - 🌐 **中英双语界面** —— 支持中文/英文，应用内可实时切换语言。 38 - 💾 **数据持久化** —— 已登记的宠物、时间表与宠物头像都能在断电后保留。 39 - 🖥️ **即开即用的家电体验** —— 上电直接进入触摸屏界面，无需连接串口控制台。 40 41 **为什么是现在：** 2026 年 3 月，小米推出了米家智能宠物喂食器 2 视觉版——一款面向大众市场的量产产品（众筹价 ¥449，零售价 ¥549），专门加入摄像头把 AI 视觉带进喂食场景。这等于是最懂宠物主人会为什么买单的公司，用真金白银的量产产品独立验证了 VelaPaw 立项时的核心判断——摄像头理应长在喂食器上。VelaPaw 在此基础上更进一步：从"看到食盆"到"认出是哪只宠物"，凭面部识别、完全端侧运行，无需 App、账号或云端。完整对比见项目介绍文档[§06 市场与价值](VelaPaw_Project_Intro_zh.pdf)。 42 43 --- 44 45 ## 二、端侧 AI（项目的核心） 46 47 识别采用的是**开集度量学习（open-set metric learning）**，而非固定类别的分类器。模型是一个通用的宠物特征提取器（MobileNetV3-Small 主干 + 空间注意力 TSFM 模块），它把一帧摄像头画面转换成一个经 L2 归一化的 128 维**嵌入向量**。登记一只宠物即保存其若干张照片的平均嵌入；识别就是用余弦相似度与已登记宠物做匹配。正因如此，**新增一只宠物无需重新训练**——登记本身就是一等公民的功能，识别质量取决于登记照片的质量，而不是被冻结的类别集合。 48 49 | | | 50 |---|---| 51 | **身份识别模型** | MobileNetV3-Small + TSFM 注意力，INT8，128 维嵌入，128×128 输入 | 52 | **体况评估模型** | 三分类（偏瘦/理想/偏胖）INT8 CNN | 53 | **推理运行时** | TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers（`apps/mlearning/tflite-micro`） | 54 | **加速** | 在 Xtensa LX7 上使用 ESP-NN SIMD 算子 → **约 1.3 秒/次推理**（参考算子约 6.75 秒） | 55 | **模型存放** | 运行时从闪存加载（1.4 MB 身份模型 @ `0x600000`，626 KB 体况模型 @ `0x760000`）——因体积过大无法内存映射，开机时读入 PSRAM | 56 57 两个模型均在设备外训练，训练/导出流程见 [`host/`](host/)（TensorFlow/Keras → INT8 训练后量化 → `.tflite`）。 58 59 --- 60

1 # Layout — how slides, flow and pinning compose 2 3 SKILL.md shows the common slide. Read this page when a layout needs more than a column of blocks and a card row. This page explains: 4 5 - The flow-vs-pin model 6 - The flex and grid idioms 7 - How to put labels over an image 8 - The few things the editor does with structure that affect how you should write the HTML 9 10 The page format.md lists the exact CSS properties you can use. 11 12 ## Two ways to place anything 13 14 A `
` is a 1920×1080 canvas. Its style controls both its background (the "paint") and its layout. 15 16 - `padding` is the slide margin. 128px is the standard margin. 17 - `display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap` stacks the child elements from top to bottom with space between them. 18 - `justify-content:center` centers the child elements vertically. 19 - `justify-content:flex-end` sinks the child elements to the bottom. 20 21 A section with no `display` style is a plain column with no gap. 22 23 There are two ways to place child elements inside a `
`: 24 25 - **Flow**: Flow children sit one after another in the section's layout. They are sized to fit their content unless you give them a `width`, `height`, or `flex` style. Open space appears wherever the flow leaves it. Open space LOW on a slide is correct. Do not reach for `justify-content:center` on every slide. 26 27 - **Pinned**: Pinned children have `position:absolute`. They leave the flow and sit where their `left`, `right`, `top`, and `bottom` styles say, relative to the section. Give them a `width` (text needs one to wrap), or pin both sides. Use pinned children only for the things flow cannot do: 28 - A source line at the bottom edge 29 - A badge over a corner 30 - A full-bleed photo behind everything, with `position:absolute; left:0; top:0; width:1920px; height:1080px; object-fit:cover`, listed first in the HTML so the other elements paint over it 31 - A magic-move element 32 33 Put everything else in the flow. 34 35 The order of elements in the HTML source is the order they paint. There is no `z-index`. List pinned backdrops first in the HTML. Inside a `position:relative` host, pinned children always paint over its flow content. The page format.md explains this in the "Slide" section. 36 37 ## Flex idioms 38 39 - **Card row**: Use `
` with `flex:1` on the children. This makes equal columns. The default `align-items:stretch` makes every card as tall as the tallest card. A card is a `
` with `display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:12px` plus its paint (background, border, radius, and padding). 40 - **Two columns, unequal**: Use `flex:2` and `flex:1`, or set `width:800px` on one and `flex:1` on the other. 41 - **Push apart**: Put an empty `
` between siblings, or use `justify-content:space-between` on the parent. 42 - **Bottom-anchored block**: Set `display:flex; flex-direction:column` on the section. There is no `margin` property. To make space above the block, put an empty `flex:1` spacer above it. 43 - **Centered block**, for a one-off slide (a statement, a quote, a closing line): `justify-content:center` on the section's column puts the block in the middle of the height; without it a short column hangs from the top, which is what a slide with a heading wants (next idiom). 44 - **A run of slides with one layout** (the content slides of a deck; one slide per region, per step, per option): the heading sits at the top margin on every one, at the same height, so it stays put when the viewer flips from slide to slide. Leave the section's column top-aligned — no `justify-content:center` — and spread or anchor the BODY below the heading instead: `justify-content:space-between`, or a `flex:1` spacer above the block you want low. Centering the whole column makes the heading's height depend on how much the slide holds, so it hops 20–60px between neighbouring slides — a common flaw in generated decks. A slide of a different kind in the run (a centered statement, quote or closing line with no heading above its body) is free to differ. See the content slides of `samples/data-deck.html`: every `

` lands at the same height. 45 - **Align a row's items**: Use `align-items:center` to center vertically in a row, `baseline` to line up text of different sizes on one line, or `flex-end`. 46 - **Big number + caption**: Use a column with gap 8. Set the number to 160–200px with `line-height:1`. Set the caption to 28–32px in the softened tone. 47 - **Bar chart, and a row of small bar charts**: every bar stands on ONE baseline. Give the bars a track of fixed height and bottom-align inside it — `
` holding the bar `
`s (each bar's `height` is its value × one scale for the whole slide) — and put the value above each bar, the category label and any note BELOW the track. When a slide has several groups side by side (plan vs actual per department, one mini-chart per region), every group uses the same track height and the same scale, so all the bars on the slide share one floor and the labels sit on one line under it. Never build a group as a top-aligned column with the bars first: short bars then hang from the top, float at different heights, and the labels land raggedly. A waterfall (bridge) chart is the one exception — its middle bars float on purpose, each starting where the previous one ended; its first and last bars still stand on the floor. See the "Monthly active accounts" slide in `samples/data-deck.html`. 48 - **Tree / linear flowchart**: Use flow for a straight chain or a small tree (at most two levels, four leaves); pin anything bigger, a bracket, or lines that join or cross. The page reference/diagrams.md has both idioms. 49 - **Widths**: Make every column, card, pill, and legend item at least as wide as its longest word. If not, the word breaks in the middle. The rule, the numbers, and the wrap opt-ins are in format.md in the "Text" section. 50 51 A `
` is invisible unless it has background, border or box-shadow. So you can group freely. A plain grouping `
` costs nothing visually. Fifteen `
` levels is the build cap (an empty, unpainted `
`, such as a `flex:1` spacer, does not count). Past three levels, the slide wants splitting. Revising a deck you do not know was made from the type, keep to 5: its page keeps the editor it was published with, and one from before the cap rose from 5 locks a deeper slide that `validate-content.ts` passes. 52 53 ## Grid idioms 54 55 Use `display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(3, 1fr); gap:32px`. This fills children into cells in row-major order. Use `grid-column:span 2` to widen one cell. 56 57 That is the whole grid vocabulary. You can see the supported CSS in format.md in the "Supported CSS" section: tracks of `px`, `fr`, `auto`, or `repeat(N, …)`, and one `gap`. No `minmax()`, `auto-fill`, named areas, or line numbers. 58 59 Use grid for KPI tiles, photo grids, feature matrices, and anything a flex row cannot keep square. Add `aspect-ratio:1` (or `4/3`) to the tiles. Row heights follow the content unless you set `grid-template-rows`. A table is usually better than a grid of text cells when the content is tabular. 60 61 **A matrix is ONE grid, not many columns.** Three columns — each holding a chip, a blurb, and a card — look like three column stacks. But they are one grid: `display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr)`. The nine children go in row-major order: chip, chip, chip, blurb, blurb, blurb, and so on. VelaPaw · CircuitForge · recognition

[0:45 · ends 4:55] Recognition is open-set metric learning, so the model never learned bob. It turns a 128 by 128 crop into a 128-number fingerprint, an L2-normalised embedding. Enrolling a pet stores five of these, and recognition is a cosine comparison against them, so adding a pet needs no retraining. The network is MobileNetV3-Small with a TSFM spatial-attention block, quantised to INT8. The attention block widened the margin between pets by a third, 0.324 against 0.243, and lowered the equal error rate from 0.328 to 0.291. With Espressif's ESP-NN kernels one recognition takes about 1.3 seconds instead of 6.75, and it runs on a background worker so the screen never freezes. We match at 0.45: bob scores between 0.53 and 0.84, and unknown cats stay at or below 0.22. The biggest lever against false accepts is good enrollment photos.

3	description: "VelaPaw voice meal-scheduling dialog — WORKING end to end on hardware (COMMIT meal 2 = 08:00; re-verified 2026-10-11 after the mic alignment fix, COMMIT meal 1 = 09:00 with the votes carrying the hour). 9	---
10	
11	The MEAL → HOUR → CONFIRM spoken dialog in the edit-pet modal
12	(`vsched_*` in `app/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c`), on the 14-label tiny_conv KWS
13	model. **WORKING end to end on hardware, build 68 (2026-08-06):**
14	
15	    heard two 0.773    -> step2
16	    heard eight 0.938  -> step3
17	    heard yes 0.957    -> COMMIT meal 2 = 08:00
18	
19	**9.6 s, three steps, two retries, zero false accepts.** See
20	[[velapaw-mic-capture]] for the capture path underneath it.
21	
22	## Constrained decode — threshold the RAW softmax, never renormalised
23	
24	Each step knows its legal answers (MEAL `{one,two,three}`, HOUR `{zero..nine}`,
25	CONFIRM `{yes,no}`) and `velapaw_kws_best_of()` takes the argmax over just
26	those. **The score returned is the raw probability, deliberately not
27	renormalised over the subset** — the mass sitting on `_silence_`/`_unknown_`
28	is exactly the mass meaning "that wasn't one of my words". Renormalising lets
29	86% of silence/OOV clips through the confirm step; the raw score, 4.9%.
30	
31	Confirmed live: the model heard `eight 0.957` at the MEAL step and best-of
32	returned `one 0.000`. That is the design working, not a bug.
33	
34	## Thresholds (hardware-tuned, build 56; still correct at b68)
35	
36	    MEAL 0.40    HOUR 0.55    CONFIRM 0.55    TIMEOUT 15000 ms    TRIES 5
37	
38	They came *down* from 0.45/0.73/0.59 because words through the ES8311 score
39	0.68–0.71 when correctly heard, not the ~0.99 the test split suggested.
40	A wrong hour is cheap (CONFIRM reads it back); a *rejected* hour is expensive
41	(burns a try, ends with nothing set).
42	
43	## The vote rule is load-bearing — it recovers whole dialogs
44	
45	`VSCHED_VOTES 2` + `VSCHED_VOTE_FLOOR 0.25` — a step also accepts a word it
46	heard twice below threshold. Votes, **not** a consecutive run (the b62 log that
47	motivated it had the repeats interrupted by a 0.176 reading). MEAL and HOUR
48	only; CONFIRM keeps the threshold alone since agreeing twice on a two-way
49	choice is as surprising as a coin landing the same way twice.
50	
51	Two hardware runs, two different regimes, and the rule matters in one of them:
52	
53	- **b68** — every accept cleared its threshold outright (0.773 / 0.938 / 0.957);
54	  `v` never got past 0. Looked like dead weight.
55	- **b69** — the HOUR step got `eight 0.395`, then `six 0.215`, then
56	  `eight 0.266`, and **the votes accepted the correct digit** from three
57	  readings that were all far under the 0.55 gate. Note the `six` in between:
58	  a consecutive-run counter would have reset on it and the dialog would have
59	  cancelled. That is exactly the b62 failure this rule was written for.
60	- **2026-10-11, md5 `0a23aa25…`** (the first build after the mic fix in
61	  [[velapaw-mic-capture]]): one 0.828 → `nine 0.352` then `nine 0.277`,
62	  accepted on votes → yes 0.945 → COMMIT meal 1 = 09:00. That's the b69
63	  regime again: the hour step only passed because of the votes. The chip's
64	  PGA was still at the stale 24 dB ([[velapaw-audio-gain]]).
65	
66	⚠️ Don't conclude from one good run that it isn't needed — that is the mistake
67	made after b68. Scores swing roughly 2× between sessions at what looks like
68	the same speaking volume (b68 peaks 0.94–0.96, b69 peaks 0.40–0.76), and the
69	rule is what covers the bad half.
70	
71	## 🔴 The UX fault that cost a whole test session
72	
73	An owner who answers MEAL with an hour ("eight") got only "say again" — the
74	subset decode is blind to everything outside the step, so the dialog *had* the
75	answer at 0.957 and didn't pass it on. Build 69 adds `S_VC_WRONG_FMT`:
76	when the **unconstrained** winner is a real word, illegal here, and scores
77	≥ `VSCHED_WRONG_SCORE 0.60`, say `heard "eight" - say 1 / 2 / 3`.
78	
79	0.60 sits **above** the 0.40/0.55 accept gates on purpose: this message makes a
80	claim about speech we chose *not* to act on, so it needs more evidence than
81	acting would, not less.
82	
83	## Rejections are supposed to happen
84	
85	Both retries in the good run were correct rejections of bad windows
86	(`silence 0.324` → `six 0.129`; `six 0.395` → `yes 0.223`). Don't chase them.
87	For a device that commits a feeding schedule, no-false-accept is the property
88	that matters — see also the deliberate choice in `vsched_commit()` to write the
89	modal's **scratch** copy, so voice never bypasses the Save/Cancel buttons.

11	**SHIPPED + HARDWARE-VERIFIED 2026-10-11.** `ask set bob's first meal to 7:30`
12	and `ask set bob's dinner to 19:15` both landed, and `status.md` read back
13	`- scheduled meals: 07:30 12:30 19:15` — two separate agent turns, both
14	persisted to flash. Four agent-driven writes have now landed in total
15	(07:30 / 13:00 / 19:15 / 18:45). Firmware `9242daf64d1c9744f9d1ec917bf13d69`
16	(1563648 B) is the complete one; `3ad206ae3c0992c6da8ebacec20d0bf3`
17	(1563536 B) is the earlier build that wrote correctly but reported an error.
18	This is the path that replaces on-device voice for meal scheduling, which is
19	hardware-blocked (see [[velapaw-mic-capture]]).
20	
21	## The three pieces
22	
23	1. **`velapaw_meal_set_by_name(name, slot, minute)`** in
24	   `apps/examples/velapaw/identity/identity.c`. Pet ids are array indices that
25	   renumber on delete (`identity.h:52`), so a **name is the only stable handle**
26	   an agent or dialog can hold. It normalises both sides — lower-case, strip
27	   leading whitespace, trim trailing non-alphanumerics — because the enrolled
28	   pet on this board is literally `bob,` with a comma from the on-screen
29	   keyboard. The model sent `"pet": "bob"` and it matched; the normaliser
30	   earned its place on the first real call. Returns 0 / -1 bad args / -2 no
31	   such pet / -3 ambiguous / -4 rejected, else the save rc. It **copies all
32	   three slots** before writing one, because `velapaw_identity_update()` writes
33	   every slot it is handed; passing 0 for portion/limit means "leave alone".
34	2. **`vp_status_write()` publishes the meal times** as
35	   `- scheduled meals: HH:MM HH:MM HH:MM` (or `off`). This is why there is
36	   **no `get_meal_schedule` tool** — the agent already reaches `status.md`
37	   through `read_file`, so reading costs zero schema budget. That budget was
38	   hard-won (36→16 tools; see
39	   [[velapaw-ai-agent-integration-progress]]), and the write tool took it to 17
40	   builtin / Tools JSON 5245 B, still comfortable.
41	   **2026-10-13 (fix9): `status.md` is now also rewritten after every agent,
42	   Edit or voice-dialog change and pet delete.** Before, it refreshed only at
43	   boot and after a feed, so the agent read back times it had just changed —
44	   see [[velapaw-agent-on-lcd]].
45	3. **`set_meal_schedule`** in `packages/ai_agent/src/tools/tool_meal.c`.
46	   Declares `velapaw_meal_set_by_name` by hand with `extern` rather than
47	   including `identity.h` — same FLAT image so it links, and the header would
48	   drag in the app's whole include path. Accepts `pet`/`pet_name`/`name`,
49	   `slot`/`meal`, and either `"HH:MM"` or separate `hour`/`minute`. Its success
50	   string **states the Model-B gate explicitly** ("dispenses it only when %s is
51	   recognised at the bowl at or after that time"), or the model promises the
52	   owner food appears on the clock alone, which is false.
53	
54	## THE TRAP: `Local tool shortcut: skip LLM round`
55	
56	`agent_loop.c` ~1230 short-circuits the turn when a round has exactly one
57	"local" tool call: it hands the raw tool output to the user as the final reply
58	and never does another LLM round. **That structurally kills every two-step
59	plan.** First run of the new tool: the model correctly called `read_file` on
60	`status.md` to find the pet name, the shortcut fired, the owner got a raw
61	status dump, and the meal was never set — `iters=1 tools=1`, `status=ok`. It
62	looks like a successful turn.
63	
64	The fix was already half-written in the file: an `is_instruction_read` escape
65	hatch exists for exactly this reason (skill files, `AGENT_HEARTBEAT_FILE`), and
66	`list_dir` had already been pulled out of the local set for the same bug with
67	the same symptom. Added `strstr(path, "/velapaw/")` to that condition —
68	everything in `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/` (`status.md`, `feed_log.md`,
69	`history.bin`) is **data to reason over, never a finished answer**. Correct
70	trace afterwards is `iters=2 tools=2` with a `set_meal_schedule` step, and
71	`[agent] Skill file read — no shortcut` in the log. **Read that trace line
72	before believing a turn worked** — `status=ok iters=1` is the failure mode.
73	
74	Deliberately did NOT "fix" this by rewriting the tool description to make the
75	model skip the read. Read-then-write is the correct behaviour (right name,
76	current times) and must not depend on the model choosing to skip a step.
77	
78	## SOLVED: the HTTP 400 invalid unicode code point was a use-after-free
79	
80	Every successful write used to end with the owner seeing `Sorry, I encountered
81	an error`, because the round *after* `set_meal_schedule` returned was rejected
82	with `[llm] API error 400: … messages[N].content: invalid unicode code point`.
83	The write was already on flash, so a working action reported failure.
84	
85	**Root cause, in `tool_meal.c`:** `cJSON_Delete(root)` ran while `const char
86	*pet` still pointed **into** that tree, and all six `switch` branches format
87	`pet` afterwards. The success string therefore carried raw freed-heap bytes at
88	the `%s`, and DeepSeek rejected the whole request. Fix is three lines — copy
89	the name into a `char petbuf[64]` and repoint `pet` at the copy **before** the
90	delete; reassigning `pet` covers all six branches without renaming anything.
91	Verified 2026-10-11 on firmware `9242daf64d1c9744f9d1ec917bf13d69`
92	(1563648 B): `result: 151 bytes`, no sanitiser warning, `status=ok iters=3
93	tools=2` in 5 s, real owner-facing reply.
94	
95	**The byte arithmetic was the signal all along.** The log said `result: 163
96	bytes`; hand-counting the format string twice gave 151. I trusted the count and
97	hunted an encoder bug instead of asking why the gap existed. `"Meal 2 for "` is
98	11 bytes and the diagnostic reported only 13 valid — corruption began exactly
99	at the `%s`, which names the variable.
100	
101	**Two theories falsified on the way — do not re-derive either.** (1) History
102	truncation: first failure at column 8230 against `hist=8192` looked conclusive;
103	`session_clear_all` reproduced it at column 4536 in a 10286-byte body.
104	(2) A stale over-read of `tool_output`: `cJSON_AddStringToObject` passes bytes
105	through verbatim and takes its own `strlen`, and `agent_tool_exec_streamed`
106	(`static inline` in `src/core/agent_mem.h:278`) is a clean malloc/execute/
107	memcpy with no appending — the message holds exactly our NUL-terminated bytes.
108	Also wrong: re-indexing `messages[N]` onto the assistant message. `msg[0]
109	role=user` proves the **system prompt is not in the messages array**.
110	
111	**Kept as defence:** `utf8_valid_prefix()` + `add_clean_string()` in
112	`agent_loop.c` now sanitise all four content sites (assistant `content` and
113	`reasoning_content`, single- and parallel-tool results), logging `[agent]
114	UTF-8: trimmed N of M byte(s) from "<key>"`. That warning is what localised
115	this bug; a malformed string no longer hard-fails a turn. The companion
116	`msg[N] role=… len=… utf8ok=…` dump (the 25-line `DIAGNOSTIC (velapaw
117	2026-10-11)` block) was **removed 2026-10-13**: `agent_loop.c` `c1c8ebf1…` →
118	`1474c400505aa4e472d7a77bf3bbe73e`, image `0e51e11b5c61786c966ebe072015f04a`
119	(1,564,608 B, fix10 + this only), gates `grep -ac "utf8ok="` = 0 and
120	`grep -ac "UTF-8: trimmed"` = 1. Flashed on COM3 and hardware-verified
121	2026-10-13: `ask change bob's dinner to 18:20` → `END status=ok iters=3
122	tools=2` in 5 s, saved to flash, and no `msg[N]` lines printed. About 10 min
123	later, `ask set bob's launch to 12` (a typo and a bare hour) set slot 2 to
124	12:00. It took the same 3 iterations, 2 tools and 5 s, after the agent
125	reconnected on its own (`Pooled connection stale, reconnecting`). Rollback:
126	the fix10 golden's `app-sources.tar.gz` has the old `agent_loop.c`.
127	
128	## Verification discipline that worked
129	
130	- `grep -ac "set_meal_schedule" nuttx/nuttx.bin` + `grep -ac "scheduled meals"`
131	  + `nm nuttx/nuttx | grep -E "velapaw_meal_set_by_name|tool_meal_set_execute"`
132	  as flash gates.
133	- `cat /data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md` **before** any LLM call proves the
134	  VelaPaw half independently of the agent.
135	- The agent's reply text is never the discriminator — only `status.md` is. The
136	  model will happily narrate a write it never performed.
137	- `cat` does not exist at the `vela>` prompt; `quit` back to `nsh>` first.
138	- There is **no direct tool-invoke command** in the agent CLI (`help` lists
139	  none), so tool verification always costs an LLM round trip.
140	- **An ask that hangs after `REQ written` is the USB network, not this
141	  tool** — the CDC-NCM TX wedge, fixed by fix10 on 2026-10-13; see
142	  [[velapaw-ncm-tx-wedge]].

10	
11	**Improvement item 8, SHIPPED 2026-10-13.** The user's goal: judges should see
12	the agent on the LCD instead of in a terminal — "watch the feeder change",
13	not "read the terminal".
14	
15	**Why:** this is the demo's centrepiece for the defense.
16	**How to apply:** demo with fresh sentences (see the cache note), judge success
17	by the `set_meal_schedule` trace line or `status.md`, never by the reply text,
18	and expect the toast within about a second of `ask`.
19	
20	## What is on the screen (item-8 patch, 6 files)
21	
22	Rollback copy: `~/velapaw-golden/pre-item8-agent-lcd/`.
23	
24	- **Toast under the bell for every `ask`:** "You: <question>" → "Agent
25	  working… N s" counting up → the reply. It stays 30 s; a tap dismisses it.
26	- **Heartbeat:** an all-clear is a green toast for 10 s. A warning is a red
27	  toast that stays, turns the bell red and is listed in the bell panel until
28	  the next all-clear. A *failed* heartbeat shows nothing, so a dead network at
29	  the offline defense doesn't clutter the screen.
30	- **Live My Pets:** an identity generation counter makes the card redraw on
31	  whatever tab is showing. An open Edit dialog picks up the change too, so
32	  pressing Save can't write the old time back. Before this, My Pets only
33	  redrew when you entered the tab.
34	- Bilingual; the Chinese strings use only glyphs already in the font subset
35	  ([[velapaw-i18n]]).
36	
37	## fix9 — why "the toast works but the times don't change"
38	
39	6 files: `store.h`, `store_stub.c`, `identity.c`, `ui_lvgl.c`,
40	`tool_registry.c`, `nsh_commands.c`. Rollback:
41	`~/velapaw-golden/pre-fix9-status-refresh/`. Image
42	`148bf5d5eff85947a89e00eaafd538c3`.
43	
44	- `status.md` is the agent's only source of meal times, and it was rewritten
45	  only at boot and after a feed — one turn after moving breakfast, the agent
46	  read the old time back. It is now also rewritten after an agent change, an
47	  Edit or voice-dialog save, and a pet delete.
48	- The model answered "Done" without calling `set_meal_schedule`. The tool
49	  description now says a meal changes only when the tool succeeds.
50	- `ask` text carried raw backspace/arrow-key bytes from the terminal; they are
51	  now applied or dropped before the message is sent.
52	- **Still open, not in fix9. SEEN ON HARDWARE 2026-10-13:** sending
53	  `ask change bob's dinner to 18:20` twice in a row gave `Cache hit, skipping
54	  LLM call` and `END status=ok iters=1 tools=0 … elapsed=0s`. It replayed
55	  "Done — … 18:20" without calling `set_meal_schedule`. That time it was
56	  harmless, since the meal already was 18:20. After an Edit-dialog change it
57	  would be a false "Done".
58	- **How the cache works** (`src/llm/llm_cache.c` and `include/llm/llm_cache.h`;
59	  values read from the D: checkout, which is upstream code we never modified):
60	  - It is RAM-only, with 8 slots.
61	  - Entries expire after 300 s, but **every hit re-stores the entry and
62	    restarts the 300 s**.
63	  - The key is a djb2 hash of the prompt's first 64 characters, with no string
64	    compare. Long asks that differ only after character 64 therefore collide.
65	  - The store is at `agent_loop.c` `send_reply:` (~line 1451). It is gated
66	    only on `LLM_COMPLEXITY_SIMPLE` and the non-heartbeat `cacheable` flag.
67	- **Fix** = add `&& trace.total_tool_calls == 0` to that store condition. That
68	  counter is what the END line prints as `tools=`. Not applied yet. Until then,
69	  use a fresh sentence, wait 5 minutes, or restart `ai_agent`.
70	
71	## Status
72	
73	Confirmed on hardware: the ask toast; My Pets updating live 12:00 → 12:30 with
74	no reboot; fix9. After fix10 ([[velapaw-ncm-tx-wedge]]), three back-to-back
75	asks (13:15 / 14:00 / 13:45) all landed in 4–9 s, and the user confirmed My
76	Pets then showed the last one, 13:45. The heartbeat toast, the
77	Edit-dialog-open case and the backspace case were on the to-test list and are
78	not confirmed in the notes. Asks queue FIFO (16 deep) and run one at a time,
79	so typing several in a row is fine.
80	
81	**A second ask stalling after `REQ written` was the USB network, not the
82	agent** — see [[velapaw-ncm-tx-wedge]].
83

CLI half: `ask which of my pets should I be worried about today and what should I do` → `iters=3 tools=2 llm_ms=6830`, four tool executions (`read_file` skill → `get_current_time` → `read_file` status.md → `read_file` feed_log.md), bodies 8898 → 10643 → 11970, no cache replay, and an answer that independently reached the same verdict as the heartbeat: Jay fine at 68 % of baseline, **Bob flagged at 33 % (10 g vs a 30 g baseline), below the skill's 50 % threshold**, with four concrete actions. Artifacts in `velapaw-snapshots\2026-09-04-ai-agent-sessionfix\` (`ask_capture.py`, `bringup.py`, `ask_capture6_raw.log`, both run outputs, `nuttx-maxargs.bin` + md5).
149	
150	**`ask` was silently truncating at seven words — `#define MAX_ARGS 8` in `nsh_commands.c`.** `cmd_ask` rejoins `argv[1..argc-1]`, and `tokenise()` stops at `max_argc`, so a 15-word question reached the model as `which of my pets should I be` and it correctly replied that the message looked garbled. Fixed to 32. **How the diagnosis was pinned, because the first one was wrong:** I blamed CDCACM flow control and added per-character typing with an echo check. The echo check is what cleared the wire — but the decisive evidence was a **cache hit on the second run** (`llm_ms=0`): `llm_cache` hashes the first 64 chars (`djb2_hash`, `LLM_CACHE_KEY_LEN`), so a hit proves both runs delivered byte-identical content and the loss was a fixed buffer, not the serial link. **A cache hit is a free byte-for-byte equality test between two runs — use it.** The slow-typing code was left in place but addressed a cause that wasn't there.
151	
152	**"Stale console history suppresses tool calls" — I RECORDED THIS AS CONFIRMED OFF ONE OBSERVATION AND IT DID NOT HOLD.** The original claim: same firmware, same question, 20 min apart, stale `tg_console.jsonl` → `iters=1 tools=0` and an answer that missed Bob; cleared → `iters=3 tools=2` and the right answer. **Two later control runs with stale history never reproduced `tools=0`** — both called tools and failed for an entirely different reason (a broken `list_dir`, below). One A/B with a confounded variable is not a mechanism. **The real defect chain was in the tools, not the history**, and the correct answer now comes back *with* stale history in place. Keep the general caution — a turn about current device state *can* in principle be answered from replayed history — but treat it as unproven on this device. **The lesson worth more than the finding: do not write a single observation into memory as a confirmed mechanism when the two runs differed in more than one variable.**
153	
154	**`list_dir` was broken two ways at once, and the shortcut turned that into a wrong answer delivered to the user — fixed 2026-09-04, hardware-verified.** (1) The prefix was matched against the *absolute* path (`/data/ai_agent/velapaw`) while the model passes a *relative* one (`velapaw`), so every entry was filtered out; worse, the `continue` ran **before** the recursive call, so non-matching directories were never descended into. (2) `list_dir` sat in the local-tool shortcut set in `agent_loop.c`, so its empty result **ended the turn and was handed to the user as the answer** — a user asking which pet to worry about literally received `(no files found)`. Fixes: match the prefix against **either** the relative or the absolute path (`strncmp(full_path,…) || strncmp(rel,…)`), always recurse, and drop `list_dir` from the shortcut set. Also added: no shortcut when tool output starts with `"Error: "` (the `tool_files.c` convention is `Error: …`/`OK: …` at every one of ~20 sites). **My own trap, worth repeating: I first replaced absolute matching with relative matching — fixing the case I had observed and breaking the case I hadn't. I considered accepting both while designing it and then didn't implement it.** Across three hardware runs the model used three different call shapes (`"velapaw"`, `"/data/ai_agent/"`, no prefix at all) — **a tool that only handles the spelling you happened to observe will look fixed and then fail**; the passing run used no prefix, so the both-forms branch is proven by code reading, not by that run.
155	
156	**Forcing a re-read beats trimming history.** Added to `build_messages` in `agent_loop.c`: when history is non-empty, append a mid-array `{"role":"system"}` message before the user turn saying device state may have changed, any earlier figure is stale, and to re-read the relevant files before answering about present state. Mid-array system messages are already used in this file (lines ~813, ~983) and DeepSeek accepts them. Guard is free: heartbeat blanks `history_json` → `cJSON_Parse` NULL → empty array → skipped. Result with stale history still on disk: `iters=3 tools=2`, both `read_file`s on the real files, answer opens *"Now I have the current feeding data"* and flags Bob correctly. **`AGENT_AI_AGENT_MAX_HISTORY` (10, `agent_config.h:108`) was NOT trimmed — it stays the fallback lever if this regresses.**
157	
158	**Cutting a tool leaves callers behind — the NL fast paths in `agent_loop.c` dispatched to five removed tools, fixed + hardware-verified 2026-09-04 (`cd2b4edd3baf27b25edae5db200ffe4a`).** `handle_nl_fast_path` runs *before* the LLM and returns its result as the final answer, so a shortcut pointing at an unregistered tool ends the turn with garbage. Three separate sites, and **finding them needed one grep, not code reading**: `grep -n 'get_heartrate\|get_steps\|get_wear_state\|vibrate\|music_\|feishu_\|quickapp' agent_loop.c` — run it after ANY change to `s_excluded_tools`, and require it to come back empty.
159	1. **The `s_intents[]` table** — five dead rows (`get_heartrate`, `get_steps`, `music_pause`, `music_stop`, `music_resume`). `calloc` + a failed `tool_registry_execute` leaves the buffer zeroed, so the user got an empty reply with the LLM skipped. Rows removed, plus a **general guard**: `if (reply && reply[0] == '\0') { free(reply); reply = NULL; }` so any future missing tool falls through to the LLM instead of answering blank.
160	2. **A hand-written music block** (~60 lines, `kw_play` → `music_search` → `music_play`). **The guard could not have saved this one** — on failure it `snprintf`s `"找到了 %s - %s，但播放失败: %s"`, i.e. a confident *non-empty* wrong sentence, or `strncpy`s the zeroed `search_result` into a 4096 B buffer. Deleted entirely.
161	3. **`inject_session_context` still told the model about `feishu_send_mention`/`feishu_chat_members`** in the system prompt of **every** request — dead bytes working against the request-size fix, plus an invitation to call tools that don't exist. Removed along with the `[mentioned_users: …]` paragraph (Feishu-only, and no Feishu channel is built).
162	Verified directly, not by inference: `ask play some music for my cat` → `NL fast path fired: NO`, one LLM round, `END status=ok`, and a real answer ("I don't have the ability to play music directly") that still knew Bob and Jay from session context. The digest path was re-run unchanged: `iters=3 tools=2`, both files read, `cache replay: no`, Bob correctly flagged at 33 %. **Image size is a usable signal here for once** — 1567872 → 1567632 (table) → 1567152 (music+prompt); an earlier rebuild after a *refused* patch came out at the unchanged 1567872 and I nearly mistook its new md5 (`e85d67fe…`, a build-timestamp difference) for the fix. **Process failure worth keeping: I scoped this fix three times and was wrong twice** — first "two dead entries" (the table had five), then "the table" (two more sites sat outside it). The grep above was available from the start.
163	
164	**`Ethernet 2` can silently reroute board traffic into the VPN — and "0 % loss" does not mean the board answered.** A run that ended `END status=timeout llm_ms=480920` (exactly `AGENT_LLM_SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SEC`) was not a model problem: the board's USB Ethernet link was down, so `Get-NetIPInterface` showed `ConnectionState: Disconnected`, 192.168.137.1 sat at `AddressState: Tentative` (DAD never completed ⇒ unusable as a source ⇒ **all routes on that interface are skipped**), and Windows fell through to WireGuard's `128.0.0.0/1`. **My own false pass: `ping -n 2` reported `Received = 2, Lost = 0 (0% loss)` while every reply read `Reply from 10.234.0.0: Destination port unreachable` — ICMP errors from the tunnel. Read the reply source address, never the loss percentage.** The full green checklist before any ask: adapter `Up`/`Connected` with a non-zero LinkSpeed, 192.168.137.1 `Preferred`, `Find-NetRoute -RemoteIPAddress 192.168.137.2` selecting `Ethernet 2`, ping replies **from 192.168.137.2**, `Get-NetNeighbor` `Reachable`. No route change was needed — resetting the board and re-running `ifconfig` fixed all five. `scratchpad\bringup.py` does the board half and deliberately stops before starting the agent so the link can be checked in between.
165	
166	**`D:\openVela\packages\ai_agent` is now materially behind the VM and must not be used to author patches** — three anchor misses in one session (`llm_proxy.c` `#include <stdio.h>`, `AGENT_LLM_TIMEOUT_SEC` 60 vs 180, `AGENT_LLM_SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SEC` 120 vs 480). `D:` is what ships to the contest repo, so it needs one clean VM→D: sync of that package before submission, then a diff to confirm nothing unintended rode along.

11	VelaPaw **Trends tab** reworked to match a shared product mockup, running on the ESP32-S3 (2026-07-21). Three stacked cards, all in `app/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c` (build_trends/refresh_trends + helpers). Bilingual via [[velapaw-i18n]]. Confirmed good on the panel ("perfect").
12	
13	## What's there
14	1. **Colored intake bars** — the existing `lv_chart` BAR, recolored per-bar: green if that day >= the window average, blue if below (the colour split IS the baseline, so no separate average line). Avg is computed over **completed days only** (exclude today = last index; today is often 0 g and would drag the mean so every past day reads above-average = all green).
15	2. **Appetite trend** — a second `lv_chart` LINE card: each day's intake as % of the pet's `daily_limit_g` (0-100), COL_ACCENT line.
16	3. **BCS gauge** — a 3-zone semicircular dial: three `lv_arc` bands (amber Under 180-240°, green Ideal 240-300°, red Over 300-360°; LVGL arc 0°=3 o'clock, CW, so 180-360 = top half) + an `lv_line` needle + a hub. GA_D=150, arc width 18, needle width 7 **white** for a real reading / grey for "no reading", white-ringed hub, big class label below. Needle tip offsets are hardcoded per class (only 3 classes) — no trig/math.h: under=(-54,-31), ideal=(0,-62), over=(54,-31), NA=(0,-36).
17	
18	## LVGL 9.1 API gotchas (each cost a cycle — the console is dead during any wedge, so it's build+flash+eyeball only)
19	- **Per-bar chart colour**: use the `LV_EVENT_DRAW_TASK_ADDED` event + `lv_obj_add_flag(chart, LV_OBJ_FLAG_SEND_DRAW_TASK_EVENTS)`. In 9.1 read the base dsc via **`task->draw_dsc`** (the getter `lv_draw_task_get_draw_dsc()` is **9.2-only** → undefined reference at link). `lv_draw_task_get_fill_dsc()` DOES exist in 9.1. The point index is **`base->id1`** (NOT id2 — id2 is the series index; with a single series id2 is always 0 → every bar reads vals[0] → all one colour).
20	- **No `lv_meter`** in 9.x. `lv_scale` exists and `lv_scale_set_line_needle_value` IS in 9.1, but the section range/style setters are NOT (they're later) — so I built the coloured zones from stacked `lv_arc` instead of lv_scale sections.
21	- Forward-declare `refresh_bcs_gauge` before refresh_trends (it's defined after, but called by it).
22	
23	## Data note
24	BCS (`velapaw_store_get_bcs`) is a 3-class score set only when a pet is **recognized** (the 2nd model majority-votes). Empty demo data → gauge shows grey "-" (no reading). To demo the needle swinging, recognize a pet on the Recognize tab first. No per-day BCS history is stored, so the mockup's little BCS sparkline was NOT built.

71	### 2.2 Custom Skill (基础要求 §2)
72	
73	**`velapaw-feeding-digest`** — installed at `/data/ai_agent/skills/velapaw-feeding-digest.md`,
74	alongside the 10 built-in skills.
75	
76	It teaches the agent VelaPaw's domain: where the feeding records live, what the
77	columns mean, and — critically — **what counts as a concern**:
78	
79	```
80	4. Flag a concern ONLY if any of these is true:
81	   - appetite below 50 percent of baseline
82	   - grams today reached the owner daily limit
83	   - body condition is not ideal
84	   - no feed event today in the log
85	5. Otherwise say the pet is on track, one sentence.
86	6. Use only numbers from those files. Never invent.
87	```
88	
89	The explicit thresholds are what make the output actionable rather than a
90	restatement of the log, and rule 6 is what keeps a language model from
91	inventing plausible-looking grams.
92	
93	**The data bridge** is a deliberate design choice: VelaPaw's C application
94	writes its feeding and body-condition history to plain Markdown at
95	`/data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md` and `feed_log.md`. The agent reads them with
96	the ordinary `read_file` tool — no custom tool, no IPC, no shared memory. The
97	app and the agent stay decoupled, and the same files are human-readable when
98	debugging.
99	
100	### 2.3 Proactive + execution scenario (基础要求 §3)
101	
102	**Type: 定时主动 (scheduled) with 阈值主动 (threshold) decision logic.**
103	
104	The `ai_agent` **heartbeat** service — not `cron` — is the proactive path. Every
105	30 minutes it feeds `/data/ai_agent/HEARTBEAT.md` to the agent as a `system`
106	message:
107	
108	```markdown
109	# Heartbeat
110	周期性检查任务（agent 定期执行）：
111	- [ ] Run the VelaPaw Feeding Digest skill.
112	If it finds a concern, notify the owner with numbers.
113	If all is on track, reply HEARTBEAT_OK only.
114	```
115	
116	Each firing is a full agentic run: the agent loads the skill, calls `read_file`
117	on the two data files, applies the threshold rules, and either pushes a warning
118	or answers `HEARTBEAT_OK`. **Silence is the normal case** — the device speaks
119	only when a threshold is crossed, which is what makes the alert worth reading.
120	
121	Captured unattended on hardware: `iters=4 tools=3`, four `read_file` calls,
122	request bodies growing 15 592 → 16 209 → 17 697 → 18 760 B as tool results
123	accumulated. Verified genuinely live, not replayed, by enrolling a new pet
124	mid-run and watching the next firing find it.
125	
126	### 2.4 Bonus: memory across sessions (进阶要求 §2)
127	
128	`session_mgr` persists every conversation to
129	`/data/ai_agent/sessions/tg_<chat_id>.jsonl` on littlefs, so context survives a
130	**power cut**, not merely a process restart — the constrained-storage case the
131	guide asks about. Chats are namespaced by `chat_id` (`console`, `heartbeat`),
132	so the CLI conversation and the proactive channel keep separate histories.
133	
134	Cross-session memory cuts both ways, and handling that is part of the work: a
135	device whose *state changes between turns* must not answer today's question
136	from yesterday's reply. See §3.3.
137	
138	### 2.5 Bonus: custom LVGL application (进阶要求 §3)
139	
140	VelaPaw ships a complete touchscreen LVGL application — enrollment, schedules,
141	trends, bilingual EN/中文 UI — described in the [main README](../README.md). The
142	agent runs on the same device and reads the same data the UI displays.

VelaPaw · CircuitForge · voice

14	**0.750**, silence correctly rejected. Every earlier result was weak
15	(b46: yes 0.539, no 0.715) because of the two defects below, both in capture,
16	neither in the model.
17	
18	## ✅ SOLVED 2026-10-11 — ROOT CAUSE: PSRAM RX buffer alignment (software, not hardware)
19	
20	**Forensic proof, from the Aug 2–6 `RXDUMP` logs in the session transcript**
21	(the only builds that printed the RX descriptor buffer address —
22	`VELAPAW_I2S_PROBES=1`): all **18 stalled runs** had `d[0] buf` ≡ **8 mod 16**
23	(0x3c4bdb48/…58, 0x3c510668/…88); all **13 runs that delivered audio** had it
24	≡ **0 mod 16** (0x3c4bfc40, 0x3c4c1cb0, 0x3c512ed0, 0x3c50ee40 …). No
25	exceptions. mod 32 does NOT separate them (working runs sit at both 0 and 16),
26	so the rule is exactly 16 B — the GDMA `IN_EXT_MEM_BK_SIZE` default.
27	
28	**Mechanism.** The mic node `/dev/audio/pcm_in0` is an **es8311** lower half
29	with `allocbuffer = NULL`, so `nuttx/audio/audio.c` `audio_allocbuffer()` calls
30	libc `apb_alloc()` directly. **A fix in the I2S driver's
31	`AUDIOIOC_ALLOCBUFFER` case would never run** — that path is only reached via
32	`audio_i2s.c`, which this board does not register. `apb_alloc` does
33	`lib_umemalign(MAX(up_get_dcache_linesize(), 1), n)`; without
34	`CONFIG_ARCH_DCACHE` the linesize is 0 → alignment 1 → plain malloc → 8 B.
35	`esp32s3_dma_setup()` rounds PSRAM RX *lengths* to 16 (the 4080+16 split in
36	`desc 80000ff0 80000010` is the proof the buffer is in PSRAM) but never
37	aligns the *address*. Misaligned PSRAM target → descriptor 0 never completes
38	(owner 1, length 0, no EOF, raw `000000a0`; the later probe builds showed
39	`0000000f`).
40	
41	**Why it posed as hardware.** `samp = apb + 0x98` and the record buffers are
42	allocated back-to-back with a stride that is a multiple of 16 (0x20a0), so
43	ONE coin flip on the first apb's address decides the WHOLE boot. Identical
44	addresses repeat run after run for a given build + heap history, so a layout
45	that lands on 8 fails every time. Boot-time allocations depend on /data
46	contents (pets, history, UI objects), so flashing the Aug b82 image did NOT
47	restore the Aug heap — the 2026-09-22 "known-good image fails ⇒ hardware"
48	inference below never controlled for heap layout. Fits everything: b81's
49	"3 of 5 cold boots", "bad from the FIRST capture", kicks never recovering, TX
50	unaffected, the RESET-tap stall.
51	
52	**Fix (2026-10-11, CONFIRMED on hardware — see below):** in
53	`~/openvela/nuttx/libs/libc/audio/lib_buffer.c`, `MAX(up_get_dcache_linesize(), 1)`
54	→ `MAX(…, 64)` (64 covers every ext-mem block size and keeps buffers on
55	whole 32-B cache lines). Backup `~/lib_buffer.c.pre-rxalign`. **VM-only patch
56	— `repo sync` will eat it.** libc joins the stale-object list
57	([[velapaw-stale-libarch-trap]]): `find libs/libc -name lib_buffer.o -delete;
58	rm -f libs/libc/libc.a staging/libc.a` (objects build in `libs/libc/bin/`).
59	Build gate: `xtensa-esp32s3-elf-objdump -d --disassemble=apb_alloc nuttx |
60	grep -B4 '<memalign>'` must show `a10, 64` (stale object shows `a10, 1`).

The LCD bug alone took about 60 build cycles; a ¥45 logic analyzer finally narrowed it down.

VelaPaw · CircuitForge · engineering

[0:45 · ends 7:15] Most of our time went below the application. One story in full: hardware SPI drew nothing on the screen. After about 60 build cycles, a 45-yuan logic analyzer showed the bytes on the wire were perfect, so the fault was inside the panel. Its chip-select is tied low, so one stray clock edge at the pin handover desynchronised it for good. Resetting the panel after the handover fixed it, and it now runs at 40 MHz with DMA. The rest in one line each: a C++ static-init deadlock behind a blue screen; a mic DMA that stalls at one buffer alignment; an agent stack in PSRAM, which goes dark during flash reads; and USB FIFOs that overlapped. Each one was fixed and verified on the board.

[0:45 · ends 7:15] Most of our time went below the application. One story in full: hardware SPI drew nothing on the screen. After about 60 build cycles, a 45-yuan logic analyzer showed the bytes on the wire were perfect, so the fault was inside the panel. Its chip-select is tied low, so one stray clock edge at the pin handover desynchronised it for good. Resetting the panel after the handover fixed it, and it now runs at 40 MHz with DMA. The rest in one line each: a C++ static-init deadlock behind a blue screen; a mic DMA that stalls at one buffer alignment; an agent stack in PSRAM, which goes dark during flash reads; and USB FIFOs that overlapped. 1 # Layout — how slides, flow and pinning compose 2 3 SKILL.md shows the common slide. Read this page when a layout needs more than a column of blocks and a card row. This page explains: 4 5 - The flow-vs-pin model 6 - The flex and grid idioms 7 - How to put labels over an image 8 - The few things the editor does with structure that affect how you should write the HTML 9 10 The page format.md lists the exact CSS properties you can use. 11 12 ## Two ways to place anything 13 14 A `
` is a 1920×1080 canvas. Its style controls both its background (the "paint") and its layout. 15 16 - `padding` is the slide margin. 128px is the standard margin. 17 - `display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap` stacks the child elements from top to bottom with space between them. 18 - `justify-content:center` centers the child elements vertically. 19 - `justify-content:flex-end` sinks the child elements to the bottom. 20 21 A section with no `display` style is a plain column with no gap. 22 23 There are two ways to place child elements inside a `
`: 24 25 - **Flow**: Flow children sit one after another in the section's layout. They are sized to fit their content unless you give them a `width`, `height`, or `flex` style. Open space appears wherever the flow leaves it. Open space LOW on a slide is correct. Do not reach for `justify-content:center` on every slide. 26 27 - **Pinned**: Pinned children have `position:absolute`. They leave the flow and sit where their `left`, `right`, `top`, and `bottom` styles say, relative to the section. Give them a `width` (text needs one to wrap), or pin both sides. Use pinned children only for the things flow cannot do: 28 - A source line at the bottom edge 29 - A badge over a corner 30 - A full-bleed photo behind everything, with `position:absolute; left:0; top:0; width:1920px; height:1080px; object-fit:cover`, listed first in the HTML so the other elements paint over it 31 - A magic-move element 32 33 Put everything else in the flow. 34 35 The order of elements in the HTML source is the order they paint. There is no `z-index`. List pinned backdrops first in the HTML. Inside a `position:relative` host, pinned children always paint over its flow content. The page format.md explains this in the "Slide" section. 36 37 ## Flex idioms 38 39 - **Card row**: Use `
` with `flex:1` on the children. This makes equal columns. The default `align-items:stretch` makes every card as tall as the tallest card. A card is a `
` with `display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:12px` plus its paint (background, border, radius, and padding). 40 - **Two columns, unequal**: Use `flex:2` and `flex:1`, or set `width:800px` on one and `flex:1` on the other. 41 - **Push apart**: Put an empty `
` between siblings, or use `justify-content:space-between` on the parent. 42 - **Bottom-anchored block**: Set `display:flex; flex-direction:column` on the section. There is no `margin` property. To make space above the block, put an empty `flex:1` spacer above it. 43 - **Centered block**, for a one-off slide (a statement, a quote, a closing line): `justify-content:center` on the section's column puts the block in the middle of the height; without it a short column hangs from the top, which is what a slide with a heading wants (next idiom). 44 - **A run of slides with one layout** (the content slides of a deck; one slide per region, per step, per option): the heading sits at the top margin on every one, at the same height, so it stays put when the viewer flips from slide to slide. This fills children into cells in row-major order. Use `grid-column:span 2` to widen one cell. 56 57 That is the whole grid vocabulary. You can see the supported CSS in format.md in the "Supported CSS" section: tracks of `px`, `fr`, `auto`, or `repeat(N, …)`, and one `gap`. No `minmax()`, `auto-fill`, named areas, or line numbers. 58 59 Use grid for KPI tiles, photo grids, feature matrices, and anything a flex row cannot keep square. Add `aspect-ratio:1` (or `4/3`) to the tiles. Row heights follow the content unless you set `grid-template-rows`. A table is usually better than a grid of text cells when the content is tabular. 60 61 **A matrix is ONE grid, not many columns.** Three columns — each holding a chip, a blurb, and a card — look like three column stacks. But they are one grid: `display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr)`. The nine children go in row-major order: chip, chip, chip, blurb, blurb, blurb, and so on. Grid rows line up across the columns. Separate stacks drift apart as their content heights differ. Parallel content — like a bilingual table or a before/after pair — shares rows the same way: use one table with both languages as column groups (or one flex row per row). Add a `gap` or a divider between side-by-side tables so their rules don't read as one. 62 63 ## Footer band 64 65 A footer — a page number, a source line, a logo — is ONE pinned 24px row (text, or a logo no taller) at `bottom:64px`, in the same spot on every slide that has one. 2	name: velapaw-scheduled-feeding
3	description: "VelaPaw Model-B scheduled feeding + the PCF85063 RTC-over-I2C solution, and the CONFIG_RTC trap that kills the USB console on this board"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: 3659500b-38f3-47db-bbd0-9b2aab159cd9
8	  modified: 2026-09-03T01:05:59.037Z
9	---
10	
11	Scheduled feeding for VelaPaw (2026-07-13). See [[velapaw-recognize-tuning]] for the
12	recognize path this builds on.
13	
14	**Model B (recognition-gated schedule) — the feature.** Recognition decides WHO is at
15	the bowl; the pet's meal time decides WHEN it may eat. A recognized pet is fed only if
16	its meal is DUE (`wall_min() >= pet->meal_min`) and it hasn't eaten today
17	(`g_meal_fed_day[id] != wall_day()`); then that day is stamped so it can't double-feed.
18	- `struct velapaw_pet` gained `int meal_min` (minute-of-day, -1 = none);
19	  `velapaw_identity_enroll()` takes it (both call sites: ui do_save + velapaw_main).
20	- Enroll tab has **Meal time** (+/-1h, +/-5m) and **Clock now** (+/-1h, +/-5m) setters;
21	  header shows the live clock. "Next day" (Trends) resets `g_meal_fed_day` so it re-feeds.
22	- Status strings: "next meal at HH:MM" / "Fed Ng at HH:MM" / "already ate today".
23	
24	**!!! TRAP: enabling NuttX `CONFIG_RTC` KILLS THE USB CONSOLE on this board !!!**
25	`CONFIG_RTC`+`RTC_DRIVER` on ESP32-S3 requires `CONFIG_ESP32S3_RT_TIMER` (esp32s3_rtc.c
26	needs `esp32s3_rt_timer_time_us`). That combo (high-prio RT-timer task + DRAM pressure --
27	the build overflowed dram0_0_seg by 6KB and only fit after dropping `LIBC_LOCALTIME`)
28	makes the CDC/ACM console (VID 0525 = COM4) fail to enumerate at runtime. Board still
29	boots (LCD goes gray) but is unreachable. Tried 3 ways, all dead. **Do not enable
30	CONFIG_RTC.** (Also: swapping to native `ESP32S3_USBSERIAL` console didn't help because
31	`CONFIG_BOARDCTL_USBDEVCTRL=y` selects `USBDEV`, so CDCACM stayed on and both USB stacks
32	fought over GPIO19/20.)
33	
34	**THE SOLUTION: drive the on-board PCF85063 RTC chip DIRECTLY over I2C.** The board has a
35	real battery-backed RTC on the same I2C bus as the touch/AXP/camera. Bypassing NuttX's RTC
36	framework entirely = persistent time with ZERO config changes and no USB risk.
37	- In the board file (`esp32s3_st7789.c`, which already holds the I2C handle): `PCF_ADDR
38	  0x51`, time regs `0x04..0x0A` = sec(bit7=OS flag) min hour day weekday month year, BCD.
39	  `pcf_rd`/`pcf_wr` via `I2C_TRANSFER`; `days_from_civil`/`civil_from_days` (Hinnant) so no
40	  localtime/mktime needed. `board_rtc_gettime()` -> `clock_settime(CLOCK_REALTIME)` at boot;
41	  exported `board_rtc_settime(time_t)` for the app.
42	- velapaw `wall_set_min()` calls `board_rtc_settime()` so Set-Clock persists.
43	- **GOTCHA: the PCF85063 only stores years 2000-2099** (year reg is an offset from 2000).
44	  Seeding a 1970/day-0 epoch makes `year-2000 = -30` -> garbage BCD -> bogus readback.
45	  Seed a real 2026 epoch.
46	
47	**!!! The boot seed must be a FLOOR, not a plausibility test — fixed 2026-09-03 !!!**
48	The original seed re-dated the clock only when `tv_sec < 1500000000` (pre-2017). That
49	fires exactly once, on a virgin chip; afterwards the RTC reads back plausible forever and
50	the board is **permanently pinned to whatever constant that seed named**. Symptom: 7 weeks
51	later every feed-log line still said `2026-07-13`, and *nothing on the board could correct
52	it*:
53	- `wall_set_min()` (ui_lvgl.c) computes `ts.tv_sec = (ts.tv_sec/86400)*86400 + min*60` —
54	  it **preserves the day** and only rewrites HH:MM. The Enroll clock control structurally
55	  cannot change the date (it CAN fix time-of-day, which is what it's for).
56	- nsh has **no `date` command** (verified: `command not found`, absent from `help`), and no
57	  `i2c` tool. `CONFIG_RTC` is off (see the trap above), so nothing on the console reaches
58	  the chip. A rebuild is the ONLY way to change the date.
59	**Fix pattern:** compare against the *build date* so the seed is self-correcting —
60	`#define VELAPAW_CLOCK_ANCHOR <epoch of build day 00:00>`, `if (tv_sec < ANCHOR)` seed
61	`ANCHOR + 8*3600`. Board behind the anchor is pushed up once; board already ahead is left
62	alone; each rebuild advances the floor. **Bump the constant when the board comes back
63	reading an old date.**
64	- Verifying the rebuild took is NOT possible with `strings` (it's a numeric literal) and
65	  NOT possible by size (the swap is byte-neutral — nuttx.bin was identical at 1,567,312 B).
66	  Search nuttx.bin for the packed LE u32 instead: new seed value present, all old
67	  constants absent. Note the compiler folds `ANCHOR + 8*3600` into one literal and may
68	  optimise the bare-ANCHOR comparison away, so test on the *folded* value.
69	- Safe to reflash: day-rolling is driven only by the manual **Next Day** button
70	  (`EV_NEXTDAY` -> `velapaw_store_roll_day()`), and the 30-day window is a shift register
71	  with no calendar dates in it — so a clock jump does NOT disturb history.bin. Confirmed
72	  on hardware: 52-day jump, digest and enrollment untouched.
73	- VERIFIED: set 10:56 -> reset -> boot log `RTC ok: synced epoch=1783940198` = 2026-07-13
74	  10:56:38. Time survives resets. "Clock now" is a ONE-TIME setup, not per-session.
75	
76	**!!! CRITICAL: a blocking printf() FREEZES the whole app when no PC is attached !!!**
77	The console is USB CDC with `CONFIG_CDCACM_TXBUFSIZE=193` (tiny). With nothing draining
78	the port -- i.e. the ACTUAL DEMO CONDITION, no laptop plugged in -- that TX buffer fills
79	and `printf()` BLOCKS, hanging the UI + camera. Symptom that led here: "the 2nd recognize
80	identifies then the UI and camera go dead" -- because the 2nd recognition is the one where
81	the meal is DUE, so it FEEDS, and the feed path is the only path that printfs
82	(`feeder_mock` "dispensing", `store_stub` "event"). First recognition = no feed = no
83	printf = no freeze. FIX (in `velapaw_ui_run()` before `lv_init()`): make stdout+stderr
84	non-blocking so printf DROPS output instead of stalling --
85	`fcntl(STDOUT_FILENO, F_SETFL, fcntl(STDOUT_FILENO,F_GETFL,0) | O_NONBLOCK)` (same for
86	STDERR). Logging still works whenever a host IS reading. Verified: feeds cleanly and stays
87	responsive with the serial port released. **Always test the demo with the console
88	DISCONNECTED** -- a drained console hides this class of bug entirely.
89	
90	**Meal history (per-pet timeline, in My Pets):** no store/ring-buffer needed -- just record
91	`g_meal_fed_min[pet][slot]` and `g_meal_fed_g[pet][slot]` next to the existing
92	`g_meal_fed_day[pet][slot]` (~192 B total). My Pets then renders schedule-vs-reality per
93	pet: "08:00 ate 08:02 15g" (eaten) / "12:30 waiting for pet" (due, food reserved, pet
94	hasn't shown) / "18:00 pending". Feed events now carry a real wall-clock ts from the RTC.
95	
96	**USB/host gotchas hit along the way:** ports showing `CM_PROB_PHANTOM` = device not
97	present at all. VMware's `VMUSBArbService` can hijack the board's USB (VM Settings -> USB ->
98	uncheck "automatically connect new USB devices"). After a firmware change that changes USB,
99	a full unplug/replug is needed to clear Windows' poisoned enumeration. COM3 (ROM, download
100	mode) working while COM4 (firmware console) doesn't = firmware console problem, not cable.

11	**Improvement item 8, SHIPPED 2026-10-13.** The user's goal: judges should see
12	the agent on the LCD instead of in a terminal — "watch the feeder change",
13	not "read the terminal".
14	
15	**Why:** this is the demo's centrepiece for the defense.
16	**How to apply:** demo with fresh sentences (see the cache note), judge success
17	by the `set_meal_schedule` trace line or `status.md`, never by the reply text,

20	## What is on the screen (item-8 patch, 6 files)
21	
22	Rollback copy: `~/velapaw-golden/pre-item8-agent-lcd/`.
23	
24	- **Toast under the bell for every `ask`:** "You: <question>" → "Agent
25	  working… N s" counting up → the reply. It stays 30 s; a tap dismisses it.
26	- **Heartbeat:** an all-clear is a green toast for 10 s. A warning is a red
27	  toast that stays, turns the bell red and is listed in the bell panel until
28	  the next all-clear. A *failed* heartbeat shows nothing, so a dead network at
29	  the offline defense doesn't clutter the screen.
30	- **Live My Pets:** an identity generation counter makes the card redraw on
31	  whatever tab is showing. An open Edit dialog picks up the change too, so
32	  pressing Save can't write the old time back. Before this, My Pets only
33	  redrew when you entered the tab.

35	  ([[velapaw-i18n]]).

37	## fix9 — why "the toast works but the times don't change"
38	
39	6 files: `store.h`, `store_stub.c`, `identity.c`, `ui_lvgl.c`,
40	`tool_registry.c`, `nsh_commands.c`. Rollback:
41	`~/velapaw-golden/pre-fix9-status-refresh/`. Image
42	`148bf5d5eff85947a89e00eaafd538c3`.
43	
44	- `status.md` is the agent's only source of meal times, and it was rewritten
45	  only at boot and after a feed — one turn after moving breakfast, the agent
46	  read the old time back. It is now also rewritten after an agent change, an
47	  Edit or voice-dialog save, and a pet delete.
48	- The model answered "Done" without calling `set_meal_schedule`. The tool
49	  description now says a meal changes only when the tool succeeds.
50	- `ask` text carried raw backspace/arrow-key bytes from the terminal; they are
51	  now applied or dropped before the message is sent.
52	- **Still open, not in fix9. SEEN ON HARDWARE 2026-10-13:** sending
53	  `ask change bob's dinner to 18:20` twice in a row gave `Cache hit, skipping
54	  LLM call` and `END status=ok iters=1 tools=0 … elapsed=0s`. It replayed
55	  "Done — … 18:20" without calling `set_meal_schedule`. That time it was
56	  harmless, since the meal already was 18:20. After an Edit-dialog change it
57	  would be a false "Done".
58	- **How the cache works** (`src/llm/llm_cache.c` and `include/llm/llm_cache.h`;
59	  values read from the D: checkout, which is upstream code we never modified):
60	  - It is RAM-only, with 8 slots.
61	  - Entries expire after 300 s, but **every hit re-stores the entry and
62	    restarts the 300 s**.
63	  - The key is a djb2 hash of the prompt's first 64 characters, with no string
64	    compare. Long asks that differ only after character 64 therefore collide.
65	  - The store is at `agent_loop.c` `send_reply:` (~line 1451). It is gated
66	    only on `LLM_COMPLEXITY_SIMPLE` and the non-heartbeat `cacheable` flag.
67	- **Fix** = add `&& trace.total_tool_calls == 0` to that store condition. That
68	  counter is what the END line prints as `tools=`. Not applied yet. Until then,
69	  use a fresh sentence, wait 5 minutes, or restart `ai_agent`.
