14	`conv.cc`** active in `apps/mlearning/tflite-micro/.../micro/kernels/esp_nn/` — so
15	DepthwiseConv/FullyConnected/Pooling/Add/Mul/Softmax ran the SLOW reference kernels
16	(MobileNetV3 is mostly depthwise!). Fix: `cp apps/mlearning/esp_nn_kernels/{depthwise_conv,fully_connected,pooling,add,mul,softmax}.cc`
17	into that active esp_nn dir + `rm` its stale `.o` + delete `libtflite-micro*.a`, rebuild.
18	The Makefile auto-globs `esp_nn/*.cc` and filters out the matching reference kernels.
19	(Note: esp-nn's S3-SIMD sources `*esp32s3.c` are `filter-out`'d in the Makefile — a
20	further ~2-4x is likely left on the table if those + `-DCONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32S3`
21	can be made to build under NuttX.)
22	
23	**Background-thread recognize (no UI freeze).** The 1.3s Invoke ran on the LVGL/UI
24	loop -> froze touch+preview. Fixed in `ui/ui_lvgl.c`: a `recog_worker` pthread
25	(32KB stack) runs embed()+match(); UI hands off a frame via `g_inf_state` (0 idle,
26	1 request, 2 busy, 3 done) and pauses preview capture while busy so the shared frame
27	buffer isn't overwritten. All LVGL updates + BCS + feed stay on the UI thread in the
28	state==3 consume block. Confirmed: touch/preview live during inference.
29	
30	**Match tuning:** `VELAPAW_MATCH_THRESHOLD=0.45` (velapaw.h), `RECOG_STABLE_N=1`,
31	retry cap `recog_tries>=2`. On-device scores: bob 0.53-0.84 (dips to ~0.20 on bad
32	frames), unknowns <=0.22 -> 0.45 cleanly separates (0.15 default caused false feeds).
33	Embedding is noisy but discriminative enough. STABLE_N=1 acts on the first good frame.
34	
35	**ENROLLMENT QUALITY is the dominant lever for FALSE-ACCEPTS (2026-07-17).** User pointed the camera at a CHAIR and Recognize confidently returned "bob 0.71" — a false accept well above the 0.45 gate. Root cause is fundamental to open-set recognition with a generic pet feature-extractor: the model was never trained to reject non-pets, so OOD inputs (chair/wall/hand) still produce an embedding that can land near an enrolled pet. With ONE enrolled pet the margin (best-second) can't help either. **No threshold cleanly fixes it** — a 0.71 chair sits inside bob's legitimate 0.53-0.84 range, so raising the gate to reject the chair also rejects real bob frames. **THE FIX THAT WORKED: re-enroll the pet properly** — 5 shots with the pet's FACE FILLING THE FRAME, close, well-lit, minimal background. A hasty/background-heavy enrollment puts the centroid in a "generic" region where lots of things score high; tight face-on shots pull it to a distinctive spot and the chair correctly reads Unknown. Confirmed on hardware. **Demo implication:** enrollment quality, not the threshold, is what makes recognition trustworthy — enroll carefully before the defense. (Deeper fixes for arbitrary-object rejection = a pet/no-pet gate model or an individually-trained model; both need GPU/data, not done.)
36	
37	**GOTCHA - header edits don't recompile:** editing `velapaw.h` (the threshold) did
38	NOT rebuild `identity.o` — the incremental build missed the header dep, so the old
39	0.15 stayed compiled in and false-matching persisted. Fix: `find apps/examples/velapaw
40	-name '*.c' -exec touch {} +` to force recompilation after any HEADER change.
41	
42	The "recognize hangs" the user reported was NOT an infinite loop (the `recog_tries`
43	cap was present) — it was the on-UI-thread freeze + the false-matching. Both fixed above.
44	A later "hangs on 2nd recognize" was a FALSE ALARM: after identifying, `recog_done=1`
45	rests until you leave+re-enter the tab (on-demand model) — traces showed the loop alive.
46	
47	**Two-feed accounting fix:** `g_fed_visit` (feed-once-per-visit gate) only reset in the
48	"pet left" path, which `recog_done` stops -> a pet could never be fed a 2nd time.
49	Fix: reset `g_fed_visit = VELAPAW_PET_UNKNOWN` in the tab-leave re-arm block; the per-pet
50	cooldown (`g_last_fed` + `cooldown_s`, `UI_DEMO_COOLDOWN_S=10`) still gates rapid feeds.
51	
52	**Camera orientation:** sensor mounted rotated; baked a 90-deg **counter-clockwise**
53	rotation into `frame_to_565` (square 128x128 frame): `dst(dr,dc)=src(dc, W-1-dr)`.
54	Fixes both live preview and enroll thumbnails in one place. (90 CW gave upside-down.)
55	Also removed the mock "View" scene-cycle button/label from Enroll and moved Capture up
56	under the camera/filmstrip so samples stay visible while shooting.

43	## Design decisions worth keeping
44	- **At-most-once feeding:** `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/fed.bin` (magic `VPF1`, via `velapaw_store_put/get`) is saved BEFORE the dispense; `FEED_GAP_MIN` 20; a slot closed by the daily limit shows "skipped"; skips restore only on the same day.
45	- **Stall monitor:** a prio+10 thread (2 KB stack) watches the UI heartbeat (2 min; 10 min while the tag is `feed`) and the recognition worker (1 min). A prio+5 note thread (6 KB) writes `STALL <kind> at <tag> <age>s | <health line>` to flash, then `up_systemreset()` (reset code 0x03); it waits at most 3 s for the note. Started right before the main loop. **Not a HW watchdog** — an interrupts-off hang isn't caught.
46	- **health.log** = `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/health.log`, rotates at 4 KB into `health.old`. Boot line `HH:MM boot rst 0xNN`; every 10 min `HH:MM up Nm tab T cap N max Nms slow N same N err N embed N hit N miss N inf S drop N`. `velapaw voice` (read-only probe) prints the live line + the boot code.
47	- **There is NO software-reset command in this build:** `reboot` → `nsh: reboot: command not found` (2026-10-18), probably because `CONFIG_BOARDCTL_RESET` is off. **Don't suggest ai_agent's `restart`**: without BOARDCTL_RESET it prints "Restarting..." and sleeps forever, which parks the agent CLI. The RESET button gives 0x01, so the 0x03 → start-on-Recognize path can only be exercised by a real stall.
48	- Reset codes (`esp32s3_reset_reasons(0)`): 0x01 power-on/brown-out/RESET button, **0x03 CORE_SW = the stall monitor's `up_systemreset()`**, 0x07/0x08 MWDT, 0x09 RTC WDT, 0x0f brown-out, 0x15/0x16 USB UART/JTAG (esptool). Any other code than 0x01/0x15/0x16, with pets enrolled, boots on Recognize.
49	- Never patch `ui_i18n.c` — stab1 reuses `S_POINT_AT_PET`, `S_NEXT_MEAL_FMT`, `S_SKIPPED`.
50	
51	## Gotchas
52	- All velapaw sources are **LF** — an in-session note that said CRLF was wrong.
53	- No LVGL heap metric (`CONFIG_LV_USE_CLIB_MALLOC=y`) and a heap walk kills the board ([[velapaw-heap-walk-kills-board]]).
54	- Thread stacks come from IMEM (~64 KB headroom before stab1's 8 KB).
55	- Pre-existing VM warnings outside the patched files — ignore: `ui_i18n.c:245` `f14` set but not used; `agent_loop.c:740` `-Wformat-truncation`.
56	- Local compile check: `cc_check.sh <a|b> <file>` = arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.4 after `source /d/openVela/vela-env.sh`, flags from `compile_commands.json`, item8/b headers (`identity.h` 564256ad, `ui_i18n.h` 778b1a32). The VM is xtensa GCC 12.2, so the VM warning gate is the real check.
57	- Still-ungated prints (feeder, TFLM, BCS lazy init, identity, boot init, camera + LVGL syslog): a jam there now ends in a stall reset + a log line instead of a silent hang.
58	- A stall reset re-enumerates USB: reopen COM8, redo `ifconfig eth0 …`, ping to prime ARP ([[velapaw-cdcncm-networking]]).
59	
60	Offered, not done: HW watchdog (`CONFIG_WATCHDOG` + automonitor), `CONFIG_BOARD_RESET_ON_ASSERT`, syslog hardening, auto-ifconfig after a reset, idle return to Recognize, a camera HAL that returns -1 / re-inits. Related: [[velapaw-agent-on-lcd]] (the open `llm_cache` fix), [[velapaw-scheduled-feeding]], [[velapaw-recognize-tuning]].

4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project

10	
11	**SOLVED + SHIPPED 2026-08-09.** VelaPaw's Enroll-tab camera preview had two bugs that looked related but weren't: an orientation bug (image rotated) and a color bug (purple tint). Both are now fixed and confirmed correct on real hardware (hand test: fingers-up renders fingers-up; color no longer purple).
12	
13	## Orientation: it was a 90 deg transpose, not a flip
14	
15	**Diagnostic trick that broke the case open:** hold a real hand up in front of the camera (fingers pointing up) and look at the preview. A **vertical→horizontal** result (fingers appearing sideways) can *only* come from a 90 deg rotation/transpose. Flip and mirror (the OV5640's `0x3820`/`0x3821` registers) can each only reverse one axis — neither, nor any combination, can ever turn vertical into horizontal. Chasing this with sensor flip/mirror registers is structurally unable to work; a color-bar test earlier in the debugging session had hinted at this (horizontal bars where vertical were expected) but got wrongly dismissed as a binning artifact.
16	
17	**Fix:** correct the rotation in software, in the HAL's downscale/resample step — `app/velapaw/hal/camera_ov5640.c`, in `velapaw_camera_get_frame()`. The old code was a plain resize + horizontal mirror. Determined the needed correction was **90 deg CW** by tracing where each output-image corner samples from in the raw 320x240 buffer (not by guessing — get this backwards and it's another flash cycle to find out). Final resample also folds in the existing selfie-mirror on the corrected (post-rotation) axis:
18	
19	```c
20	int dy = y * w / VELAPAW_FRAME_H;   /* w = CAM_W = 320 */
21	int sx = dy;
22	...
23	int mox = (VELAPAW_FRAME_W - 1) - x;
24	int dx = mox * h / VELAPAW_FRAME_W; /* h = CAM_H = 240 */
25	int sy = (h - 1) - dx;
26	const uint8_t *p = buf + ((size_t)sy * w + sx) * 2;
27	```
28	
29	**Important dependency:** this transpose is derived against whatever the sensor's raw output orientation is *at the time of the hand test*. If sensor-side flip/mirror registers (`0x3820`/`0x3821`) ever change again, the raw buffer's orientation changes too, and the hand test (and possibly the CW/CCW direction) needs to be redone. See [[velapaw-camera-connector]] for the physical mount/pinout side of the camera.
30	
31	## Color: the purple tint was from splitting OV5640's flip bits
32	
33	Earlier debugging assumed `0x3820`/`0x3821` bit1 = "sensor-side flip" (shifts Bayer CFA phase, causes purple) and bit2 = "ISP-side flip" (safe, post-debayer). Testing bit2-only (`0x05`/`0x05`) still produced the purple tint — that hypothesis was wrong. In the OV5640 (per standard reference driver code, e.g. esp32-camera's `ov5640.c`), **bits 1 and 2 are meant to be toggled together as one flip unit (mask `0x06`)**, not used as independent safe/unsafe halves — setting bit2 alone leaves the sensor in an undefined partial-flip state.
34	
35	**Fix:** since software now owns 100% of the orientation correction (see above), there's no need for the sensor to flip/mirror at all. Cleared bits 1+2 entirely, preserving whatever bit0 was for (unknown purpose, untouched, was already `1` in the working baseline): `ov5640_wr(i,0x3820,0x01);ov5640_wr(i,0x3821,0x01);` (board file, `ov5640_config_qvga()`). Do not reintroduce `0x3820`/`0x3821` bit1 or bit2 without re-testing color — that combination is the confirmed cause.
36	
37	## Purple round 2 — the REAL other half was `0x4514` (SOLVED 2026-09-05)
38

The standard pairing (Linux `ov5640` driver, esp32-camera):

41	- mirror **on** (`0x3821` bits 1+2 set) → `0x4514 = 0xbb`
42	- mirror **off** (`0x3821` bits cleared) → `0x4514 = 0x88`

46	**The symptom tells you which of the two it is, and it's decisive:** a flip/Bayer-phase error *exchanges* red and blue and leaves green alone (green is 2 of 4 Bayer cells either way) — it physically cannot cause green loss. The delay has two causes working together. Poor pictures make the looks fail, and after two failed looks the firmware slows itself down on purpose.

**What the firmware on the board does**
- When something appears, it looks once at once, then again about 2.5 s later. Each look takes about 1.3 s.
- If neither look reaches a score of 0.45, it shows **"Point at a pet"** and stops looking.
- It only looks again when:
  - you tap the screen;
  - the picture changes;
  - or once a minute for the first 30 minutes after a meal comes due.
- After each failed round, a change only counts after a longer wait: 3 s, then 6, 12 and 20 s. Only a match or leaving the tab resets this.
- **A pet or photo held still doesn't count as a change.** It can sit on "Point at a pet" until you move it.
- After a match, it ignores movement for 30 s. A second pet shown right after the first has to wait.

**Why the looks fail (from your photos)**
- **The room is dim.** The camera turns its gain up, and the magenta and green speckle is noise. The firmware shrinks the picture by picking single pixels rather than averaging them, so all that noise reaches the model.
- **Red, yellow and orange wires hang in front of the lens.** Anything in view that wasn't there when the pet was enrolled lowers the score.
- **The flat purple patches look like over-bright spots (glare).** The camera clips those to purple. If you're holding up a printed photo, tilt it until the reflection goes.
- **The junk top row is cosmetic.** It's the camera's last line of each frame arriving corrupted, one row in 128, so it isn't why it's slow.

**Try now, no reflash**
1. Light the bowl area from the side or above. Bring a small USB lamp to Beijing too, since you can't rely on the stage lighting.
2. Tape the wires out of the camera's view and wipe the lens.
3. When it says "Point at a pet", tap the camera picture. It takes two fresh looks at once. Do the same before showing a second pet.
4. If scores stay low in good light, re-enroll the pet in your demo light and position: 5 close shots with the face filling the frame. Re-enrolling means deleting the pet, which also deletes its Trends feeding history. If you want that history in the demo, re-enroll only once, close to the finals.

**Send me two numbers**, with the pet in view and the light fixed:
- **The score:** shown in "Unknown (0.xx)" for about 2 s before "Point at a pet", or next to the name if it matches.
- **The time per look:** the "infer ___ ms" line under the picture.

What they mean:
- A score of 0.30–0.44 means picture quality.
- A score below 0.25 means the enrollment doesn't match.
- An infer time well over 1300 ms means something is slowing the processor.

If you're on COM8 anyway, this also shows the match and miss counts:
```
cat /data/ai_agent/velapaw/health.log
```

**Firmware fix I can prepare.** It would be a script you paste into the VM, like stab1b, with the current image as the rollback:
- 3 looks per round instead of 2;
- 0.6 s between looks instead of 1.2 s;
- the longest wait after failed rounds cut from 20 s to 6 s.

No re-enrollment is needed, and the 0.45 threshold stays. I'd keep the tries modest, because every extra look at something that isn't a pet is another chance to feed by mistake.

The fix could also average neighbouring camera pixels, which roughly halves the noise, and drop the junk line. That changes what the model sees, so every pet would need re-enrolling, and their Trends history would be lost.

**Board firmware and hardware**

**Recognition loop (ui_lvgl.c stab1b)**
- A round is 2 looks:
  - look 1 starts immediately (`last_recog = 0`);
  - look 2 comes after `RECOG_INTERVAL_MS` 1200 plus ~1.3 s of embed;
  - then it rests with "Point at a pet".
- Re-arm triggers:
  - a tap (`g_last_touch > done_at && !ui_touch_active()`), immediately;
  - `scene_changed && since >= rearm_gap`;
  - `since >= MEAL_POLL_MS (60000) && meal_window_open()` (one look, `tries = 1`).
- Gaps:
  - the miss gap goes 3000 → 6000 → 12000 → 20000 (`REARM_MISS_MS`, `REARM_MISS_MAX_MS`); only a hit or leaving the tab resets it;
  - after a hit, `REARM_HIT_MS` is 30000.
- The motion detector:
  - `scene_sig` takes a 4×4 brightness grid;
  - `scene_moved` needs `SIG_CELL_DIFF` 20 on at least `SIG_MIN_CELLS` 2 cells, or a global shift above `SIG_SHIFT_MAX` 48.
- `RECOG_STABLE_N` is 1; `VELAPAW_MATCH_THRESHOLD` is 0.45.
- No console print is made per look.
- The look-1 score "Unknown (0.xx)" shows for ~2.5 s. Look 2's score is overwritten by "Point at a pet" in the same pass.
- `recog_worker` holds `g_tflm_lock`, which it shares with the voice KWS.

**Camera chain**
- The HAL (`camera_ov5640.c`) downsamples 320×240 RGB565 by nearest neighbour with a 90° CW remap:
  - `sx = y*w/128`;
  - `sy = (h-1) - ((127-x)*h/128)`.
- `frame_to_565` then rotates 90° CCW for display: `dst(dr,dc) = src(dc, W-1-dr)`.
- So the display's top row = frame column 127 = raw DVP row 239, the last line, which shows junk.

37	## Why it "hung" / stopped recognizing (ranked)
38	1. **`recog_done` latch** — after one match or 2 misses, Recognize waited for a tab re-entry; looks exactly like "fails to recognize". stab1 re-arms on a tap, on a scene change (4×4 brightness signature), and once a minute while a meal is due (its first 30 min); gap 30 s after a hit, 3 s doubling to 20 s after misses.
39	2. **Console jam** — `uart_write` takes `xmit.lock` BEFORE it checks O_NONBLOCK, so one blocking writer + a host that stopped draining COM8 (PuTTY closed, PC asleep) jams every writer, UI thread included. stab1: `uprintf` (UI) and `vp_say` (store) ask FIONSPACE first (answered under a spinlock) and drop the line instead (counted as `drop`). Rejected: a pipe relay (CONFIG_PIPES off) and a dup2 mute.
40	3. Midnight: `today_total` wasn't reconciled for a board running past midnight → a day that ended at the cap refused the next day's meals. Fix: `velapaw_store_sync_day()` on the UI's day change.
41	4. Skips survived midnight. 5. BCS ran outside `g_tflm_lock` (raced KWS). 6. The preview ran at 150 ms forever after a match. 7. The worker could stick in state 2. 8. The camera HAL hides failures: `velapaw_camera_get_frame` always returns 0 and keeps the old frame, so watch `same`, not `err`. 9. After a reset the UI booted on Enroll (pauses after 30 s). 10. Fed/skip flags were RAM-only → a reset could re-serve an eaten meal. 11. `g_last_fed` was never read → no gap between two due meals. 12. The limit-hit path left stale `fed_min`/`fed_g`.
42	
43	## Design decisions worth keeping
44	- **At-most-once feeding:** `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/fed.bin` (magic `VPF1`, via `velapaw_store_put/get`) is saved BEFORE the dispense; `FEED_GAP_MIN` 20; a slot closed by the daily limit shows "skipped"; skips restore only on the same day.
45	- **Stall monitor:** a prio+10 thread (2 KB stack) watches the UI heartbeat (2 min; 10 min while the tag is `feed`) and the recognition worker (1 min). A prio+5 note thread (6 KB) writes `STALL <kind> at <tag> <age>s | <health line>` to flash, then `up_systemreset()` (reset code 0x03); it waits at most 3 s for the note. Started right before the main loop. **Not a HW watchdog** — an interrupts-off hang isn't caught.
46	- **health.log** = `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/health.log`, rotates at 4 KB into `health.old`. Boot line `HH:MM boot rst 0xNN`; every 10 min `HH:MM up Nm tab T cap N max Nms slow N same N err N embed N hit N miss N inf S drop N`. `velapaw voice` (read-only probe) prints the live line + the boot code.
47	- **There is NO software-reset command in this build:** `reboot` → `nsh: reboot: command not found` (2026-10-18), probably because `CONFIG_BOARDCTL_RESET` is off. **Don't suggest ai_agent's `restart`**: without BOARDCTL_RESET it prints "Restarting..." and sleeps forever, which parks the agent CLI. The RESET button gives 0x01, so the 0x03 → start-on-Recognize path can only be exercised by a real stall.
48	- Reset codes (`esp32s3_reset_reasons(0)`): 0x01 power-on/brown-out/RESET button, **0x03 CORE_SW = the stall monitor's `up_systemreset()`**, 0x07/0x08 MWDT, 0x09 RTC WDT, 0x0f brown-out, 0x15/0x16 USB UART/JTAG (esptool). Any other code than 0x01/0x15/0x16, with pets enrolled, boots on Recognize.
49	- Never patch `ui_i18n.c` — stab1 reuses `S_POINT_AT_PET`, `S_NEXT_MEAL_FMT`, `S_SKIPPED`.
50	
51	## Gotchas
52	- All velapaw sources are **LF** — an in-session note that said CRLF was wrong.
53	- No LVGL heap metric (`CONFIG_LV_USE_CLIB_MALLOC=y`) and a heap walk kills the board ([[velapaw-heap-walk-kills-board]]).
54	- Thread stacks come from IMEM (~64 KB headroom before stab1's 8 KB).
55	- Pre-existing VM warnings outside the patched files — ignore: `ui_i18n.c:245` `f14` set but not used; `agent_loop.c:740` `-Wformat-truncation`.
56	- Local compile check: `cc_check.sh <a|b> <file>` = arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.4 after `source /d/openVela/vela-env.sh`, flags from `compile_commands.json`, item8/b headers (`identity.h` 564256ad, `ui_i18n.h` 778b1a32). The VM is xtensa GCC 12.2, so the VM warning gate is the real check.
57	- Still-ungated prints (feeder, TFLM, BCS lazy init, identity, boot init, camera + LVGL syslog): a jam there now ends in a stall reset + a log line instead of a silent hang.
58	- A stall reset re-enumerates USB: reopen COM8, redo `ifconfig eth0 …`, ping to prime ARP ([[velapaw-cdcncm-networking]]).
59	
60	Offered, not done: HW watchdog (`CONFIG_WATCHDOG` + automonitor), `CONFIG_BOARD_RESET_ON_ASSERT`, syslog hardening, auto-ifconfig after a reset, idle return to Recognize, a camera HAL that returns -1 / re-inits. Related: [[velapaw-agent-on-lcd]] (the open `llm_cache` fix), [[velapaw-scheduled-feeding]], [[velapaw-recognize-tuning]].

11	**SOLVED + SHIPPED 2026-09-04, hardware-verified.** VelaPaw's rolling intake
12	window is `g_day_g[8][30]` / `g_day_m[8][30]` in
13	`apps/examples/velapaw/store/store_stub.c`, with slot `DAYS-1` meaning
14	"today". Nothing advanced it: `velapaw_store_roll_day()`'s only caller was
15	the `EV_NEXTDAY` demo button in `ui_lvgl.c`, so **every feeding since the
16	board was built accumulated into one slot**. On hardware that summed a
17	2026-07-13 event with four 2026-09-03 events into a single 60 g "today",
18	putting jay at his 60 g owner limit on 48 g of real food. Over-reporting
19	intake makes a feeder *withhold* meals, so this failed in the dangerous
20	direction — it is a product bug, not a reporting one.
21	
22	**The fix** (`VP01` → `VP02`): a 4th header word holds the civil day that
23	owns slot TODAY, and `vp_sync_day()` reconciles against the wall clock from
24	`velapaw_store_init()` and from the top of `velapaw_store_log_feeding()`.
25	Three guarded cases, all load-bearing: clock below `VP_TS_SANE` ⇒ do
26	nothing; day unknown (a `VP01` file, first run) ⇒ adopt today **without
27	shifting**, because guessing a shift throws real days away; clock went
28	*backwards* ⇒ do nothing, which is not hypothetical — the build-date boot
29	anchor from [[velapaw-scheduled-feeding]] makes every cold start look like a
30	jump back, and shifting on it would zero populated slots. Only a genuine
31	forward delta shifts, clamped to `DAYS`. Use a real days-from-civil
32	conversion, **not `tm_yday`**: 12-31 → 01-01 must be a delta of 1, not −364,
33	or the clamp wipes the whole window every New Year. `VP01` files are
34	accepted and upgraded in place, never reset.
35	
36	**Reading the feeding data off the board.** Three files in
37	`/data/ai_agent/velapaw/`, and they are three *views*, so disagreement
38	localises the bug: `status.md` is a derived snapshot **rewritten on every
39	event**, `feed_log.md` is **append-only**, `history.bin` is the store both
40	come from. Dump the binary over nsh with
41	`hexdump <path> skip=<n> count=<n>` — but note **nsh prints offsets relative
42	to each dump, not absolute**, so a parser keyed on absolute offsets rejects
43	everything; decode by hand or key on the dump's own origin. Geometry is
44	recoverable from the size alone: `12 + 4*(2*P*D + P) = 1964` solves to
45	P=8 pets, D=30 days (16 + … = 1968 under VP02, and that size change is
46	itself the cleanest proof the new format landed).
47	
48	**Two traps hit while verifying.** `velapaw` **auto-starts at boot**, so a
49	before/after probe that launches it is already too late — and launching a
50	*second* instance wedges the console via the mic-reopen path from
51	[[velapaw-mic-capture]] (`mic: session belonged to pid 5, reopening`), after
52	which `ser.write()` blocks for ever with no output; always set
53	`write_timeout` on the serial port. Also, on a `CONFIG_VELAPAW_UI` build
54	`velapaw_main.c` goes straight into `velapaw_ui_run()`, so the scaffold path
55	that enrolls demo pets "Rex"/"Milo" is dead code and cannot pollute the pet
56	list.
57	
58	**Still open, deliberately not fixed:** the stale 12 g already in jay's slot
59	29 cannot be re-bucketed — `history.bin` stores totals, not events, so the
60	date is unrecoverable; it rolls off naturally at the next day boundary.
61	`velapaw_store_baseline_g()` divides by `DAYS-1` **including zero days**, and
62	slots 0–28 are all synthetic enrollment seed, so every baseline and appetite
63	% on the device is measured-today against demo data — the write-up must not
64	claim the baseline is learned. Pet names are stored with leading whitespace
65	(`"  bob"` appears in both derived files), so `"bob"` and `"  bob"` would be
66	distinct keys on re-enrollment; trim on enroll.

68	## 2026-10-11: the VP02 fix is correct but INERT — the anchor freezes the clock
69	
70	The day-roll fix above has never once fired on hardware, and the reason is
71	`ui_lvgl.c:3620`:
72	
73	```c
74	#define VELAPAW_CLOCK_ANCHOR 1788393600L           /* 2026-09-03 00:00 */
75	if (_ts.tv_sec < VELAPAW_CLOCK_ANCHOR)
76	    _ts.tv_sec  = VELAPAW_CLOCK_ANCHOR + 8 * 3600; /* 08:00 that day */
77	```
78	
79	Every cold boot sets the wall clock to **2026-09-03 08:00**. So `vp_sync_day()`
80	computes `today == g_hist_day` for ever, takes its (correct) never-shift-
81	backwards branch, and the 30-day window can never roll. Five weeks of real
82	time had passed with the board still reporting "today" as 09-03. **Bump the
83	anchor whenever the reported date looks stale** — 2026-10-11 00:00 is
84	`1791676800L`. The guard is right; the clock feeding it is wrong.
85	
86	Same root cause, bigger consequence: at 08:00 every morning meal reads as
87	**due on every power-up**, so the board dispenses unprompted at boot
88	(`[feeder] dispensed 3 pocket(s) ~15g (1023 steps, asked 13g)`), then logs it
89	against a timestamp that collides with previous boots'.
90	
91	**The fingerprint to look for:** `feed_log.md` is append-only, so file order
92	*is* write order — yet timestamps run 08:01 → 19:02 → 09:08 → 08:02. Time
93	going *backwards* in an append-only log can only mean the clock reset between
94	writes, which is the anchor. Reading that pattern is how the mechanism was
95	found before the `#define` was ever opened.
96	
97	**Do not use `feed_log.md` for totals.** `vp_feedlog_append()` treats
98	`st.st_size > VP_LOG_MAX` by reopening with `"w"` — it **truncates and
99	restarts**, it does not rotate. The visible file is the latest fragment only,
100	which is why a pet's "last 7 days" legitimately exceeds everything in it.
101	`status.md` is also *live* (regenerated from the current identity table) while
102	the log's names are *fossils* captured at each event, so the two disagreeing
103	about which pets exist is normal after a delete, not corruption.
104	
105	**Delete-compaction is already handled correctly — don't go hunting there.**
106	`do_delete_pet()` in `ui_lvgl.c` shifts its four `g_meal_*` tables, calls
107	`velapaw_store_delete(id)` ("history + BCS, shifted to match") and
108	`velapaw_identity_delete(id)`, then invalidates every held id.
109	`identity.h:52` documents the renumbering hazard explicitly. A single enrolled
110	pet alongside four names in the log just means three were deleted via the UI.
111	
112	Name junk enters at the **UI enroll dialog** (`ui_lvgl.c:1041`), not the
113	Rex/Milo scaffold — those literals are clean. The on-screen keyboard admits a
114	stray comma or double space, and `identity.c:276` stores argv verbatim
115	(`strncpy`, no trim). It is the single write site, so trimming there covers
116	the dialog, the CLI and any future agent tool.
117	
118	### Anchor bump VERIFIED 2026-10-11 — and it lands one boot LATE
119	
120	Flashed `89f1f3f1877c8e525cd696973393a88e` (1561984 B) with the anchor at
121	`1791676800L`. **First boot: nothing changed.** Second boot: `status.md` read
122	`today: 0 g in 0 meal(s)` / `last 7 days: 0 g` / `baseline 0 g/day` — the
123	38-day delta clamped to `DAYS` and the synthetic seed is finally gone. BCS
124	stays `over`, correctly: it is a stored per-pet assessment, not derived from
125	the window.
126	
127	**Why one boot late.** `velapaw_store_init()` is called at `ui_lvgl.c:3594`,
128	**26 lines before** the anchor block at 3620. The clock is already sane at
129	that point — `board_lcd_initialize` syncs it from the PCF85063, and the *old*
130	anchor had written itself there via `board_rtc_settime()`. So store-init sees
131	2026-09-03, takes the equal-day no-op branch, and only then does the anchor
132	push the clock (and the RTC) to 2026-10-11, which the *next* boot picks up.
133	Corollary: on any board that has booted once, the `tv_sec < VP_TS_SANE`
134	branch can never fire — the RTC always reads back plausible. Moving those
135	eleven anchor lines above the `velapaw_store_init()` call would make a bump
136	take effect on the boot you flash it. Not done yet.
137	
138	**`status.md` is written at every boot** — `velapaw_store_init()` runs
139	`vp_history_load()` → `vp_sync_day()` → `vp_status_write()`, and the comment
140	at ~428 says that call exists so a freshly booted board gives the agent's
141	skill something to read. So `status.md` reflects RAM *after* the sync and is
142	the cheapest place to see a day roll (and, since nsh has no `date`, the
143	cheapest proxy for the clock).
144	
145	`history.bin` is persisted on the roll too, but **not by a name you will
146	find in `velapaw_store_init()`**: the save lives one level down, inside
147	`vp_sync_day()`'s shift path, as `vp_history_save()` — not the `vp_persist()`
148	that `velapaw_store_log_feeding()` calls. Grepping init for `vp_persist` and
149	concluding "the shift never reaches disk" is wrong, and it cost a round here.
150	(Header decode: `32 30 50 56` is `"VP02"` little-endian, then 8 pets, 30
151	days, then the day stamp.)
152	
153	**Diagnostic discipline that would have saved three rounds:** a reset-and-
154	recheck is only evidence if the pasted scrollback contains the `NuttShell
155	(NSH)` banner. One intermediate hexdump here had no banner, still read the
156	old day stamp, and sent me hunting for a persistence bug that did not exist.
157	Demand the banner before believing a reboot happened.
158	
159	**The boot-dispense claim above is NOT established.** Two clean boots with
160	nothing in front of the camera produced no `[feeder] dispensed` line at all,
161	because Model-B meals are **recognition-gated** — the clock alone never
162	dispenses. The earlier unprompted feed must have had a recognition event
163	behind it. Do not "fix" this by moving the anchor hour to 04:00; there is no
164	evidence for the mechanism.
165	
166	Firmware `708b0bcadd63743002a4ddba0ccf55e5` (1567136 B). The image got
167	**16 bytes smaller** despite ~150 lines of new C — `roll_day` traded an
168	inlined double loop for a call into the shared `vp_shift_days`. Size was
169	useless as a staleness check here; `nm nuttx/nuttx | grep vp_` proved the
170	code was linked in (absence would have proved nothing — statics can be
171	inlined away).

36	
37	## Why it "hung" / stopped recognizing (ranked)
38	1. **`recog_done` latch** — after one match or 2 misses, Recognize waited for a tab re-entry; looks exactly like "fails to recognize". stab1 re-arms on a tap, on a scene change (4×4 brightness signature), and once a minute while a meal is due (its first 30 min); gap 30 s after a hit, 3 s doubling to 20 s after misses.
39	2. **Console jam** — `uart_write` takes `xmit.lock` BEFORE it checks O_NONBLOCK, so one blocking writer + a host that stopped draining COM8 (PuTTY closed, PC asleep) jams every writer, UI thread included. stab1: `uprintf` (UI) and `vp_say` (store) ask FIONSPACE first (answered under a spinlock) and drop the line instead (counted as `drop`). Rejected: a pipe relay (CONFIG_PIPES off) and a dup2 mute.
40	3. Midnight: `today_total` wasn't reconciled for a board running past midnight → a day that ended at the cap refused the next day's meals. Fix: `velapaw_store_sync_day()` on the UI's day change.
41	4. Skips survived midnight. 5. BCS ran outside `g_tflm_lock` (raced KWS). 6. The preview ran at 150 ms forever after a match. 7. The worker could stick in state 2. 8. The camera HAL hides failures: `velapaw_camera_get_frame` always returns 0 and keeps the old frame, so watch `same`, not `err`. 9. After a reset the UI booted on Enroll (pauses after 30 s). 10. Fed/skip flags were RAM-only → a reset could re-serve an eaten meal. 11. `g_last_fed` was never read → no gap between two due meals. 12. The limit-hit path left stale `fed_min`/`fed_g`.
42	
43	## Design decisions worth keeping
44	- **At-most-once feeding:** `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/fed.bin` (magic `VPF1`, via `velapaw_store_put/get`) is saved BEFORE the dispense; `FEED_GAP_MIN` 20; a slot closed by the daily limit shows "skipped"; skips restore only on the same day.
45	- **Stall monitor:** a prio+10 thread (2 KB stack) watches the UI heartbeat (2 min; 10 min while the tag is `feed`) and the recognition worker (1 min). A prio+5 note thread (6 KB) writes `STALL <kind> at <tag> <age>s | <health line>` to flash, then `up_systemreset()` (reset code 0x03); it waits at most 3 s for the note. Started right before the main loop. **Not a HW watchdog** — an interrupts-off hang isn't caught.
46	- **health.log** = `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/health.log`, rotates at 4 KB into `health.old`. Boot line `HH:MM boot rst 0xNN`; every 10 min `HH:MM up Nm tab T cap N max Nms slow N same N err N embed N hit N miss N inf S drop N`. `velapaw voice` (read-only probe) prints the live line + the boot code.
47	- **There is NO software-reset command in this build:** `reboot` → `nsh: reboot: command not found` (2026-10-18), probably because `CONFIG_BOARDCTL_RESET` is off. **Don't suggest ai_agent's `restart`**: without BOARDCTL_RESET it prints "Restarting..." and sleeps forever, which parks the agent CLI. The RESET button gives 0x01, so the 0x03 → start-on-Recognize path can only be exercised by a real stall.
48	- Reset codes (`esp32s3_reset_reasons(0)`): 0x01 power-on/brown-out/RESET button, **0x03 CORE_SW = the stall monitor's `up_systemreset()`**, 0x07/0x08 MWDT, 0x09 RTC WDT, 0x0f brown-out, 0x15/0x16 USB UART/JTAG (esptool). Any other code than 0x01/0x15/0x16, with pets enrolled, boots on Recognize.
49	- Never patch `ui_i18n.c` — stab1 reuses `S_POINT_AT_PET`, `S_NEXT_MEAL_FMT`, `S_SKIPPED`.
50	
51	## Gotchas
52	- All velapaw sources are **LF** — an in-session note that said CRLF was wrong.
53	- No LVGL heap metric (`CONFIG_LV_USE_CLIB_MALLOC=y`) and a heap walk kills the board ([[velapaw-heap-walk-kills-board]]).
54	- Thread stacks come from IMEM (~64 KB headroom before stab1's 8 KB).
55	- Pre-existing VM warnings outside the patched files — ignore: `ui_i18n.c:245` `f14` set but not used; `agent_loop.c:740` `-Wformat-truncation`.
56	- Local compile check: `cc_check.sh <a|b> <file>` = arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.4 after `source /d/openVela/vela-env.sh`, flags from `compile_commands.json`, item8/b headers (`identity.h` 564256ad, `ui_i18n.h` 778b1a32). The VM is xtensa GCC 12.2, so the VM warning gate is the real check.
57	- Still-ungated prints (feeder, TFLM, BCS lazy init, identity, boot init, camera + LVGL syslog): a jam there now ends in a stall reset + a log line instead of a silent hang.
58	- A stall reset re-enumerates USB: reopen COM8, redo `ifconfig eth0 …`, ping to prime ARP ([[velapaw-cdcncm-networking]]).
59	
60	Offered, not done: HW watchdog (`CONFIG_WATCHDOG` + automonitor), `CONFIG_BOARD_RESET_ON_ASSERT`, syslog hardening, auto-ifconfig after a reset, idle return to Recognize, a camera HAL that returns -1 / re-inits. Related: [[velapaw-agent-on-lcd]] (the open `llm_cache` fix), [[velapaw-scheduled-feeding]], [[velapaw-recognize-tuning]].

---
name: velapaw-appetite-review
description: "2026-10-25 check of VelaPaw's appetite maths on stab1b: the counting is right, the scoring is wrong (the screen uses the 60 g cap as the yardstick, status.md uses a ÷29 baseline, and each power-on session counts as a day); explains the red bell; ap1 fix offered, not started"
metadata:
  type: project
---

**Verdict.** Code read in the stab1b `b/` sources; the board image is `50a701e8`.

**The counting is right:**
- feeds land in the right day;
- the window rolls at midnight and on every clock-lost boot;
- history survives resets;
- today's grams, the meal count, the week total and the 60 g hard cap are all correct.

**The scoring is wrong.**

**Screen (My Pets, the Trends line, the bell)**
- `pet_appetite_pct` = today ÷ `daily_limit_g`, capped at 100 (`ui_lvgl.c:1365-1377`).
- `pet_alert_drop` fires when yesterday < half the limit.
- With Bob's numbers (13 g portion × 3 meals = 39 g, 60 g limit):
  - a perfect day = 65%, shown amber (green needs ≥70%);
  - 09:54 after breakfast = 21%, shown red;
  - the alert fires on any day under 30 g, so **missing one meal of three** is enough.
- My Pets then reads "⚠ Appetite drop (21%)": yesterday's flag next to today's running %.

**status.md (what the agent reads, `store_stub.c:582-623`)**
- The baseline is the sum of the 29 prior days ÷ 29 **always**, but the window was wiped on 2026-10-11.
  - 10-18 read 13/29 = 0 g/day, then a hard-coded "100% of baseline".
  - Once it fills a little, e.g. 117/29 = 4, a normal 39 g day reads 975%.
- Its alert (yesterday < half the ÷28 average) fires only on a near-zero day.
- The "Avg: X g/day" on My Pets and Trends is the same deflated number.
- **So the bell and the agent can disagree.**

**No battery, so a "day" is really a power-on session (stab1b)**
- The last short session becomes "yesterday" at the next plug-in, which turns the bell red.
- This is the most likely cause of the red bell in the 09:54 photo.
- To confirm it on the device:
  - tap the bell: a "bob: sudden appetite drop…" line means the rule above; a line with a time stamp means the agent heartbeat (`g_ag_alert`);
  - on Trends, tap the second-to-last bar to see yesterday's grams.

**Finals risk**
- The cold boot makes the last rehearsal session "yesterday", so the bell goes red unless Bob got ≥30 g in that session.
- A voice "yes" on Recognize with Bob recognised serves an off-schedule portion without marking a meal slot.

**Other notes**
- The grams logged are the portion asked (13 g); the motor drops ~15 g (3 pockets). There is no scale, so say "served", not "eaten".
- Enrolling (or re-enrolling) seeds 29 fake days at portion × 3 ± 10 g (`ui_lvgl.c:1626` → `velapaw_store_seed`).
- "Next Day (demo)" on My Pets rolls the window, which can demo the alert on purpose.

**ap1: offered, NOT started (wait for a yes)**
- The yardstick becomes the planned day = min(limit, portion × meals set − owner skips).
- Today is measured against the meals due so far.
- The alert fires only for a day that ended while the board was running (the midnight branch or Next Day), and only when the pet got under half the plan (= missed 2 of 3 meals). This uses a RAM flag, so neither history.bin nor fed.bin changes format.
- status.md uses the same numbers. Its baseline becomes the average since the first fed day, with "not enough days yet" under 3 days.
- No `ui_i18n.c` change: existing strings only.

Related: [[velapaw-feeding-history-daystamp]], [[velapaw-stability-stab1]], [[velapaw-trends-dashboard]], [[velapaw-recognize-tuning]].

Summary:

The user wrote: "a few seconds and can you check iif appetite is being calculated correctly".
- "a few seconds" answers my earlier question: Bob is now recognized in a few seconds. Per my recommendation, the recognition firmware stays as it is; rt1 is not needed.

**Earlier work: done**

2. Key Technical Concepts

**Board and firmware**
- The board runs stab1b, md5 `50a701e808a3a63da472965ca45d9cd3`. Rollback: stab1 `a109963a` in `~/velapaw-golden/pre-stab1b-clock/`.
- There is no battery. Every unplug loses the RTC, and the next cold boot starts the day after the store's last day, at 08:00 (`clock lost` in health.log). So a board "day" = a power-on session unless the board stays on past midnight.
- `wall_day()` = epoch/86400 (UTC); the store's `vp_today_num()` uses `localtime_r`. They are the same with no TZ.

**Store (store_stub.c)**
- `g_day_g[8][30]` (grams) and `g_day_m[8][30]` (meals); slot 29 = TODAY.
- History file: history.bin, VP02 = 4-word header with the day stamp. A geometry mismatch resets it.
- `vp_sync_day()` shifts forward only. It is called from init, from log_feeding, and from `velapaw_store_sync_day()`; the UI calls that at a day change and in the clock-lost path.
- status.md is rewritten on every persist, on status_refresh, and at init.

**Bob's settings**
- Portion 13 g; the motor actually drops ~15 g (3 pockets, "asked 13g").
- Daily limit 60 g.
- Meals 07:50 / 12:15 / 18:00 (status.md, 10-18). The photo showed "next meal at 18:30", which is unexplained; I asked and got no answer.
- History was wiped on 2026-10-11 by the 38-day clock jump. Since then the data is real but sparse.

**Feeding paths**
- Both the scheduled and the voice "yes" paths trim the serving to min(portion, limit − today) and log `amount` (the asked grams).
- The voice yes-feed needs a recognized pet (g_cand) and deliberately does not consume a meal slot.

**Alerts and controls**
- The bell turns red if `g_ag_alert` (an ai_agent heartbeat reply that isn't OK) or `pet_alert_drop()` fires for any pet.
- The bell popup lists:
  - S_ALERT_APPETITE_FMT: "⚠ %s: sudden appetite drop - consider a vet check.";
  - BCS under/over lines;
  - the agent warning, with a time (S_AG_WARN_FMT);
  - otherwise "All pets eating normally."
- The "Next Day (demo)" button (S_NEXT_DAY, My Pets tab, ui_lvgl.c:2365) handles EV_NEXTDAY: it calls `velapaw_store_roll_day()`, resets `g_meal_fed_day` to −1 and clears skips.

3. Files and Code Sections

All sources are under `D:\openVela\velapaw-snapshots\2026-10-18-stab1b-prepared\b\apps\examples\velapaw\`. They are board-identical; MANIFEST.md5: ui_lvgl.c 230e2022, store_stub.c 5c0920dc, store.h 7cf5ddf6.

**`ui/ui_lvgl.c`, lines 1358–1377: the UI appetite rules (limit-based)**
```c
static int pet_appetite_pct(velapaw_pet_id_t id, const struct velapaw_pet *p)
{
  int today = velapaw_store_today_total(id);
  int pct = (p->daily_limit_g > 0) ? today * 100 / p->daily_limit_g : 100;
  return (pct > 100) ? 100 : pct;   /* limit is a cap: never over 100% */
}
/* appetite-drop alert: the last completed day was under half the daily limit. */
static int pet_alert_drop(velapaw_pet_id_t id, const struct velapaw_pet *p)
{
  int yesterday = velapaw_store_day_total(id, 1);
  return (p->daily_limit_g > 0 && yesterday * 2 < p->daily_limit_g) ? 1 : 0;
}
```

**`ui/ui_lvgl.c`, other sections**
- **1456–1461:** `g_ag_alert`, `g_ag_min`, `g_ag_txt[160]`.
- **1508–1576:** `bell_cb` lists the alerts.
- **1626:** `velapaw_store_seed(id, portion * 3);   /* baseline ~3 meals/day for trends */` runs at enrollment and fills 29 fake prior days.
- **2120–2267, `refresh_pets`:**
  - `avg = velapaw_store_baseline_g(i)`, `pct = pet_appetite_pct`, `alert = pet_alert_drop`;
  - `pcol = (pct >= 70) ? COL_FED : (pct >= 40) ? COL_COOL : COL_UNK`;
  - shows S_APPETITE_DROP_FMT "⚠ Appetite drop (%d%%)" when the alert is set, else "Appetite: %d%%";
  - S_AVG_WEEK_FMT "Avg: %d g/day    Week: %d g".
- **2595–2675, `refresh_trends`:**
  - the bars show grams per day (`velapaw_store_day_total`);
  - `g_trend_avg` = completed days in the view / (n−1);
  - the appetite line plots each day's grams × 100 / daily_limit_g, capped at 100;
  - the stats line S_TREND_STATS_FMT "Today %d/%dg   Avg %dg/day\nWeek %dg   Month %dg   Appetite %d%%" uses `velapaw_store_baseline_g` and `pet_appetite_pct`.
- **2680–2702:** bar colour: green if ≥ g_trend_avg, else accent.
- **2707–2727:** the appetite chart is a line chart, Y range 0–100.
- **3596–3675:** the voice yes/no path. "yes" plus g_cand checks the limit (S_LIMIT_HIT_FMT), trims, dispenses and logs the feeding. It does NOT mark a meal slot ("off-schedule treat").
- **4313–4344, `ag_poll`:** `if (g_ag_hb && g_ag_state == AG_REPLIED) { g_ag_min = wall_min(); g_ag_alert = !g_ag_ok; ... }`.
- **4660–4687:** the clock-lost floor. `day = last+1` if `last` lies in [anchor day, anchor day+3660); 08:00; `g_clock_lost = 1`; `velapaw_store_sync_day()`.
- **4740–4766:** the day-change block runs `velapaw_store_sync_day()`. If `last_day >= 0` (midnight while running), it clears `g_meal_skipped`, calls `fed_save()` and refreshes pets and trends. This is the hook point for a "complete day" mark.
- **4801–4815:** EV_NEXTDAY.
- **5154–5196:** scheduled feed trim, `fed_save` before dispense, then `velapaw_store_log_feeding(&ev2)`.

**`store/store_stub.c`**
- **241–322, `vp_status_write`:** prints:
  - "- today: %d g in %d meal(s)"
  - "- last 7 days"
  - "- baseline (average of prior days): %d g/day"

**Appetite findings (verified from code), to deliver to the user**

What's right:
- day bucketing and rolling (midnight and clock-lost boots);
- persistence;
- today's grams, meals, week total;
- the 60 g hard cap trim;
- the Trends bars, which show true grams per day.

What's wrong:
1. **The screen uses the 60 g limit as the yardstick.**
   - A full day (3×13 = 39 g) reads 65%, amber; it can never be green.
   - At 09:54 after breakfast it reads 21%, red.
   - My Pets then shows "⚠ Appetite drop (21%)", mixing yesterday's flag with today's partial figure.
2. **The bell is too sensitive.** It fires when yesterday < 30 g, so missing one meal (26 g) triggers "sudden appetite drop - consider a vet check."
3. **Each cold boot creates a "day".** A short session becomes yesterday, which turns the bell red. This is most likely the red bell in the photo; on 10-18, yesterday was 13 g, also red.
4. **The status.md baseline divides by 29 including empty days.**
   - 10-18: 13/29 → 0, printed as a fixed "100% of baseline".
   - Example: 3 days of 39 g → 117/29 = 4 → a normal day reads 975%.
   - My Pets and Trends "Avg" show the same deflated number.
5. **The agent's status.md alert disagrees with the screen.** It fires only when yesterday ≈ 0 against the deflated base.

Heads-ups:
- The grams are served (asked 13 g, ~15 g dropped), not eaten; there is no scale.
- Re-enrolling (or enrolling live at the finals) seeds 29 fake days at ≈39 g/day.

How to confirm without a console:
- Tap the bell: the "bob: sudden appetite drop…" line is the drop rule; a line with a time and agent text came from the agent.
- On Trends, tap the second-to-last bar: "yesterday: N g" — if N < 30, that's the cause.
- Optional: `cat /data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md` (never config.json).

**Finals risk**
A cold boot makes the last pre-finals session "yesterday". Under 30 g means a red bell and "Appetite drop" in front of the judges.

Possible workarounds without firmware:
- Make sure Bob gets ≥ 3 portions (≥ 30 g) in the last session.
- Voice "yes" feeds add grams without using a slot, but I hadn't confirmed what triggers the voice prompt, so present this with care or skip it.
- Or explain the bell.

**Verdict.** Code read in the stab1b `b/` sources; the board image is `50a701e8`.

**The counting is right:**
- feeds land in the right day;
- the window rolls at midnight and on every clock-lost boot;
- history survives resets;
- today's grams, the meal count, the week total and the 60 g hard cap are all correct.

**The scoring is wrong.**

**Screen (My Pets, the Trends line, the bell)**
- `pet_appetite_pct` = today ÷ `daily_limit_g`, capped at 100 (`ui_lvgl.c:1365-1377`).
- `pet_alert_drop` fires when yesterday < half the limit.
- With Bob's numbers (13 g portion × 3 meals = 39 g, 60 g limit):
  - a perfect day = 65%, shown amber (green needs ≥70%);
  - 09:54 after breakfast = 21%, shown red;
  - the alert fires on any day under 30 g, so **missing one meal of three** is enough.
- My Pets then reads "⚠ Appetite drop (21%)": yesterday's flag next to today's running %.

**status.md (what the agent reads, `store_stub.c:582-623`)**
- The baseline is the sum of the 29 prior days ÷ 29 **always**, but the window was wiped on 2026-10-11.
  - 10-18 read 13/29 = 0 g/day, then a hard-coded "100% of baseline".
  - Once it fills a little, e.g. 117/29 = 4, a normal 39 g day reads 975%.
- Its alert (yesterday < half the ÷28 average) fires only on a near-zero day.
- The "Avg: X g/day" on My Pets and Trends is the same deflated number.
- **So the bell and the agent can disagree.**

**No battery, so a "day" is really a power-on session (stab1b)**
- The last short session becomes "yesterday" at the next plug-in, which turns the bell red.
- This is the most likely cause of the red bell in the 09:54 photo.
- To confirm it on the device:
  - tap the bell: a "bob: sudden appetite drop…" line means the rule above; a line with a time stamp means the agent heartbeat (`g_ag_alert`);
  - on Trends, tap the second-to-last bar to see yesterday's grams.

**Finals risk**
- The cold boot makes the last rehearsal session "yesterday", so the bell goes red unless Bob got ≥30 g in that session.
- A voice "yes" on Recognize with Bob recognised serves an off-schedule portion without marking a meal slot.

**Other notes**
- The grams logged are the portion asked (13 g); the motor drops ~15 g (3 pockets). There is no scale, so say "served", not "eaten".
- Enrolling (or re-enrolling) seeds 29 fake days at portion × 3 ± 10 g (`ui_lvgl.c:1626` → `velapaw_store_seed`).
- "Next Day (demo)" on My Pets rolls the window, which can demo the alert on purpose.

**ap1: offered, NOT started (wait for a yes)**
- The yardstick becomes the planned day = min(limit, portion × meals set − owner skips).
- Today is measured against the meals due so far.
- The alert fires only for a day that ended while the board was running (the midnight branch or Next Day), and only when the pet got under half the plan (= missed 2 of 3 meals). This uses a RAM flag, so neither history.bin nor fed.bin changes format.
- status.md uses the same numbers. Its baseline becomes the average since the first fed day, with "not enough days yet" under 3 days.
- No `ui_i18n.c` change: existing strings only.

Related: [[velapaw-feeding-history-daystamp]], [[velapaw-stability-stab1]], [[velapaw-trends-dashboard]], [[velapaw-recognize-tuning]].

Fix: `cp apps/mlearning/esp_nn_kernels/{depthwise_conv,fully_connected,pooling,add,mul,softmax}.cc` 18 into that active esp_nn dir + `rm` its stale `.o` + delete `libtflite-micro*.a`, rebuild. 19 The Makefile auto-globs `esp_nn/*.cc` and filters out the matching reference kernels. 20 (Note: esp-nn's S3-SIMD sources `*esp32s3.c` are `filter-out`'d in the Makefile — a 21 further ~2-4x is likely left on the table if those + `-DCONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32S3` 22 can be made to build under NuttX.) 23 24 **Background-thread recognize (no UI freeze).** The 1.3s Invoke ran on the LVGL/UI 25 loop -> froze touch+preview. Fixed in `ui/ui_lvgl.c`: a `recog_worker` pthread 26 (32KB stack) runs embed()+match(); UI hands off a frame via `g_inf_state` (0 idle, 27 1 request, 2 busy, 3 done) and pauses preview capture while busy so the shared frame 28 buffer isn't overwritten. All LVGL updates + BCS + feed stay on the UI thread in the 29 state==3 consume block. Confirmed: touch/preview live during inference. 30 31 **Match tuning:** `VELAPAW_MATCH_THRESHOLD=0.45` (velapaw.h), `RECOG_STABLE_N=1`, 32 retry cap `recog_tries>=2`. On-device scores: bob 0.53-0.84 (dips to ~0.20 on bad 33 frames), unknowns <=0.22 -> 0.45 cleanly separates (0.15 default caused false feeds). 34 Embedding is noisy but discriminative enough. STABLE_N=1 acts on the first good frame. 35 36 **ENROLLMENT QUALITY is the dominant lever for FALSE-ACCEPTS (2026-07-17).** User pointed the camera at a CHAIR and Recognize confidently returned "bob 0.71" — a false accept well above the 0.45 gate. Root cause is fundamental to open-set recognition with a generic pet feature-extractor: the model was never trained to reject non-pets, so OOD inputs (chair/wall/hand) still produce an embedding that can land near an enrolled pet. With ONE enrolled pet the margin (best-second) can't help either. **No threshold cleanly fixes it** — a 0.71 chair sits inside bob's legitimate 0.53-0.84 range, so raising the gate to reject the chair also rejects real bob frames. **THE FIX THAT WORKED: re-enroll the pet properly** — 5 shots with the pet's FACE FILLING THE FRAME, close, well-lit, minimal background. A hasty/background-heavy enrollment puts the centroid in a "generic" region where lots of things score high; tight face-on shots pull it to a distinctive spot and the chair correctly reads Unknown. Confirmed on hardware. **Demo implication:** enrollment quality, not the threshold, is what makes recognition trustworthy — enroll carefully before the defense. (Deeper fixes for arbitrary-object rejection = a pet/no-pet gate model or an individually-trained model; both need GPU/data, not done.) 37 38 **GOTCHA - header edits don't recompile:** editing `velapaw.h` (the threshold) did 39 NOT rebuild `identity.o` — the incremental build missed the header dep, so the old 40 0.15 stayed compiled in and false-matching persisted. Fix: `find apps/examples/velapaw 41 -name '*.c' -exec touch {} +` to force recompilation after any HEADER change. 42 43 The "recognize hangs" the user reported was NOT an infinite loop (the `recog_tries` 44 cap was present) — it was the on-UI-thread freeze + the false-matching. Look 1 starts at once, look 2 comes `RECOG_INTERVAL_MS` 1200 + ~1.3 s later. With no match, the status shows "Point at a pet" and recognition rests. The rest ends on a tap (immediately), on a scene change once the miss gap has passed, or on the 1/min meal poll. The miss gap is 3→6→12→20 s and is reset only by a hit or by leaving the tab. **A still pet or photo never counts as a change.** After a hit, movement is ignored for 30 s (`REARM_HIT_MS`), so **tap before showing a second pet**. Almost. The Next Day button is the right tool, but I'd skip the clean slate, and the order matters: **feed Bob first, then press Next Day.** I checked both in the code.

**Why I'd skip the clean slate**
- **Deleting and re-enrolling Bob:** the board fills the previous 29 days with made-up days of about 40 g, so the bell starts grey. But it has costs:
  - Bob's real history is gone for good, and Trends shows made-up data.
  - The next unplug undoes it, because the enrolling session becomes "yesterday".
  - Recognition is only as good as the new enrollment photos. It takes a few seconds now, so I wouldn't risk it.
- **Wiping the history file:** every past day becomes 0 g, so the bell goes red straight away.
- **Erasing the flash:** don't. It also wipes the recognition and voice models and the agent's settings.

**Why the order matters.** Next Day turns today into "yesterday" and makes all of Bob's meals due again. If Bob had less than 30 g today when you press it, the bell turns red.

**Venue routine (no firmware change).** Do this during setup, in the same power-on you'll present with:
1. Plug in and let the board recognize Bob, so breakfast is served (13 g). Ignore the bell for now.
2. On Recognize, with voice on, say "yes" twice. Bob is now at 39 g.
3. On My Pets, press Next Day (demo). Yesterday becomes 39 g, so the bell turns grey.
4. Take Bob's photo out of view straight away. Otherwise breakfast is served again on the spot and there's nothing to show on stage. Empty the bowl and top up the hopper.
5. Don't unplug until your slot is over. RESET is fine because it keeps the clock.

On stage, show Bob and breakfast is served.

**Optional: show the alert on purpose.** After that on-stage breakfast, press Next Day again. The bell turns red, and tapping it shows "bob: sudden appetite drop - consider a vet check". That's correct by the board's own rules, since Bob had one meal of three that "day", and it shows off the health watchdog.

**What the routine can't fix**
- My Pets reads "Appetite: 0%" until breakfast, then 21%, both in red. You can say "13 of today's 60 g so far."
- The agent's appetite figures are still wrong, so don't ask it about Bob's appetite on stage.

Only the ap1 firmware fix sorts those out, and with it you wouldn't need the routine at all. That offer still stands if you want it.

37	## Why it "hung" / stopped recognizing (ranked)
38	1. **`recog_done` latch** — after one match or 2 misses, Recognize waited for a tab re-entry; looks exactly like "fails to recognize". stab1 re-arms on a tap, on a scene change (4×4 brightness signature), and once a minute while a meal is due (its first 30 min); gap 30 s after a hit, 3 s doubling to 20 s after misses.
39	2. **Console jam** — `uart_write` takes `xmit.lock` BEFORE it checks O_NONBLOCK, so one blocking writer + a host that stopped draining COM8 (PuTTY closed, PC asleep) jams every writer, UI thread included. stab1: `uprintf` (UI) and `vp_say` (store) ask FIONSPACE first (answered under a spinlock) and drop the line instead (counted as `drop`). Rejected: a pipe relay (CONFIG_PIPES off) and a dup2 mute.
40	3. Midnight: `today_total` wasn't reconciled for a board running past midnight → a day that ended at the cap refused the next day's meals. Fix: `velapaw_store_sync_day()` on the UI's day change.
41	4. Skips survived midnight. 5. BCS ran outside `g_tflm_lock` (raced KWS). 6. The preview ran at 150 ms forever after a match. 7. The worker could stick in state 2. 8. The camera HAL hides failures: `velapaw_camera_get_frame` always returns 0 and keeps the old frame, so watch `same`, not `err`. 9. After a reset the UI booted on Enroll (pauses after 30 s). 10. Fed/skip flags were RAM-only → a reset could re-serve an eaten meal. 11. `g_last_fed` was never read → no gap between two due meals. 12. The limit-hit path left stale `fed_min`/`fed_g`.
42	
43	## Design decisions worth keeping
44	- **At-most-once feeding:** `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/fed.bin` (magic `VPF1`, via `velapaw_store_put/get`) is saved BEFORE the dispense; `FEED_GAP_MIN` 20; a slot closed by the daily limit shows "skipped"; skips restore only on the same day.
45	- **Stall monitor:** a prio+10 thread (2 KB stack) watches the UI heartbeat (2 min; 10 min while the tag is `feed`) and the recognition worker (1 min). A prio+5 note thread (6 KB) writes `STALL <kind> at <tag> <age>s | <health line>` to flash, then `up_systemreset()` (reset code 0x03); it waits at most 3 s for the note. Started right before the main loop. **Not a HW watchdog** — an interrupts-off hang isn't caught.
46	- **health.log** = `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/health.log`, rotates at 4 KB into `health.old`. Boot line `HH:MM boot rst 0xNN`; every 10 min `HH:MM up Nm tab T cap N max Nms slow N same N err N embed N hit N miss N inf S drop N`. `velapaw voice` (read-only probe) prints the live line + the boot code.
47	- **There is NO software-reset command in this build:** `reboot` → `nsh: reboot: command not found` (2026-10-18), probably because `CONFIG_BOARDCTL_RESET` is off. **Don't suggest ai_agent's `restart`**: without BOARDCTL_RESET it prints "Restarting..." and sleeps forever, which parks the agent CLI. The RESET button gives 0x01, so the 0x03 → start-on-Recognize path can only be exercised by a real stall.
48	- Reset codes (`esp32s3_reset_reasons(0)`): 0x01 power-on/brown-out/RESET button, **0x03 CORE_SW = the stall monitor's `up_systemreset()`**, 0x07/0x08 MWDT, 0x09 RTC WDT, 0x0f brown-out, 0x15/0x16 USB UART/JTAG (esptool). Any other code than 0x01/0x15/0x16, with pets enrolled, boots on Recognize.
49	- Never patch `ui_i18n.c` — stab1 reuses `S_POINT_AT_PET`, `S_NEXT_MEAL_FMT`, `S_SKIPPED`.
50	
51	## Gotchas
52	- All velapaw sources are **LF** — an in-session note that said CRLF was wrong.
53	- No LVGL heap metric (`CONFIG_LV_USE_CLIB_MALLOC=y`) and a heap walk kills the board ([[velapaw-heap-walk-kills-board]]).
54	- Thread stacks come from IMEM (~64 KB headroom before stab1's 8 KB).
55	- Pre-existing VM warnings outside the patched files — ignore: `ui_i18n.c:245` `f14` set but not used; `agent_loop.c:740` `-Wformat-truncation`.
56	- Local compile check: `cc_check.sh <a|b> <file>` = arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.4 after `source /d/openVela/vela-env.sh`, flags from `compile_commands.json`, item8/b headers (`identity.h` 564256ad, `ui_i18n.h` 778b1a32). The VM is xtensa GCC 12.2, so the VM warning gate is the real check.
57	- Still-ungated prints (feeder, TFLM, BCS lazy init, identity, boot init, camera + LVGL syslog): a jam there now ends in a stall reset + a log line instead of a silent hang.
58	- A stall reset re-enumerates USB: reopen COM8, redo `ifconfig eth0 …`, ping to prime ARP ([[velapaw-cdcncm-networking]]).
59	
60	Offered, not done: HW watchdog (`CONFIG_WATCHDOG` + automonitor), `CONFIG_BOARD_RESET_ON_ASSERT`, syslog hardening, auto-ifconfig after a reset, idle return to Recognize, a camera HAL that returns -1 / re-inits. 11	The VM's `apps/examples/velapaw/Makefile` is **untracked by git** — if it's clobbered, git cannot restore it. I destroyed it once (2026-07-13) by copying the contest repo's Makefile over it; they are NOT the same file (the contest one uses `-I$(APPDIR)/packages/demos/contest2026_043_velapaw`, mock camera, and stub inference). Master copy now lives at `D:\openVela\contest2026_043_CircuitForge\app\velapaw\Makefile`.
12	
13	**How to recover it if lost again:** the `.o` files from the last good build are a fingerprint of the real source list — `find . -name '*.o'` in the app dir tells you exactly what was compiled. `CMakeLists.txt` (the mirror build) gives the flags/defines.
14	
15	**⚠️ THE BIG ONE — never put `-DTF_LITE_STATIC_MEMORY` in this Makefile.** The Make-built TFLM library (`apps/mlearning/tflite-micro/Makefile`) does **not** define it, and that macro **changes the layout of `TfLiteTensor`** in `tensorflow/lite/core/c/common.h`. Define it on the app side only and the two disagree on field offsets: `AllocateTensors` still succeeds (all inside the library), then **the first `Invoke()` writes through a garbage pointer and HARD-WEDGES THE SoC** — console dies ("semaphore timeout" on open), no crash dump, on *any* thread, from *any* tab. It looks exactly like a camera/DMA/stack bug and it is none of those. Cost a full evening (2026-07-13): I blamed the servo, then idle camera streaming, then the PSRAM stack, all wrong. **`CMakeLists.txt` DOES define it — correctly, because the CMake `tflite_micro` target compiles the library with it too. So flags from the CMake build are NOT portable into this Makefile.** Symptom to recognize instantly: models load, `AllocateTensors OK`, then the board dies on the first inference.
16	
17	**The other flags that each cost a failed build:**
18	1. `CXXEXT = .cc` — NuttX `Application.mk`'s C++ pattern rule keys off `CXXEXT` (default `.cxx`). Without this, `.cc` sources give *"target doesn't match the target pattern"* and `g++: fatal error: no input files`.
19	2. **Mirror tflite-micro's `-D` set exactly** (from `apps/mlearning/tflite-micro/Makefile`, and note the debug trio is an **if/else — not all three**): ours is the strip branch → `TF_LITE_STRIP_ERROR_STRINGS` (NOT `TF_LITE_SHOW_MEMORY_USE`/`TF_LITE_USE_CTIME`, which are the `CONFIG_TFLITEMICRO_DEBUG=y` branch), plus `TFLITE_EMULATE_FLOAT`, `TF_LITE_DISABLE_X86_NEON`, `TF_LITE_USE_GLOBAL_CMATH_FUNCTIONS`, and the esp-nn block `-DESP_NN=1 -DCONFIG_NN_OPTIMIZED -mlongcalls`. `TF_LITE_STRIP_ERROR_STRINGS` compiles `MicroPrintf()` *out of the library*, so an app built without it → `undefined reference to MicroPrintf` at link (that link error is a useful *confirmation* of which branch the library used).
20	3. `CXXFLAGS += -fno-threadsafe-statics` — see [[velapaw-tflm-onboard]]; without it TFLM deadlocks in `__cxa_guard_acquire` → blue screen.
21	
22	**Rule of thumb:** the app and the prebuilt TFLM library share headers, so ANY header-visible define must match on both sides. When inference misbehaves in a way that makes no sense, diff the app's flags against the library's Makefile before suspecting hardware.
23	
24	TFLM's `Make.defs` does NOT export include dirs globally, so velapaw must carry its own `-I`: TFLM root + `third_party/flatbuffers/include` + `$(APPDIR)/math/{gemmlowp,kissfft,ruy}/*`, plus `-include .../float_shim.h -fpermissive`. Also `STACKSIZE = 32768` (LVGL) and `-DVELAPAW_HAVE_BCS` on **both** CFLAGS and CXXFLAGS.
25	
26	## ⚠️ Two silent stale-build traps — `make` lies about having rebuilt
27	
28	Both look **identical to a successful build of unchanged source**: `make -j8`
29	goes straight from the linker-script `CPP:` steps to `LD: nuttx`, no `CC:` of
30	any app file, `Generated: nuttx.bin`, exit 0. NuttX embeds a build timestamp,
31	so the image even has a *new md5* at the *same size*. Nothing warns you.
32	
33	1. **Missing/incorrect `Make.defs`.** An app joins `CONFIGURED_APPS` via a
34	   `Make.defs` in its own directory. Registering a directory that does not
35	   exist drops the app silently — `make` skips it and links stale objects out
36	   of `libapps.a`. The contest repo's version pointed at
37	   `packages/demos/contest2026_043_velapaw`, which does not exist in the VM;
38	   it now probes for `$(APPDIR)/examples/velapaw/Makefile` first.
39	2. **Stale `Make.dep` / `.built`** (hit 2026-08-05, build 43). After a
40	   `make apps_clean`, the app dir's `Make.dep` no longer describes the current
41	   sources, so make has no rule connecting `mic.o` to a rewritten `mic.c`. It
42	   writes a fresh `.built` and moves on. Tell-tale: `.built`/`.depend`/
43	   `Make.dep` timestamps NEWER than the source you just extracted.
44	
45	**Therefore, after extracting any new tarball into the VM app dir:**
46	
47	```sh
48	cd ~/openvela/apps/examples/velapaw && \
49	rm -f .built .depend Make.dep && find . -name "*.o" -delete
50	```
51	
52	**And always prove the new code is in the image before flashing** — pick a
53	string only the new build contains:
54	`grep -ac "some new printf text" nuttx.bin` must be non-zero. `strings` is not
55	available in this Git Bash; `grep -a` on the binary works.
56	
57	Related: **never `rm -rf` the app dir in a fetch command — extract over the
58	top.** Doing so on 2026-08-04 destroyed `ui/ hal/ infer/ identity/ store/
59	assets/` and `Make.defs`, because the tarball only carried `voice/`.
60	
61	Real sources (not the contest repo's): `hal/camera_ov5640.c` (real camera), `hal/feeder_servo.c` (real servo, was `feeder_mock.c`), `ui/ui_lvgl.c`, `assets/velapaw_assets.c`, `infer/backend_tflm.cc` + `infer/gen/velapaw_model_data.cc` (pre-generated, committed — no Python gen step in the Make path).

# Conversation summary: VelaPaw ap1 appetite fix (approved 2026-10-29)

## 1. Primary Request and Intent

**CURRENT, just approved: the ap1 appetite fix.**
- The user said **"lets fix that"**. That answers my last line: "Only the ap1 firmware fix sorts those out, and with it you wouldn't need the routine at all. That offer still stands if you want it."
- This is the explicit yes the standing rule required ("Don't start … any new firmware patch, including ap1, without a yes").
- The task: prepare the ap1 firmware patch kit, give the user the VM apply/build/flash commands as text, and give a hardware test plan.

**ap1 design, as promised to the user:**
- **Plan per day.** Measure each day against Bob's plan: portion × meals set, minus meals the owner skipped, capped by the daily limit. For Bob that is 39 g, so a full day reads 100% (green).
- **Today so far.** Measure today only against the meals due so far, so after breakfast it reads 100%, not 21%.
- **When to judge a day.** Only judge a day that ended while the board was running: real midnight, or "Next Day (demo)". Alert only if the pet got less than half the plan, i.e. missed 2 of 3 meals.
  - Unplugging never raises the alert.
  - The alert flag is RAM-only, so an unplug also clears a real alert.
- **One set of numbers.** status.md (the agent's file) and "Avg" use the same numbers. The average counts only days since tracking began. status.md says "not enough days yet" until there are 3 days.
- **No format changes:**
  - no on-screen text changes (never patch `ui_i18n.c`; reuse existing strings);
  - no history.bin or fed.bin format changes, so Bob's history is kept.
- **Delivery.** Same VM apply-and-flash routine as stab1b.
- **Trade-off, already told to the user:** this is the last firmware change before the finals.

**Earlier in this segment (done):**
- Appetite check delivered. Verdict: the counting is right, the scoring is wrong.
- The "clean slate + Next Day" question was answered:
  - Skip the clean slate.
  - Venue routine: feed Bob 39 g (breakfast plus 2 voice "yes"), then Next Day, then hide Bob, and don't unplug before the slot.
  - This stays the fallback if ap1 isn't flashed in time.

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

**Board and clock**
- The board runs **stab1b, md5 `50a701e808a3a63da472965ca45d9cd3`**. Rollback: stab1 `a109963a` in `~/velapaw-golden/pre-stab1b-clock/`.
- The flashed copy is `D:\openVela\velapaw-snapshots\2026-10-18-stab1b-flashed`.
- The prepared tree is `D:\openVela\velapaw-snapshots\2026-10-18-stab1b-prepared\b\apps\examples\velapaw\`. It is board-identical. MANIFEST md5s:
  - ui_lvgl.c 230e2022
  - store_stub.c 5c0920dc
  - store.h 7cf5ddf6
- There is no battery. Every unplug loses the RTC, and the next boot starts the day after the store's last day, at 08:00 (`clock lost`). So a "day" is really a power-on session.
- A RESET keeps the clock.

**Store (store_stub.c)**
- `g_day_g[8][30]` holds grams and `g_day_m[8][30]` holds meal counts. `TODAY` = 29, `DAYS` = 30.
- `g_hist_day` is the day stamp.
- `vp_sync_day()` only shifts forward.
- status.md is rewritten on every persist, on `velapaw_store_status_refresh()`, and at init. The agent reads status.md.
- `velapaw_store_day_total(id, back)`: back 1 = yesterday.

**UI meal tracking**
- `g_meal_fed_day[pet][k]` equals `wall_day()` when that meal was eaten; −1 resets it.
- Also per pet and meal: `g_meal_fed_min`, `g_meal_fed_g` (0 = closed with nothing served because the limit was hit), `g_meal_skipped`.
- The feed logic uses `wall_day()` and `wall_min()`.

**Pet data**
- `struct velapaw_pet` fields: `name`, `portion_g`, `daily_limit_g`, `meal_min[VELAPAW_MAX_MEALS]` (−1 = unset), `cooldown_s`.
- Bob: 13 g portion, 60 g limit, meals 07:50 / 12:15 / 18:00 (last known). The feeder physically drops about 15 g.

**Colours and screens**
- `COL_FED` 0x57d977 green, `COL_COOL` 0xf0b24a amber, `COL_UNK` 0xe06464 red, `COL_ACCENT` 0x66ccff.
- Appetite % colour: ≥70 green, ≥40 amber, otherwise red.
- The bell turns red **only** on `g_ag_alert` (an agent heartbeat that isn't OK) or `pet_alert_drop()` for any pet. BCS lines appear in the bell list but don't turn it red.

**Voice "yes" feeds**
- They only work on the Recognize tab (tab 1), when voice is running and not dismissed, and Bob is recognized (`g_cand` set, `g_stable >= RECOG_STABLE_N`).
- Each serves min(portion, limit − today) and logs it. No meal slot is marked, and there is no cooldown check.

**Constants and VM**
- `FEED_GAP_MIN` spaces two due meals; `MEAL_POLL_WIN_MIN` is the meal-poll window.
- Build in the VM with `./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j4` from `~/openvela`.
- Clear `.built`, `.depend` and `Make.dep` after every extract. `touch *.c` after any header change.
- Gate on strings (`grep -ac`), never `nm`.
- Flash from Windows with `python -m esptool` on COM3 (check the port first), using BOOT-hold plus a RESET tap.
- The console is COM8. The VM is 192.168.160.128; the Windows host is .1.
- `write-flash 0x0 nuttx.bin` leaves the `.tflite` blobs at 0x600000/0x760000 untouched. Never erase-flash.

## 3. Files and Code Sections

Base path: `D:\openVela\velapaw-snapshots\2026-10-18-stab1b-prepared\b\apps\examples\velapaw\`

### ui/ui_lvgl.c

**Lines 88–91: colour defines** (values above).

```

static int feed_wait_min(int id, long today, int nowm)
{
  int wait_min = 0;
  for (int k = 0; k < VELAPAW_MAX_MEALS; k++)
    {
      int ago = nowm - g_meal_fed_min[id][k];
      if (g_meal_fed_day[id][k] == today && g_meal_fed_g[id][k] > 0 &&
          ago >= 0 && ago < FEED_GAP_MIN && FEED_GAP_MIN - ago > wait_min)

## 5. Problem Solving

**Appetite findings, delivered to the user**

What's correct:
- Day bucketing and rolling.
- Persistence.
- Today's, meal, week and cap figures.
- The Trends bars.

What's wrong:
1. The yardstick is the 60 g limit: a full 39 g day reads 65% amber, and after breakfast 21% red.
2. The alert fires when yesterday is under 30 g, so one missed meal (or an owner skip) triggers it.
3. Every unplug makes a new day, so a short session turns the bell red. This was most likely the bell in the photo.
4. The status.md and Avg baseline divides by 29 including empty days. Results: 0 g/day and "100%", or a normal day reading "975%".
5. The screen and the agent use different alert rules.

**Clean-slate analysis**
- Re-enrolling seeds 29 days (yesterday 43 g, so a grey bell). But:
  - the history is fake;
  - Bob's real history is lost;
  - the enroll defaults reset (15 g, 60 g, 08:00/12:30/18:00);
  - recognition is at risk;
  - the next unplug undoes it.
- A history wipe makes yesterday 0 g, so the bell is red at once.
- Erase-flash kills the models and `/data` (config.json).
- Next Day only after Bob has ≥30 g today. After one meal it turns the bell red; that can be used deliberately to demo the alert.

**Fallback venue routine (if ap1 isn't ready)**
- During setup, in the same power-on as the slot:
  1. Bob is recognized and gets breakfast.
  2. Two voice "yes" bring Bob to 39 g.
  3. Next Day turns the bell grey.
  4. Hide Bob's photo at once (otherwise breakfast is re-served) and empty the bowl.
  5. Don't unplug before the slot.

- **Planned grams:**

- **Day-end judgement:** at the midnight branch (only if `velapaw_store_hist_day()` changed during `sync_day`) and at `EV_NEXTDAY`.
  - Compute before the skips are cleared.
  - Grams of the ended day: `day_total(id,1)` after the roll, or `today_total` before it.

37	## Why it "hung" / stopped recognizing (ranked)
38	1. **`recog_done` latch** — after one match or 2 misses, Recognize waited for a tab re-entry; looks exactly like "fails to recognize". stab1 re-arms on a tap, on a scene change (4×4 brightness signature), and once a minute while a meal is due (its first 30 min); gap 30 s after a hit, 3 s doubling to 20 s after misses.
39	2. **Console jam** — `uart_write` takes `xmit.lock` BEFORE it checks O_NONBLOCK, so one blocking writer + a host that stopped draining COM8 (PuTTY closed, PC asleep) jams every writer, UI thread included. stab1: `uprintf` (UI) and `vp_say` (store) ask FIONSPACE first (answered under a spinlock) and drop the line instead (counted as `drop`). Rejected: a pipe relay (CONFIG_PIPES off) and a dup2 mute.
40	3. Midnight: `today_total` wasn't reconciled for a board running past midnight → a day that ended at the cap refused the next day's meals. Fix: `velapaw_store_sync_day()` on the UI's day change.
41	4. Skips survived midnight. 5. BCS ran outside `g_tflm_lock` (raced KWS). 6. The preview ran at 150 ms forever after a match. 7. The worker could stick in state 2. 8. The camera HAL hides failures: `velapaw_camera_get_frame` always returns 0 and keeps the old frame, so watch `same`, not `err`. 9. After a reset the UI booted on Enroll (pauses after 30 s). 10. Fed/skip flags were RAM-only → a reset could re-serve an eaten meal. 11. `g_last_fed` was never read → no gap between two due meals. 12. The limit-hit path left stale `fed_min`/`fed_g`.
42	
43	## Design decisions worth keeping
44	- **At-most-once feeding:** `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/fed.bin` (magic `VPF1`, via `velapaw_store_put/get`) is saved BEFORE the dispense; `FEED_GAP_MIN` 20; a slot closed by the daily limit shows "skipped"; skips restore only on the same day.
45	- **Stall monitor:** a prio+10 thread (2 KB stack) watches the UI heartbeat (2 min; 10 min while the tag is `feed`) and the recognition worker (1 min). A prio+5 note thread (6 KB) writes `STALL <kind> at <tag> <age>s | <health line>` to flash, then `up_systemreset()` (reset code 0x03); it waits at most 3 s for the note. Started right before the main loop. **Not a HW watchdog** — an interrupts-off hang isn't caught.
46	- **health.log** = `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/health.log`, rotates at 4 KB into `health.old`. Boot line `HH:MM boot rst 0xNN`; every 10 min `HH:MM up Nm tab T cap N max Nms slow N same N err N embed N hit N miss N inf S drop N`. `velapaw voice` (read-only probe) prints the live line + the boot code.
47	- **There is NO software-reset command in this build:** `reboot` → `nsh: reboot: command not found` (2026-10-18), probably because `CONFIG_BOARDCTL_RESET` is off. **Don't suggest ai_agent's `restart`**: without BOARDCTL_RESET it prints "Restarting..." and sleeps forever, which parks the agent CLI. The RESET button gives 0x01, so the 0x03 → start-on-Recognize path can only be exercised by a real stall.
48	- Reset codes (`esp32s3_reset_reasons(0)`): 0x01 power-on/brown-out/RESET button, **0x03 CORE_SW = the stall monitor's `up_systemreset()`**, 0x07/0x08 MWDT, 0x09 RTC WDT, 0x0f brown-out, 0x15/0x16 USB UART/JTAG (esptool). Any other code than 0x01/0x15/0x16, with pets enrolled, boots on Recognize.
49	- Never patch `ui_i18n.c` — stab1 reuses `S_POINT_AT_PET`, `S_NEXT_MEAL_FMT`, `S_SKIPPED`.
50	
51	## Gotchas
52	- All velapaw sources are **LF** — an in-session note that said CRLF was wrong.
53	- No LVGL heap metric (`CONFIG_LV_USE_CLIB_MALLOC=y`) and a heap walk kills the board ([[velapaw-heap-walk-kills-board]]).
54	- Thread stacks come from IMEM (~64 KB headroom before stab1's 8 KB).
55	- Pre-existing VM warnings outside the patched files — ignore: `ui_i18n.c:245` `f14` set but not used; `agent_loop.c:740` `-Wformat-truncation`.
56	- Local compile check: `cc_check.sh <a|b> <file>` = arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.4 after `source /d/openVela/vela-env.sh`, flags from `compile_commands.json`, item8/b headers (`identity.h` 564256ad, `ui_i18n.h` 778b1a32). The VM is xtensa GCC 12.2, so the VM warning gate is the real check.
57	- Still-ungated prints (feeder, TFLM, BCS lazy init, identity, boot init, camera + LVGL syslog): a jam there now ends in a stall reset + a log line instead of a silent hang.
58	- A stall reset re-enumerates USB: reopen COM8, redo `ifconfig eth0 …`, ping to prime ARP ([[velapaw-cdcncm-networking]]).
59	
60	Offered, not done: HW watchdog (`CONFIG_WATCHDOG` + automonitor), `CONFIG_BOARD_RESET_ON_ASSERT`, syslog hardening, auto-ifconfig after a reset, idle return to Recognize, a camera HAL that returns -1 / re-inits. Related: [[velapaw-agent-on-lcd]] (the open `llm_cache` fix), [[velapaw-scheduled-feeding]], [[velapaw-recognize-tuning]].

3	description: "The velapaw app Makefile (apps/examples/velapaw) — the 3 non-obvious flags it MUST have, and how to rebuild it from scratch if lost"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
