70	trace afterwards is `iters=2 tools=2` with a `set_meal_schedule` step, and
71	`[agent] Skill file read — no shortcut` in the log. **Read that trace line
72	before believing a turn worked** — `status=ok iters=1` is the failure mode.
73	
74	Deliberately did NOT "fix" this by rewriting the tool description to make the
75	model skip the read. Read-then-write is the correct behaviour (right name,
76	current times) and must not depend on the model choosing to skip a step.
77	
78	## SOLVED: the HTTP 400 invalid unicode code point was a use-after-free
79	
80	Every successful write used to end with the owner seeing `Sorry, I encountered
81	an error`, because the round *after* `set_meal_schedule` returned was rejected
82	with `[llm] API error 400: … messages[N].content: invalid unicode code point`.
83	The write was already on flash, so a working action reported failure.
84	
85	**Root cause, in `tool_meal.c`:** `cJSON_Delete(root)` ran while `const char
86	*pet` still pointed **into** that tree, and all six `switch` branches format
87	`pet` afterwards. The success string therefore carried raw freed-heap bytes at
88	the `%s`, and DeepSeek rejected the whole request. Fix is three lines — copy
89	the name into a `char petbuf[64]` and repoint `pet` at the copy **before** the
90	delete; reassigning `pet` covers all six branches without renaming anything.
91	Verified 2026-10-11 on firmware `9242daf64d1c9744f9d1ec917bf13d69`
92	(1563648 B): `result: 151 bytes`, no sanitiser warning, `status=ok iters=3
93	tools=2` in 5 s, real owner-facing reply.
94	
95	**The byte arithmetic was the signal all along.** The log said `result: 163
96	bytes`; hand-counting the format string twice gave 151. I trusted the count and
97	hunted an encoder bug instead of asking why the gap existed. `"Meal 2 for "` is
98	11 bytes and the diagnostic reported only 13 valid — corruption began exactly
99	at the `%s`, which names the variable.
100	
101	**Two theories falsified on the way — do not re-derive either.** (1) History
102	truncation: first failure at column 8230 against `hist=8192` looked conclusive;
103	`session_clear_all` reproduced it at column 4536 in a 10286-byte body.
104	(2) A stale over-read of `tool_output`: `cJSON_AddStringToObject` passes bytes
105	through verbatim and takes its own `strlen`, and `agent_tool_exec_streamed`
106	(`static inline` in `src/core/agent_mem.h:278`) is a clean malloc/execute/
107	memcpy with no appending — the message holds exactly our NUL-terminated bytes.
108	Also wrong: re-indexing `messages[N]` onto the assistant message. `msg[0]
109	role=user` proves the **system prompt is not in the messages array**.
110	
111	**Kept as defence:** `utf8_valid_prefix()` + `add_clean_string()` in
112	`agent_loop.c` now sanitise all four content sites (assistant `content` and
113	`reasoning_content`, single- and parallel-tool results), logging `[agent]
114	UTF-8: trimmed N of M byte(s) from "<key>"`. That warning is what localised
115	this bug; a malformed string no longer hard-fails a turn. The companion
116	`msg[N] role=… len=… utf8ok=…` dump (the 25-line `DIAGNOSTIC (velapaw
117	2026-10-11)` block) was **removed 2026-10-13**: `agent_loop.c` `c1c8ebf1…` →
118	`1474c400505aa4e472d7a77bf3bbe73e`, image `0e51e11b5c61786c966ebe072015f04a`
119	(1,564,608 B, fix10 + this only), gates `grep -ac "utf8ok="` = 0 and
120	`grep -ac "UTF-8: trimmed"` = 1. Flashed on COM3 and hardware-verified
121	2026-10-13: `ask change bob's dinner to 18:20` → `END status=ok iters=3
122	tools=2` in 5 s, saved to flash, and no `msg[N]` lines printed. About 10 min
123	later, `ask set bob's launch to 12` (a typo and a bare hour) set slot 2 to
124	12:00. It took the same 3 iterations, 2 tools and 5 s, after the agent
125	reconnected on its own (`Pooled connection stale, reconnecting`). Rollback:
126	the fix10 golden's `app-sources.tar.gz` has the old `agent_loop.c`.
127	
128	## Verification discipline that worked
129	
130	- `grep -ac "set_meal_schedule" nuttx/nuttx.bin` + `grep -ac "scheduled meals"`
131	  + `nm nuttx/nuttx | grep -E "velapaw_meal_set_by_name|tool_meal_set_execute"`
132	  as flash gates.
133	- `cat /data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md` **before** any LLM call proves the
134	  VelaPaw half independently of the agent.
135	- The agent's reply text is never the discriminator — only `status.md` is. The
136	  model will happily narrate a write it never performed.
137	- `cat` does not exist at the `vela>` prompt; `quit` back to `nsh>` first.
138	- There is **no direct tool-invoke command** in the agent CLI (`help` lists
139	  none), so tool verification always costs an LLM round trip.
140	- **An ask that hangs after `REQ written` is the USB network, not this
141	  tool** — the CDC-NCM TX wedge, fixed by fix10 on 2026-10-13; see
142	  [[velapaw-ncm-tx-wedge]].

38	## Why it "hung" / stopped recognizing (ranked)
39	1. **`recog_done` latch** — after one match or 2 misses, Recognize waited for a tab re-entry; looks exactly like "fails to recognize". stab1 re-arms on a tap, on a scene change (4×4 brightness signature), and once a minute while a meal is due (its first 30 min); gap 30 s after a hit, 3 s doubling to 20 s after misses.
40	2. **Console jam** — `uart_write` takes `xmit.lock` BEFORE it checks O_NONBLOCK, so one blocking writer + a host that stopped draining COM8 (PuTTY closed, PC asleep) jams every writer, UI thread included. stab1: `uprintf` (UI) and `vp_say` (store) ask FIONSPACE first (answered under a spinlock) and drop the line instead (counted as `drop`). Rejected: a pipe relay (CONFIG_PIPES off) and a dup2 mute.
41	3. Midnight: `today_total` wasn't reconciled for a board running past midnight → a day that ended at the cap refused the next day's meals. Fix: `velapaw_store_sync_day()` on the UI's day change.
42	4. Skips survived midnight. 5. BCS ran outside `g_tflm_lock` (raced KWS). 6. The preview ran at 150 ms forever after a match. 7. The worker could stick in state 2. 8. The camera HAL hides failures: `velapaw_camera_get_frame` always returns 0 and keeps the old frame, so watch `same`, not `err`. 9. After a reset the UI booted on Enroll (pauses after 30 s). 10. Fed/skip flags were RAM-only → a reset could re-serve an eaten meal. 11. `g_last_fed` was never read → no gap between two due meals. 12. The limit-hit path left stale `fed_min`/`fed_g`.
43	
44	## Design decisions worth keeping
45	- **At-most-once feeding:** `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/fed.bin` (magic `VPF1`, via `velapaw_store_put/get`) is saved BEFORE the dispense; `FEED_GAP_MIN` 20; a slot closed by the daily limit shows "skipped"; skips restore only on the same day.
46	- **Stall monitor:** a prio+10 thread (2 KB stack) watches the UI heartbeat (2 min; 10 min while the tag is `feed`) and the recognition worker (1 min). A prio+5 note thread (6 KB) writes `STALL <kind> at <tag> <age>s | <health line>` to flash, then `up_systemreset()` (reset code 0x03); it waits at most 3 s for the note. Started right before the main loop. **Not a HW watchdog** — an interrupts-off hang isn't caught.
47	- **health.log** = `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/health.log`, rotates at 4 KB into `health.old`. Boot line `HH:MM boot rst 0xNN`; every 10 min `HH:MM up Nm tab T cap N max Nms slow N same N err N embed N hit N miss N inf S drop N`. `velapaw voice` (read-only probe) prints the live line + the boot code.

The RESET button gives 0x01, so the 0x03 → start-on-Recognize path can only be exercised by a real stall.
49	- Reset codes (`esp32s3_reset_reasons(0)`): 0x01 power-on/brown-out/RESET button, **0x03 CORE_SW = the stall monitor's `up_systemreset()`**, 0x07/0x08 MWDT, 0x09 RTC WDT, 0x0f brown-out, 0x15/0x16 USB UART/JTAG (esptool). 11	**SOLVED + hardware-verified 2026-10-13 (fix10).** Symptom: an `ask` hangs
12	forever after `[vela_tls] REQ written: …`, intermittently, usually the second
13	ask in a row while the first completed fine. nsh keeps working. The signature
14	is only visible on Windows: `Ethernet 2` (UsbNcm.sys) **rx counter frozen
15	while tx keeps climbing, neighbour 192.168.137.2 stuck at `Incomplete`**,
16	never recovering without a board reboot.
17	
18	**Why:** it looked like an agent/LLM/TLS problem and the board-side log gives
19	no hint; only the host counters show the link is half-dead.
20	**How to apply:** if an ask hangs after `REQ written`, check Ethernet 2 rx vs
21	tx first. Rx frozen + tx climbing = this class. Then look for `otg: EP… abort`
22	/ `cdcncm: TX stalled` lines and confirm the fix10 md5s below are still on the
23	VM — **both files are VM-only, `repo sync` reverts them.**
24	
25	## Root cause
26	
27	`esp32s3_otg_device.c` had `#define ESP32S3_FIFO_SIZE (1280)` = 320 words, but
28	the OTG FIFO RAM is 256 words and ESP-IDF treats only 200 as usable (GDFIFOCFG
29	EPInfoBaseAddr=200). After a 158-word RX FIFO, six IN FIFOs × 27 words put EP3
30	(NCM interrupt IN) at 239..265 and **EP4 (NCM bulk IN = all board→host
31	network traffic) at 266..292, wrapping onto RX FIFO words 10..36.** Fix:
32	`ESP32S3_FIFO_SIZE (800)` → 17 words per IN FIFO (one 64-byte packet), RX 98
33	words, everything inside 0..199.
34	
35	Why one stuck IN endpoint kills RX too: EP4 never completes → cdcncm's
36	unbounded `nxsem_wait(&wrreq_idle)` blocks LPWORK (ETHWORK = LPWORK) → the OUT
37	read request is never re-armed. The console is ACM EP2 IN on a different path,
38	so nsh survives — which is what made it look like an agent bug.
39	
40	Endpoint map (`CONFIG_ESP32S3_OTG_ENDPOINT_NUM=5` → EP0..EP5): ACM = EP1 IN
41	intr, EP2 IN bulk (console), EP1 OUT; NCM = EP3 IN intr, EP4 IN bulk (TX),
42	EP2 OUT bulk (RX).
43

46	- OTG: `esp32s3_ep_cancel` left `active = true` on IN endpoints, and the ISR's
47	  EPDISD clear sat under `#if 0` while EPDM is enabled in DIEPMSK. New
48	  `esp32s3_epin_abort()`: EPDIS|SNAK, poll EPDISD, flush that TX FIFO, clear
49	  EMPMSK/DIEPINT, `active=false`, cancel requests; logs `otg: EP%d abort …`
50	  at most 3 times.
51	- cdcncm: the next NTB was formatted into the **in-flight** `wrreq->buf` (now
52	  double-buffered via `txstage`); the unbounded wait became a 2 s bounded wait
53	  + `EP_CANCEL` self-heal (`cdcncm: TX stalled, cancelled …`); added `txlock`;
54	  added `USBDEV_REQFLAGS_NULLPKT` (Windows merged an NTB whose length was a
55	  multiple of 64 with the next one); GET/SET_NTB_INPUT_SIZE were stubs (with an

18	## ✅ SOLVED 2026-10-11 — ROOT CAUSE: PSRAM RX buffer alignment (software, not hardware)
19	
20	**Forensic proof, from the Aug 2–6 `RXDUMP` logs in the session transcript**
21	(the only builds that printed the RX descriptor buffer address —
22	`VELAPAW_I2S_PROBES=1`): all **18 stalled runs** had `d[0] buf` ≡ **8 mod 16**
23	(0x3c4bdb48/…58, 0x3c510668/…88); all **13 runs that delivered audio** had it
24	≡ **0 mod 16** (0x3c4bfc40, 0x3c4c1cb0, 0x3c512ed0, 0x3c50ee40 …). No
25	exceptions. mod 32 does NOT separate them (working runs sit at both 0 and 16),
26	so the rule is exactly 16 B — the GDMA `IN_EXT_MEM_BK_SIZE` default.
27	
28	**Mechanism.** The mic node `/dev/audio/pcm_in0` is an **es8311** lower half
29	with `allocbuffer = NULL`, so `nuttx/audio/audio.c` `audio_allocbuffer()` calls
30	libc `apb_alloc()` directly. **A fix in the I2S driver's
31	`AUDIOIOC_ALLOCBUFFER` case would never run** — that path is only reached via
32	`audio_i2s.c`, which this board does not register. `apb_alloc` does
33	`lib_umemalign(MAX(up_get_dcache_linesize(), 1), n)`; without
34	`CONFIG_ARCH_DCACHE` the linesize is 0 → alignment 1 → plain malloc → 8 B.
35	`esp32s3_dma_setup()` rounds PSRAM RX *lengths* to 16 (the 4080+16 split in
36	`desc 80000ff0 80000010` is the proof the buffer is in PSRAM) but never
37	aligns the *address*. Misaligned PSRAM target → descriptor 0 never completes
38	(owner 1, length 0, no EOF, raw `000000a0`; the later probe builds showed
39	`0000000f`).
40	
41	**Why it posed as hardware.** `samp = apb + 0x98` and the record buffers are
42	allocated back-to-back with a stride that is a multiple of 16 (0x20a0), so
43	ONE coin flip on the first apb's address decides the WHOLE boot. Identical
44	addresses repeat run after run for a given build + heap history, so a layout
45	that lands on 8 fails every time. Boot-time allocations depend on /data
46	contents (pets, history, UI objects), so flashing the Aug b82 image did NOT
47	restore the Aug heap — the 2026-09-22 "known-good image fails ⇒ hardware"
48	inference below never controlled for heap layout. Fits everything: b81's
49	"3 of 5 cold boots", "bad from the FIRST capture", kicks never recovering, TX
50	unaffected, the RESET-tap stall.
51	
52	**Fix (2026-10-11, CONFIRMED on hardware — see below):** in
53	`~/openvela/nuttx/libs/libc/audio/lib_buffer.c`, `MAX(up_get_dcache_linesize(), 1)`
54	→ `MAX(…, 64)` (64 covers every ext-mem block size and keeps buffers on
55	whole 32-B cache lines). Backup `~/lib_buffer.c.pre-rxalign`. **VM-only patch
56	— `repo sync` will eat it.** libc joins the stale-object list
57	([[velapaw-stale-libarch-trap]]): `find libs/libc -name lib_buffer.o -delete;
58	rm -f libs/libc/libc.a staging/libc.a` (objects build in `libs/libc/bin/`).
59	Build gate: `xtensa-esp32s3-elf-objdump -d --disassemble=apb_alloc nuttx |
60	grep -B4 '<memalign>'` must show `a10, 64` (stale object shows `a10, 1`).

218	## 🔴 RX delivers TWO slots and one of them is dead
219	
220	`I2S_RX_MONO` marks the second slot invalid but does **not** remove it from
221	the stream — both slots reach the FIFO and the DMA, with the invalid one
222	zero-filled. Buffers read `[sample, 0, sample, 0, ...]`. This is not 32-bit
223	slot padding: `i2s_set_datawidth()` programs 16-bit slots
224	(`CHAN_BITS = HALF_SAMPLE_BITS = data_width`). It is VelaPaw patch #25:
225	`TOT_CHAN_NUM=1` (two slots) + `CHAN0_EN|CHAN1_EN` + `I2S_RX_MONO`.
226	
227	Consequence: a 16000-`int16` window was **0.5 s of audio with a zero between
228	every sample** — a mirrored spectrum landing inside micro_speech's mel bins.
229	Fix is `MIC_STRIDE 2` — keep one `int16` in two, in `mic_collect()`.
230	
231	### ⚠️ The live slot flips PER CAPTURE, not per build
232	
233	Build 52, one boot: capture 1 slot 0, capture 2 slot 0, capture 3 **slot 1**.
234	Every capture re-arms RX and the first sample lands wherever the frame is.
235	Hardcoding slot 0 makes a capture come back all zeros and look like a dead
236	mic. `mic_data_phase()` measures it, per capture, by counting **exact zeros**
237	— the dead slot is 0 to the bit while the live slot has an ADC noise floor
238	even in a silent room. It returns −1 for an all-zero buffer (RX emits a few
239	while warming up) so the phase is settled off the first buffer with content,
240	not a coin flip.
241	
242	## 🔴 Audio buffers live in PSRAM and the driver does no cache maintenance
243	
244	`apb->samp` addresses are `0x3C5x_xxxx` = the external-memory window
245	(`CONFIG_ESP32S3_SPIRAM=y`, `CONFIG_MM_REGIONS=2`). `esp32s3_i2s.c` has **no**
246	invalidate/writeback/barrier anywhere. So **reusing a buffer inside one
247	window returns a stale cached copy**: first delivery misses cache and reads
248	what DMA wrote, the copy pulls 4 KB into DCache, and ~500 ms later the same
249	buffer hits those warm lines. Signature: an 8-segment profile that repeats
250	with a period equal to the pool depth, and identical samples at the same
251	`apb` pointer.
252	
253	**Fix = never reuse a buffer inside a window.** `GETBUFFERINFO`'s `nbuffers`
254	is a *suggestion*, not a cap — `ALLOCBUFFER` is per-call. `MIC_WANT_BUFS 18`
255	(one delivery = 4092 B = 2046 `int16` = 1023 usable samples after stride, so
256	16000 needs 16 + `MIC_SKIP_BUFS`).
257	
258	### The follow-on trap: a deep pool overruns the quiesce budget
259	
260	Requeueing every accepted buffer left ~17 in flight; one buffer is 128 ms, so
261	draining needs 2.3 s against a 1 s budget sized when the pool was 4. Quiesce
262	timed out, the *next* capture armed with 6 free buffers, and they recycled 3×
263	— reintroducing the cache bug. Two fixes together:
264	- requeue only when `skipped + seq >= nrecbufs - 1` (self-adjusting: a capped
265	  pool still finishes by falling back to recycling)
266	- `MIC_QUIESCE_TRIES 80` (4 s) — a ceiling, not a cost

580	   always supplied that long before the dialog opened. b85 restores it with a
581	   boot warm-up (unarmed captures, result discarded).
582	2. **Unlimited retries.** b85 fed those warm-up failures into the shared
583	   `g_voice_consec`, and `VOICE_MAX_CAPFAIL 3` latches `g_voice_fail` and
584	   `return NULL` — **the worker thread exits and voice is dead for the boot.**
585	   b85 therefore burned the whole budget at boot and was *worse* than b83.
586	   **b86 gives the warm-up its own counter** (`g_voice_warmfail`) that never
587	   touches `g_voice_consec`, retrying forever with backoff (200 ms ×5, 2 s ×10,
588	   then 10 s). Armed/dialog captures keep the old budget.
589	
590	### What b86 proved: retrying within a boot CANNOT recover
591	
592	19 warm-up captures over 217 s, every one `-110`, hardware state **bit-identical
593	each time** and identical to b78/b79/b80:
594	
595	    rec 0/342  play 19/19      342 RX buffers in, none back; TX 19/19 fine
596	    desc 80000ff0              owner 1, length 0
597	    intraw 000000a0            INFIFO_FULL_WM + INFIFO_UDF_L1, RE-RAISED after
598	                               every kick's INT_CLR -> live starvation
599	    intena 00000002            IN_SUC_EOF enabled, never fires
600	    mickick 19 ok 0  resc 19  start 20
601	
602	TX completing 19/19 through the same GDMA proves the clock runs and the block's
603	EOF path works — **it is specifically the RX channel that never fills.**
604	
605	⚠️ **Two of my own readings here were WRONG — don't repeat them.**
606	`velapaw_i2s_rx_kick()` **does** drain `rx.act` (`while (!sq_empty(&rx.act))
607	sq_addfirst(sq_remlast(...), &rx.pend)`) and then `i2s_rxdma_start()` re-arms
608	one immediately — so `act 1 pend 1` after a kick is the kick **working**, not
609	failing. And **nothing in the UI ever closed the session in b83 either**:
610	`velapaw_mic_shutdown()` is called only from `velapaw_main.c`'s
611	`velapaw kws mic` CLI path, never from `ui_lvgl.c`.
612	
613	### The live hypothesis (b87): the FIRST capture decides, and b84 moved it
614	
615	`velapaw_mic_preopen()` opens one session at boot and **nothing ever closes
616	it**, so once that stream wedges every later capture inherits it — the kick
617	resets GDMA + I2S RX but never the ES8311.
618	
619	    b83 and earlier   first capture when the owner tapped Recognize, tens of
620	                      seconds in, board settled            -> 6 good boots
621	    b85 / b86         first capture at ~13.1 s -- mid TFLM model reads, camera
622	                      bring-up, the 5350 ms pre-open       -> 0 good boots
623	
624	**b87 holds unarmed captures until `VOICE_WARMUP_AT_MS` (30 s) after power-on**,
625	tested against `mono_ms()` (monotonic from boot). Armed captures are *not*
626	delayed. Falsifiable: the vlog shows either nothing (warm-up succeeded) or
627	`warmup FAILED -110 (#1)` at ~33 s — and if it fails at 33 s exactly as at 16 s,
628	**timing is not the variable** and the next move is rebuilding the session
629	(close both fds, re-open, which is the only thing that re-runs ES8311
630	configure). b80 removed that path because `mic_session_close()` hung, but that
631	predates b79's fix of the collect hang.
632	
633	Build chain, all esptool hash-verified on-chip:
634	`b83 288649a9` → `b84 a0860dee` → `b85 ec7c1d4d` → `b86 1666c029` →
635	`b87 95a383ed`. Console fix: [[velapaw-console-blocking]].
636	
637	## ✅ SOLVED: the `es8311 -22` boot spam is cosmetic — never chase it
638	
639	    es8311_getcoeff: MCLK = 4096000 and samplerate = 48000 not supported
640	    es8311_setsamplerate: Failed to set sample rate: -22
641	
642	The driver does it to itself. `es8311.c:2153` sets
643	`priv->samprate = ES8311_DEFAULT_SAMPRATE` (48000), then `:2191` calls
644	`es8311_setsamplerate()` during init while MCLK is 4096000 (= 256 × 16000).
645	`getcoeff(4096000, 48000)` has no table entry → `-22`. The real rate is
646	programmed later from `caps->ac_controls.hw[0]`, and `:1039` already calls
647	`es8311_reset()` *before* `:1046`'s `setsamplerate()`. **It appears in working
648	boots too**, so its presence in a failing log means nothing. This misled a
649	third-party analysis into proposing an ES8311 power-up clock race; that was
650	rejected on evidence.
651	
652	## Session shape
653	
654	Open, configure, `AUDIOIOC_START` **once**; each capture only enqueues and
655	collects. Between captures the session is running but idle. Free-running RX is
656	not an option: `mq_maxmsg = nbuffers + 8`, so with no reader the driver's
657	`mq_send` would drop buffer pointers. `mic_flush_mq()` before each re-arm.
658	
659	⚠️ **`apb->nbytes` is read by the driver *during* the enqueue ioctl** — the
660	caller sets it: record side `0`, playback side `nmaxbytes`. Zeroing it in a
661	shared helper silently sends a zero-length TX buffer → no clock → hang. TX
662	must stay primed; RX borrows BCLK/WS from TX (see [[velapaw-audio-bringup]]).
663	
664	⚠️ Do not conflate this with the falsified theory above. A **zero-length first**
665	TX buffer means `I2S_TX_START` is never set, so the clock never starts — real.
666	TX **draining after** a good buffer is harmless, because `TX_START` stays set
667	and `#16` cleared `TX_STOP_EN`.
668	
669	## Measurement, not ears
670	
671	`velapaw_mic_stats()` prints `peak N@index`, `rms`, `dc`, `rail` and an
672	8-segment peak profile. Reference at 30 dB, build 52, de-interleaved:
673	
674	    silence  rms  26  profile    87    82    87    68    55    67    56    60
675	    "yes"    rms 645  profile   447    90   107   100  4085  5019  1426  1724
676	    "no"     rms 791  profile  1949  5402  3534   596    74    66    87    94
677	
678	`MIC_TRACE` (default 0) prints one line per buffer with the `apb` pointer and
679	four samples — the check on both fixes at once: pointers must all be distinct,
680	`s` must alternate live/0. Turn it on for any future capture regression.
681	Do **not** read a full-scale spike at a fixed index as clipping — that is the
682	start-of-stream transient, see [[velapaw-audio-gain]].

11	**SHIPPED + HARDWARE-VERIFIED 2026-10-11.** `ask set bob's first meal to 7:30`
12	and `ask set bob's dinner to 19:15` both landed, and `status.md` read back
13	`- scheduled meals: 07:30 12:30 19:15` — two separate agent turns, both
14	persisted to flash. Four agent-driven writes have now landed in total
15	(07:30 / 13:00 / 19:15 / 18:45). Firmware `9242daf64d1c9744f9d1ec917bf13d69`
16	(1563648 B) is the complete one; `3ad206ae3c0992c6da8ebacec20d0bf3`
17	(1563536 B) is the earlier build that wrote correctly but reported an error.
18	This is the path that replaces on-device voice for meal scheduling, which is
19	hardware-blocked (see [[velapaw-mic-capture]]).
20	
21	## The three pieces
22	
23	1. **`velapaw_meal_set_by_name(name, slot, minute)`** in
24	   `apps/examples/velapaw/identity/identity.c`. Pet ids are array indices that
25	   renumber on delete (`identity.h:52`), so a **name is the only stable handle**
26	   an agent or dialog can hold. It normalises both sides — lower-case, strip
27	   leading whitespace, trim trailing non-alphanumerics — because the enrolled
28	   pet on this board is literally `bob,` with a comma from the on-screen
29	   keyboard. The model sent `"pet": "bob"` and it matched; the normaliser
30	   earned its place on the first real call. Returns 0 / -1 bad args / -2 no
31	   such pet / -3 ambiguous / -4 rejected, else the save rc. It **copies all
32	   three slots** before writing one, because `velapaw_identity_update()` writes
33	   every slot it is handed; passing 0 for portion/limit means "leave alone".
34	2. **`vp_status_write()` publishes the meal times** as
35	   `- scheduled meals: HH:MM HH:MM HH:MM` (or `off`). This is why there is
36	   **no `get_meal_schedule` tool** — the agent already reaches `status.md`
37	   through `read_file`, so reading costs zero schema budget. That budget was
38	   hard-won (36→16 tools; see
39	   [[velapaw-ai-agent-integration-progress]]), and the write tool took it to 17
40	   builtin / Tools JSON 5245 B, still comfortable.
41	   **2026-10-13 (fix9): `status.md` is now also rewritten after every agent,
42	   Edit or voice-dialog change and pet delete.** Before, it refreshed only at
43	   boot and after a feed, so the agent read back times it had just changed —
44	   see [[velapaw-agent-on-lcd]].
45	3. **`set_meal_schedule`** in `packages/ai_agent/src/tools/tool_meal.c`.
46	   Declares `velapaw_meal_set_by_name` by hand with `extern` rather than
47	   including `identity.h` — same FLAT image so it links, and the header would
48	   drag in the app's whole include path. Accepts `pet`/`pet_name`/`name`,
49	   `slot`/`meal`, and either `"HH:MM"` or separate `hour`/`minute`. Its success
50	   string **states the Model-B gate explicitly** ("dispenses it only when %s is
51	   recognised at the bowl at or after that time"), or the model promises the
52	   owner food appears on the clock alone, which is false.
53	
54	## THE TRAP: `Local tool shortcut: skip LLM round`
55	
56	`agent_loop.c` ~1230 short-circuits the turn when a round has exactly one
57	"local" tool call: it hands the raw tool output to the user as the final reply
58	and never does another LLM round. **That structurally kills every two-step
59	plan.** First run of the new tool: the model correctly called `read_file` on
60	`status.md` to find the pet name, the shortcut fired, the owner got a raw
61	status dump, and the meal was never set — `iters=1 tools=1`, `status=ok`. It
62	looks like a successful turn.
63	
64	The fix was already half-written in the file: an `is_instruction_read` escape
65	hatch exists for exactly this reason (skill files, `AGENT_HEARTBEAT_FILE`), and
66	`list_dir` had already been pulled out of the local set for the same bug with
67	the same symptom. Added `strstr(path, "/velapaw/")` to that condition —
68	everything in `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/` (`status.md`, `feed_log.md`,
69	`history.bin`) is **data to reason over, never a finished answer**. Correct
70	trace afterwards is `iters=2 tools=2` with a `set_meal_schedule` step, and
71	`[agent] Skill file read — no shortcut` in the log. **Read that trace line
72	before believing a turn worked** — `status=ok iters=1` is the failure mode.
73	
74	Deliberately did NOT "fix" this by rewriting the tool description to make the
75	model skip the read. Read-then-write is the correct behaviour (right name,
76	current times) and must not depend on the model choosing to skip a step.
77	
78	## SOLVED: the HTTP 400 invalid unicode code point was a use-after-free
79	
80	Every successful write used to end with the owner seeing `Sorry, I encountered
81	an error`, because the round *after* `set_meal_schedule` returned was rejected
82	with `[llm] API error 400: … messages[N].content: invalid unicode code point`.
83	The write was already on flash, so a working action reported failure.
84	
85	**Root cause, in `tool_meal.c`:** `cJSON_Delete(root)` ran while `const char
86	*pet` still pointed **into** that tree, and all six `switch` branches format
87	`pet` afterwards. The success string therefore carried raw freed-heap bytes at
88	the `%s`, and DeepSeek rejected the whole request. Fix is three lines — copy
89	the name into a `char petbuf[64]` and repoint `pet` at the copy **before** the
90	delete; reassigning `pet` covers all six branches without renaming anything.
91	Verified 2026-10-11 on firmware `9242daf64d1c9744f9d1ec917bf13d69`
92	(1563648 B): `result: 151 bytes`, no sanitiser warning, `status=ok iters=3
93	tools=2` in 5 s, real owner-facing reply.
94	
95	**The byte arithmetic was the signal all along.** The log said `result: 163
96	bytes`; hand-counting the format string twice gave 151. I trusted the count and
97	hunted an encoder bug instead of asking why the gap existed. `"Meal 2 for "` is
98	11 bytes and the diagnostic reported only 13 valid — corruption began exactly
99	at the `%s`, which names the variable.
100	
101	**Two theories falsified on the way — do not re-derive either.** (1) History
102	truncation: first failure at column 8230 against `hist=8192` looked conclusive;
103	`session_clear_all` reproduced it at column 4536 in a 10286-byte body.
104	(2) A stale over-read of `tool_output`: `cJSON_AddStringToObject` passes bytes
105	through verbatim and takes its own `strlen`, and `agent_tool_exec_streamed`
106	(`static inline` in `src/core/agent_mem.h:278`) is a clean malloc/execute/
107	memcpy with no appending — the message holds exactly our NUL-terminated bytes.
108	Also wrong: re-indexing `messages[N]` onto the assistant message. `msg[0]
109	role=user` proves the **system prompt is not in the messages array**.
110	
111	**Kept as defence:** `utf8_valid_prefix()` + `add_clean_string()` in
112	`agent_loop.c` now sanitise all four content sites (assistant `content` and
113	`reasoning_content`, single- and parallel-tool results), logging `[agent]
114	UTF-8: trimmed N of M byte(s) from "<key>"`. That warning is what localised
115	this bug; a malformed string no longer hard-fails a turn. The companion
116	`msg[N] role=… len=… utf8ok=…` dump (the 25-line `DIAGNOSTIC (velapaw
117	2026-10-11)` block) was **removed 2026-10-13**: `agent_loop.c` `c1c8ebf1…` →
118	`1474c400505aa4e472d7a77bf3bbe73e`, image `0e51e11b5c61786c966ebe072015f04a`
119	(1,564,608 B, fix10 + this only), gates `grep -ac "utf8ok="` = 0 and
120	`grep -ac "UTF-8: trimmed"` = 1. Flashed on COM3 and hardware-verified
121	2026-10-13: `ask change bob's dinner to 18:20` → `END status=ok iters=3
122	tools=2` in 5 s, saved to flash, and no `msg[N]` lines printed. About 10 min
123	later, `ask set bob's launch to 12` (a typo and a bare hour) set slot 2 to
124	12:00. It took the same 3 iterations, 2 tools and 5 s, after the agent
125	reconnected on its own (`Pooled connection stale, reconnecting`). Rollback:
126	the fix10 golden's `app-sources.tar.gz` has the old `agent_loop.c`.
127	
128	## Verification discipline that worked
129	
130	- `grep -ac "set_meal_schedule" nuttx/nuttx.bin` + `grep -ac "scheduled meals"`
131	  + `nm nuttx/nuttx | grep -E "velapaw_meal_set_by_name|tool_meal_set_execute"`
132	  as flash gates.
133	- `cat /data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md` **before** any LLM call proves the
134	  VelaPaw half independently of the agent.
135	- The agent's reply text is never the discriminator — only `status.md` is. The
136	  model will happily narrate a write it never performed.
137	- `cat` does not exist at the `vela>` prompt; `quit` back to `nsh>` first.
138	- There is **no direct tool-invoke command** in the agent CLI (`help` lists
139	  none), so tool verification always costs an LLM round trip.
140	- **An ask that hangs after `REQ written` is the USB network, not this
141	  tool** — the CDC-NCM TX wedge, fixed by fix10 on 2026-10-13; see
142	  [[velapaw-ncm-tx-wedge]].

20	## What is on the screen (item-8 patch, 6 files)
21	
22	Rollback copy: `~/velapaw-golden/pre-item8-agent-lcd/`.
23	
24	- **Toast under the bell for every `ask`:** "You: <question>" → "Agent
25	  working… N s" counting up → the reply. It stays 30 s; a tap dismisses it.
26	- **Heartbeat:** an all-clear is a green toast for 10 s. A warning is a red
27	  toast that stays, turns the bell red and is listed in the bell panel until
28	  the next all-clear. A *failed* heartbeat shows nothing, so a dead network at
29	  the offline defense doesn't clutter the screen.
30	- **Live My Pets:** an identity generation counter makes the card redraw on
31	  whatever tab is showing. An open Edit dialog picks up the change too, so
32	  pressing Save can't write the old time back. Before this, My Pets only
33	  redrew when you entered the tab.

37	## fix9 — why "the toast works but the times don't change"
38	
39	6 files: `store.h`, `store_stub.c`, `identity.c`, `ui_lvgl.c`,
40	`tool_registry.c`, `nsh_commands.c`. Rollback:
41	`~/velapaw-golden/pre-fix9-status-refresh/`. Image
42	`148bf5d5eff85947a89e00eaafd538c3`.
43	
44	- `status.md` is the agent's only source of meal times, and it was rewritten
45	  only at boot and after a feed — one turn after moving breakfast, the agent
46	  read the old time back. It is now also rewritten after an agent change, an
47	  Edit or voice-dialog save, and a pet delete.
48	- The model answered "Done" without calling `set_meal_schedule`. The tool
49	  description now says a meal changes only when the tool succeeds.
50	- `ask` text carried raw backspace/arrow-key bytes from the terminal; they are
51	  now applied or dropped before the message is sent.
52	- **Still open, not in fix9. SEEN ON HARDWARE 2026-10-13:** sending
53	  `ask change bob's dinner to 18:20` twice in a row gave `Cache hit, skipping
54	  LLM call` and `END status=ok iters=1 tools=0 … elapsed=0s`. It replayed
55	  "Done — … 18:20" without calling `set_meal_schedule`. That time it was
56	  harmless, since the meal already was 18:20. After an Edit-dialog change it
57	  would be a false "Done".
58	- **How the cache works** (`src/llm/llm_cache.c` and `include/llm/llm_cache.h`;
59	  values read from the D: checkout, which is upstream code we never modified):
60	  - It is RAM-only, with 8 slots.
61	  - Entries expire after 300 s, but **every hit re-stores the entry and
62	    restarts the 300 s**.
63	  - The key is a djb2 hash of the prompt's first 64 characters, with no string
64	    compare. Long asks that differ only after character 64 therefore collide.
65	  - The store is at `agent_loop.c` `send_reply:` (~line 1451). It is gated
66	    only on `LLM_COMPLEXITY_SIMPLE` and the non-heartbeat `cacheable` flag.
67	- **Fix** = add `&& trace.total_tool_calls == 0` to that store condition. That
68	  counter is what the END line prints as `tools=`. Not applied yet. Until then,
69	  use a fresh sentence, wait 5 minutes, or restart `ai_agent`.

38	## Why it "hung" / stopped recognizing (ranked)
39	1. **`recog_done` latch** — after one match or 2 misses, Recognize waited for a tab re-entry; looks exactly like "fails to recognize". stab1 re-arms on a tap, on a scene change (4×4 brightness signature), and once a minute while a meal is due (its first 30 min); gap 30 s after a hit, 3 s doubling to 20 s after misses.
40	2. **Console jam** — `uart_write` takes `xmit.lock` BEFORE it checks O_NONBLOCK, so one blocking writer + a host that stopped draining COM8 (PuTTY closed, PC asleep) jams every writer, UI thread included. stab1: `uprintf` (UI) and `vp_say` (store) ask FIONSPACE first (answered under a spinlock) and drop the line instead (counted as `drop`). Rejected: a pipe relay (CONFIG_PIPES off) and a dup2 mute.
41	3. Midnight: `today_total` wasn't reconciled for a board running past midnight → a day that ended at the cap refused the next day's meals. Fix: `velapaw_store_sync_day()` on the UI's day change.
42	4. Skips survived midnight. 5. BCS ran outside `g_tflm_lock` (raced KWS). 6. The preview ran at 150 ms forever after a match. 7. The worker could stick in state 2. 8. The camera HAL hides failures: `velapaw_camera_get_frame` always returns 0 and keeps the old frame, so watch `same`, not `err`. 9. After a reset the UI booted on Enroll (pauses after 30 s). 10. Fed/skip flags were RAM-only → a reset could re-serve an eaten meal. 11. `g_last_fed` was never read → no gap between two due meals. 12. The limit-hit path left stale `fed_min`/`fed_g`.

44	## Design decisions worth keeping
45	- **At-most-once feeding:** `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/fed.bin` (magic `VPF1`, via `velapaw_store_put/get`) is saved BEFORE the dispense; `FEED_GAP_MIN` 20; a slot closed by the daily limit shows "skipped"; skips restore only on the same day.
46	- **Stall monitor:** a prio+10 thread (2 KB stack) watches the UI heartbeat (2 min; 10 min while the tag is `feed`) and the recognition worker (1 min). A prio+5 note thread (6 KB) writes `STALL <kind> at <tag> <age>s | <health line>` to flash, then `up_systemreset()` (reset code 0x03); it waits at most 3 s for the note. Started right before the main loop. **Not a HW watchdog** — an interrupts-off hang isn't caught.
47	- **health.log** = `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/health.log`, rotates at 4 KB into `health.old`. Boot line `HH:MM boot rst 0xNN`; every 10 min `HH:MM up Nm tab T cap N max Nms slow N same N err N embed N hit N miss N inf S drop N`. `velapaw voice` (read-only probe) prints the live line + the boot code.
48	- **There is NO software-reset command in this build:** `reboot` → `nsh: reboot: command not found` (2026-10-18), probably because `CONFIG_BOARDCTL_RESET` is off. **Don't suggest ai_agent's `restart`**: without BOARDCTL_RESET it prints "Restarting..." and sleeps forever, which parks the agent CLI. The RESET button gives 0x01, so the 0x03 → start-on-Recognize path can only be exercised by a real stall.
49	- Reset codes (`esp32s3_reset_reasons(0)`): 0x01 power-on/brown-out/RESET button, **0x03 CORE_SW = the stall monitor's `up_systemreset()`**, 0x07/0x08 MWDT, 0x09 RTC WDT, 0x0f brown-out, 0x15/0x16 USB UART/JTAG (esptool). Any other code than 0x01/0x15/0x16, with pets enrolled, boots on Recognize.
50	- Never patch `ui_i18n.c` — stab1 reuses `S_POINT_AT_PET`, `S_NEXT_MEAL_FMT`, `S_SKIPPED`.

11	**SOLVED + hardware-verified 2026-10-13 (fix10).** Symptom: an `ask` hangs
12	forever after `[vela_tls] REQ written: …`, intermittently, usually the second
13	ask in a row while the first completed fine. nsh keeps working. The signature
14	is only visible on Windows: `Ethernet 2` (UsbNcm.sys) **rx counter frozen
15	while tx keeps climbing, neighbour 192.168.137.2 stuck at `Incomplete`**,
16	never recovering without a board reboot.
17	
18	**Why:** it looked like an agent/LLM/TLS problem and the board-side log gives
19	no hint; only the host counters show the link is half-dead.
20	**How to apply:** if an ask hangs after `REQ written`, check Ethernet 2 rx vs
21	tx first. Rx frozen + tx climbing = this class. Then look for `otg: EP… abort`
22	/ `cdcncm: TX stalled` lines and confirm the fix10 md5s below are still on the
23	VM — **both files are VM-only, `repo sync` reverts them.**
24	
25	## Root cause
26	
27	`esp32s3_otg_device.c` had `#define ESP32S3_FIFO_SIZE (1280)` = 320 words, but
28	the OTG FIFO RAM is 256 words and ESP-IDF treats only 200 as usable (GDFIFOCFG
29	EPInfoBaseAddr=200). After a 158-word RX FIFO, six IN FIFOs × 27 words put EP3
30	(NCM interrupt IN) at 239..265 and **EP4 (NCM bulk IN = all board→host
31	network traffic) at 266..292, wrapping onto RX FIFO words 10..36.** Fix:
32	`ESP32S3_FIFO_SIZE (800)` → 17 words per IN FIFO (one 64-byte packet), RX 98
33	words, everything inside 0..199.
34	
35	Why one stuck IN endpoint kills RX too: EP4 never completes → cdcncm's
36	unbounded `nxsem_wait(&wrreq_idle)` blocks LPWORK (ETHWORK = LPWORK) → the OUT
37	read request is never re-armed. The console is ACM EP2 IN on a different path,
38	so nsh survives — which is what made it look like an agent bug.
39	
40	Endpoint map (`CONFIG_ESP32S3_OTG_ENDPOINT_NUM=5` → EP0..EP5): ACM = EP1 IN
41	intr, EP2 IN bulk (console), EP1 OUT; NCM = EP3 IN intr, EP4 IN bulk (TX),
42	EP2 OUT bulk (RX).
43	
44	## Also fixed in fix10
45	
46	- OTG: `esp32s3_ep_cancel` left `active = true` on IN endpoints, and the ISR's
47	  EPDISD clear sat under `#if 0` while EPDM is enabled in DIEPMSK. New
48	  `esp32s3_epin_abort()`: EPDIS|SNAK, poll EPDISD, flush that TX FIFO, clear
49	  EMPMSK/DIEPINT, `active=false`, cancel requests; logs `otg: EP%d abort …`
50	  at most 3 times.
51	- cdcncm: the next NTB was formatted into the **in-flight** `wrreq->buf` (now
52	  double-buffered via `txstage`); the unbounded wait became a 2 s bounded wait
53	  + `EP_CANCEL` self-heal (`cdcncm: TX stalled, cancelled …`); added `txlock`;
54	  added `USBDEV_REQFLAGS_NULLPKT` (Windows merged an NTB whose length was a
55	  multiple of 64 with the next one); GET/SET_NTB_INPUT_SIZE were stubs (with an
56	  unaligned `*(FAR int *)dataout`); submit return codes are now checked.
57	- New syslog lines are rate-limited, never in an ISR or a critical section —
58	  syslog can block on the console ([[velapaw-console-blocking]]).

18	## ✅ SOLVED 2026-10-11 — ROOT CAUSE: PSRAM RX buffer alignment (software, not hardware)
19	
20	**Forensic proof, from the Aug 2–6 `RXDUMP` logs in the session transcript**
21	(the only builds that printed the RX descriptor buffer address —
22	`VELAPAW_I2S_PROBES=1`): all **18 stalled runs** had `d[0] buf` ≡ **8 mod 16**
23	(0x3c4bdb48/…58, 0x3c510668/…88); all **13 runs that delivered audio** had it
24	≡ **0 mod 16** (0x3c4bfc40, 0x3c4c1cb0, 0x3c512ed0, 0x3c50ee40 …). No
25	exceptions. mod 32 does NOT separate them (working runs sit at both 0 and 16),
26	so the rule is exactly 16 B — the GDMA `IN_EXT_MEM_BK_SIZE` default.
27	
28	**Mechanism.** The mic node `/dev/audio/pcm_in0` is an **es8311** lower half
29	with `allocbuffer = NULL`, so `nuttx/audio/audio.c` `audio_allocbuffer()` calls
30	libc `apb_alloc()` directly. **A fix in the I2S driver's
31	`AUDIOIOC_ALLOCBUFFER` case would never run** — that path is only reached via
32	`audio_i2s.c`, which this board does not register. `apb_alloc` does
33	`lib_umemalign(MAX(up_get_dcache_linesize(), 1), n)`; without
34	`CONFIG_ARCH_DCACHE` the linesize is 0 → alignment 1 → plain malloc → 8 B.

218	## 🔴 RX delivers TWO slots and one of them is dead
219	
220	`I2S_RX_MONO` marks the second slot invalid but does **not** remove it from
221	the stream — both slots reach the FIFO and the DMA, with the invalid one
222	zero-filled. Buffers read `[sample, 0, sample, 0, ...]`. This is not 32-bit
223	slot padding: `i2s_set_datawidth()` programs 16-bit slots
224	(`CHAN_BITS = HALF_SAMPLE_BITS = data_width`). It is VelaPaw patch #25:
225	`TOT_CHAN_NUM=1` (two slots) + `CHAN0_EN|CHAN1_EN` + `I2S_RX_MONO`.
226	
227	Consequence: a 16000-`int16` window was **0.5 s of audio with a zero between
228	every sample** — a mirrored spectrum landing inside micro_speech's mel bins.
229	Fix is `MIC_STRIDE 2` — keep one `int16` in two, in `mic_collect()`.
230	
231	### ⚠️ The live slot flips PER CAPTURE, not per build
232	
233	Build 52, one boot: capture 1 slot 0, capture 2 slot 0, capture 3 **slot 1**.
234	Every capture re-arms RX and the first sample lands wherever the frame is.
235	Hardcoding slot 0 makes a capture come back all zeros and look like a dead
236	mic. `mic_data_phase()` measures it, per capture, by counting **exact zeros**
237	— the dead slot is 0 to the bit while the live slot has an ADC noise floor
238	even in a silent room. It returns −1 for an all-zero buffer (RX emits a few
239	while warming up) so the phase is settled off the first buffer with content,
240	not a coin flip.
241	
242	## 🔴 Audio buffers live in PSRAM and the driver does no cache maintenance
243	
244	`apb->samp` addresses are `0x3C5x_xxxx` = the external-memory window
245	(`CONFIG_ESP32S3_SPIRAM=y`, `CONFIG_MM_REGIONS=2`). `esp32s3_i2s.c` has **no**
246	invalidate/writeback/barrier anywhere. So **reusing a buffer inside one
247	window returns a stale cached copy**: first delivery misses cache and reads
248	what DMA wrote, the copy pulls 4 KB into DCache, and ~500 ms later the same
249	buffer hits those warm lines. Signature: an 8-segment profile that repeats
250	with a period equal to the pool depth, and identical samples at the same
251	`apb` pointer.
252	
253	**Fix = never reuse a buffer inside a window.** `GETBUFFERINFO`'s `nbuffers`
254	is a *suggestion*, not a cap — `ALLOCBUFFER` is per-call. `MIC_WANT_BUFS 18`
255	(one delivery = 4092 B = 2046 `int16` = 1023 usable samples after stride, so
256	16000 needs 16 + `MIC_SKIP_BUFS`).
257	
258	### The follow-on trap: a deep pool overruns the quiesce budget
259	
260	Requeueing every accepted buffer left ~17 in flight; one buffer is 128 ms, so
261	draining needs 2.3 s against a 1 s budget sized when the pool was 4. Quiesce
262	timed out, the *next* capture armed with 6 free buffers, and they recycled 3×
263	— reintroducing the cache bug. Two fixes together:
264	- requeue only when `skipped + seq >= nrecbufs - 1` (self-adjusting: a capped
265	  pool still finishes by falling back to recycling)
266	- `MIC_QUIESCE_TRIES 80` (4 s) — a ceiling, not a cost

407	capfail 1 consec 1`. The dialog gives up at **8000 ms** (`mic never became
408	ready in 8000ms`) while the capture takes **~13 s** to fail — so the capture
409	returns ~5 s after the dialog window has already closed, and the worker's retry
410	has no armed dialog to serve. Any future retry work must fix that timing first;
411	the retry code itself is present and correct.
412	
413	## 🔴 THE TWO TIMEOUTS WERE THE SAME NUMBER (b81 fixes this)
414	
415	Independent of the DMA stall, and it bit the path that **works**:
416	
417	    ui_lvgl.c:613    VOICE_CAPTURE_MS   8000   given to velapaw_mic_capture()
418	    ui_lvgl.c:2735   VSCHED_MIC_WAIT_MS 8000   dialog's patience for ready
419	
420	The dialog gave the capture exactly as long as the capture gave itself — while
421	the capture's clock started *later*, after `mic_session_open()`. The dialog can
422	therefore **never** outlast a failing capture. Structural, not a tuning miss.
423	
424	**Session open measures 5350 ms** on this board (b80: dialog start 47220, gave
425	up 55250 = +8030, capture returned 60570 = +13350; 13350 − 8000 = 5350).
426	
427	So a **good** boot had `5350 + 2000 = 7350` against an 8000 ms deadline —
428	**650 ms of margin** — and `vsched_tick()` only prompts the user *after* the
429	first capture proves the mic open. Any jitter printed "mic never became ready"
430	**while the microphone was working perfectly.** Some fraction of failures
431	blamed on the DMA stall were probably this; from outside they look identical.
432	
433	### ✅ b81 CONFIRMED ON HARDWARE (2026-08-07) — full dialog, `COMMIT meal 1 = 09:00`
434	
435	    caps 19  lastret 16000   preopen 0  capms 3500  dialogms 8000
436	    mic stage 33 (done)  lasterr 0
437	    i2s eof 364 match 364 miss 0 empty 0   isr 364 noeof 0   act 0 pend 0
438	    i2s desc 00000000 ...   intraw 00000000
439	    i2s cfgskip 0 chst 11 resc 0 kick 0    capfail 0 consec 0
440	
441	**The cleanest I2S state ever recorded on this board** — 364/364 EOFs, no
442	stranded descriptor, `intraw` clean instead of the standing `000000a0`, and
443	`resc 0` despite `chst 11` (b79/b80 read `resc 1`).
444	
445	**b81 IS THE SHIPPING VOICE BUILD (decided 2026-08-07): 3 of 5 cold boots
446	work.** Snapshot `D:\openVela\velapaw-snapshots\2026-08-07-b81-preopen\`
447	(image + sources + patch scripts + b80 rollback + `SHA256SUMS.txt` +
448	`RESTORE.md`). Image `nuttx-b81-preopen.bin`, 1,061,880 B, sha `38cdf71a…`.
449	
450	Demo protocol, since a bad boot is bad from its FIRST capture: cold cycle, open
451	My Pets → Edit, say one word, confirm it is heard; if it times out, power cycle
452	and repeat. Two tries ≈ 84 %, three ≈ 94 %. Never `velapaw kws mic` first.
453	
454	🔴 **The timing fix is PROVEN, the stall is NOT.** Proof for the timing half:
455	every capture returns in **1230 ms**, and the dialog made **ten** captures
456	inside the same 8000 ms window that previously fit exactly one. That is the
457	margin change doing precisely what it was designed to do. 1230 ms against the
458	new 3500 ms timeout is 2.8× margin, so the shortening is empirically safe.
459	But the stall simply **did not occur** this boot — it was always intermittent,
460	and one passing boot proves nothing about it. Needs repeat cold cycles.
461	
462	b81 fixes it in the only order that works:
463	1. **`velapaw_mic_preopen()`** — worker opens the session at init, moving the
464	   5350 ms to boot. Margin 650 ms → ~6 s. Must be called **by the capturing
465	   thread** (session is owned by pid; mismatch = the `-110` reopen path).
466	   Non-fatal: on failure the first capture opens inline exactly as before.
467	2. **`VOICE_CAPTURE_MS` 8000 → 3500** — two attempts now fit in the dialog's
468	   window (3500 + 200 + 3500 = 7200), finally making b79's retry reachable.
469	   Doing (2) without (1) is pointless — retries fire into a half-eaten window.
470	
471	🔴 **The `g_mic_fresh` double-enqueue guard is load-bearing.**
472	`mic_session_open()` returns with 19 buffers **already armed and in flight** —
473	which is why the inline-open path goes straight to collect while the
474	already-open path does flush + arm. A pre-opened session would take the second
475	branch and enqueue on top of buffers the driver still holds. `g_mic_fresh`
476	marks "opened, never captured from" so the first capture skips the re-arm.
477	
478	⚠️ Name trap: `velapaw_mic_open` is a **substring of the existing**
479	`struct velapaw_mic_open_s` and `velapaw_mic_open_log`, so a `grep`-style
480	"already applied?" guard false-positives on it. The function is
481	`velapaw_mic_preopen()`.
482	
483	⚠️ `mic_status()` tag literals (`"rec enq"`, `"rec start"`, `"rec fresh"`…) are
484	**optimized out of the image** — they read 0 under `grep -a` in b80 *and* b81.
485	Do not use them as build-verification markers; use a `printf` string instead.
486	
487	## 🔴 SIX MECHANISMS FALSIFIED — do not rebuild any of them
488	
489	All with hardware counters, builds b70–b80. RX arms and its DMA never signals
490	EOF; nothing reachable from software changes that.
491	
492	1. **Dead TX ⇒ dead clock / TX requeue (b71).** `TX_STOP_EN` clear, `TX_START`
493	   set, `SIG_LOOPBACK` set, TX is master. Falsified at the register level.
494	2. **Descriptor-walk desync (patch #31's missing `else`).** `miss 0` on every
495	   run, every build. #31 is a defensible latent-bug fix but **not this bug** —
496	   kept as `patch31-i2s-rx-eof-walk.NOT-APPLIED.py` in the b68 snapshot.
497	3. **Redundant reconfigures (patch #35 half 1).** b78 measured `cfgskip 20
498	   chst 1 resc 0` — every redundant reconfigure declined, zero restarts — and
499	   the stall was unchanged. Reverted by #36.
500	4. **RX/FIFO/GDMA reset as recovery (patch #36's `velapaw_i2s_rx_kick()`).**
501	   `kick 1`, `ok 0`. The kick provably runs and clears nothing.
502	5. **Lost or masked EOF interrupt.** `isr 0` with `start 2` — there is no
503	   interrupt to lose.
504	6. **RX-before-TX start ordering (b80).** Started rec fd 200 µs before play fd.
505	   **Identical** signature: `isr 0 / eof 0 / start 2`, `desc 80000ff0`,
506	   `intraw 000000a0`. Predicted dead beforehand — RX is the *slave* and an I2S
507	   slave frames on every WS edge, so there is no one-shot sync to miss.
508	
509	**CONFIRMED REAL but non-causal:** channel-restart orphaning. b79/b80 read
510	`chst 11 resc 1` — a restart really does orphan an in-flight container and #35
511	half 2 really does rescue it. Eliminating it did not fix the stall.
512	
513	🔴 **The `intraw 000000a0` "stale boot state" reading is WITHDRAWN.** The kick
514	writes `DMA_IN_INT_CLR = 0xFFFFFFFF` and `kick 1` proves it ran — yet `intraw`
515	still reads `000000a0` afterwards. Those bits (INFIFO_FULL_WM + INFIFO_UDF_L1)
516	are **continuously re-asserting**: live evidence of persistent RX FIFO
517	starvation, not latched history.
518	
519	Standing signature of the stall, invariant across b76–b80:
520	
521	    i2s eof 0 match 0 miss 0 empty 0  start 2 busy 1     (or eof 1 / start 3)
522	    i2s desc 80000ff0 80000010        owner=1, size 4080, length 0
523	    i2s intraw 000000a0 intena 00000002
524	
525	Owner bit set with zero bytes written = **the DMA is armed and no samples are
526	arriving from the codec.** The remaining suspects are below the DMA — ES8311
527	ADC/clock bring-up or the board's mic path — not the NuttX driver.
528	
529	⚠️ `VELAPAW_I2S_PROBES` lives in the **driver** (`esp32s3_i2s.c:88`), not in
530	`mic.c`. Must be 0 in any shipping build.
531	
532	## 🔴🔴 EVERYTHING BELOW ABOUT b84 CAUSING THE STALL IS FALSIFIED (2026-08-07)
533	
534	**Read this before acting on the b84–b88 section.** b83 — the exact image with
535	six previously-good boots, re-flashed from
536	`velapaw-snapshots\2026-08-07-b83-noaudlog\nuttx-b83-noaudlog.bin`,
537	sha `288649a9…`, esptool "Hash of data verified" — **now fails identically**:
538	
539	    cap FAILED -110 at 152370 / 166940 / 178720 ms   (Recognize taps)
540	    rec 0/54   play 3/3
541	    desc 80000ff0   intraw 000000a0   intena 00000002   chst 11
542	    rxconf 0008972c   txconf 08089204
543	
544	Same binary, same late capture timing that used to work, same fingerprint.
545	**So the fault is not in the app at all.** b84 broke nothing; b85, b86, b87 and
546	b88 were four builds spent against a software regression that does not exist.
547	Do not restart that hunt.
548	
549	What survives from those builds is still true and still useful (b86's separate
550	warm-up budget is a genuine fix, b87 falsified capture timing, b88 proved the
551	session rebuild deadlocks) — but the *premise* that b84 caused the stall is dead.
552	
553	**Where it points instead.** TX runs 3/3 through the same GDMA block, same
554	clock, same peripheral. The only signal unique to the failing direction is the
555	codec's ADC data line into the SoC: `CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_DINPIN=14` (BCLK 13,
556	WS 15, MCLK 12, DOUT 16 — and `esp32s3_st7789.c:411` independently warns that
557	IO12–16 are the codec's I2S bus). Next moves are hardware, not software:
558	bisect what changed physically since the last good b83 boot, then put the FX2
559	logic analyzer on GPIO14 + BCLK + WS during a capture. DIN flat while BCLK/WS
560	toggle ⇒ codec/mic side; DIN toggling ⇒ SoC pad/mux side.
561	
562	⚠️ The `mic stage 38 (close-stop)` hang b88 hit is **not a new bug** — it is
563	already documented at `board/patches/i2s-rx-eof-walk.py:28`: es8311's worker
564	thread cannot terminate while it holds stranded buffers, so the `pthread_join`
565	inside `AUDIOIOC_STOP` never returns. A symptom of the stall, not a cause.
566	
567	## b84–b87: WHO arms the mic, and WHEN the first capture happens
568	
569	**b84 removed the Recognize tab's voice arming** — it was a second, spoken
570	feeding path (`voice_apply()` → `velapaw_feeder_dispense()`) that contradicted
571	Model B (scheduled time **AND** recognised pet). Confirmed gone on hardware.
572	Since b84 the **meal dialog is the only thing that ever opens the audio
573	device**, and `voice_apply`, `voice_idle_text`, `g_voice_lbl`,
574	`g_voice_dismissed/hold/shown` are all deleted.
575	
576	That removal exposed two things Recognize had been providing **by accident**:
577	
578	1. **Readiness.** `vsched_tick()` will not prompt until `g_voice_ready`, set in
579	   exactly one place — after a capture **succeeds**. Standing on Recognize had
580	   always supplied that long before the dialog opened. b85 restores it with a
581	   boot warm-up (unarmed captures, result discarded).
582	2. **Unlimited retries.** b85 fed those warm-up failures into the shared
583	   `g_voice_consec`, and `VOICE_MAX_CAPFAIL 3` latches `g_voice_fail` and
584	   `return NULL` — **the worker thread exits and voice is dead for the boot.**
585	   b85 therefore burned the whole budget at boot and was *worse* than b83.
586	   **b86 gives the warm-up its own counter** (`g_voice_warmfail`) that never
587	   touches `g_voice_consec`, retrying forever with backoff (200 ms ×5, 2 s ×10,
588	   then 10 s). Armed/dialog captures keep the old budget.
589	
590	### What b86 proved: retrying within a boot CANNOT recover
591	
592	19 warm-up captures over 217 s, every one `-110`, hardware state **bit-identical
593	each time** and identical to b78/b79/b80:
594	
595	    rec 0/342  play 19/19      342 RX buffers in, none back; TX 19/19 fine
596	    desc 80000ff0              owner 1, length 0
597	    intraw 000000a0            INFIFO_FULL_WM + INFIFO_UDF_L1, RE-RAISED after
598	                               every kick's INT_CLR -> live starvation
599	    intena 00000002            IN_SUC_EOF enabled, never fires
600	    mickick 19 ok 0  resc 19  start 20
601	
602	TX completing 19/19 through the same GDMA proves the clock runs and the block's
603	EOF path works — **it is specifically the RX channel that never fills.**
604	
605	⚠️ **Two of my own readings here were WRONG — don't repeat them.**
606	`velapaw_i2s_rx_kick()` **does** drain `rx.act` (`while (!sq_empty(&rx.act))
607	sq_addfirst(sq_remlast(...), &rx.pend)`) and then `i2s_rxdma_start()` re-arms
608	one immediately — so `act 1 pend 1` after a kick is the kick **working**, not
609	failing. And **nothing in the UI ever closed the session in b83 either**:
610	`velapaw_mic_shutdown()` is called only from `velapaw_main.c`'s
611	`velapaw kws mic` CLI path, never from `ui_lvgl.c`.
612	
613	### The live hypothesis (b87): the FIRST capture decides, and b84 moved it
614	
615	`velapaw_mic_preopen()` opens one session at boot and **nothing ever closes
616	it**, so once that stream wedges every later capture inherits it — the kick
617	resets GDMA + I2S RX but never the ES8311.
618	
619	    b83 and earlier   first capture when the owner tapped Recognize, tens of
620	                      seconds in, board settled            -> 6 good boots
621	    b85 / b86         first capture at ~13.1 s -- mid TFLM model reads, camera
622	                      bring-up, the 5350 ms pre-open       -> 0 good boots
623	
624	**b87 holds unarmed captures until `VOICE_WARMUP_AT_MS` (30 s) after power-on**,
625	tested against `mono_ms()` (monotonic from boot). Armed captures are *not*
626	delayed. Falsifiable: the vlog shows either nothing (warm-up succeeded) or
627	`warmup FAILED -110 (#1)` at ~33 s — and if it fails at 33 s exactly as at 16 s,
628	**timing is not the variable** and the next move is rebuilding the session
629	(close both fds, re-open, which is the only thing that re-runs ES8311
630	configure). b80 removed that path because `mic_session_close()` hung, but that
631	predates b79's fix of the collect hang.
632	
633	Build chain, all esptool hash-verified on-chip:
634	`b83 288649a9` → `b84 a0860dee` → `b85 ec7c1d4d` → `b86 1666c029` →
635	`b87 95a383ed`. Console fix: [[velapaw-console-blocking]].
636	
637	## ✅ SOLVED: the `es8311 -22` boot spam is cosmetic — never chase it
638	
639	    es8311_getcoeff: MCLK = 4096000 and samplerate = 48000 not supported
640	    es8311_setsamplerate: Failed to set sample rate: -22
641	
642	The driver does it to itself. `es8311.c:2153` sets
643	`priv->samprate = ES8311_DEFAULT_SAMPRATE` (48000), then `:2191` calls
644	`es8311_setsamplerate()` during init while MCLK is 4096000 (= 256 × 16000).
645	`getcoeff(4096000, 48000)` has no table entry → `-22`. The real rate is
646	programmed later from `caps->ac_controls.hw[0]`, and `:1039` already calls
647	`es8311_reset()` *before* `:1046`'s `setsamplerate()`. **It appears in working
648	boots too**, so its presence in a failing log means nothing. This misled a
649	third-party analysis into proposing an ES8311 power-up clock race; that was
650	rejected on evidence.
651	
652	## Session shape
653	
654	Open, configure, `AUDIOIOC_START` **once**; each capture only enqueues and
655	collects. Between captures the session is running but idle. Free-running RX is
656	not an option: `mq_maxmsg = nbuffers + 8`, so with no reader the driver's
657	`mq_send` would drop buffer pointers. `mic_flush_mq()` before each re-arm.
658	
659	⚠️ **`apb->nbytes` is read by the driver *during* the enqueue ioctl** — the
660	caller sets it: record side `0`, playback side `nmaxbytes`. Zeroing it in a
661	shared helper silently sends a zero-length TX buffer → no clock → hang. TX
662	must stay primed; RX borrows BCLK/WS from TX (see [[velapaw-audio-bringup]]).
663	
664	⚠️ Do not conflate this with the falsified theory above. A **zero-length first**
665	TX buffer means `I2S_TX_START` is never set, so the clock never starts — real.
666	TX **draining after** a good buffer is harmless, because `TX_START` stays set
667	and `#16` cleared `TX_STOP_EN`.
668	
669	## Measurement, not ears
670	
671	`velapaw_mic_stats()` prints `peak N@index`, `rms`, `dc`, `rail` and an
672	8-segment peak profile. Reference at 30 dB, build 52, de-interleaved:
673	
674	    silence  rms  26  profile    87    82    87    68    55    67    56    60
675	    "yes"    rms 645  profile   447    90   107   100  4085  5019  1426  1724
676	    "no"     rms 791  profile  1949  5402  3534   596    74    66    87    94
677	
678	`MIC_TRACE` (default 0) prints one line per buffer with the `apb` pointer and
679	four samples — the check on both fixes at once: pointers must all be distinct,
680	`s` must alternate live/0. Turn it on for any future capture regression.
681	Do **not** read a full-scale spike at a fixed index as clipping — that is the
682	start-of-stream transient, see [[velapaw-audio-gain]].

"""Copy a .pptx, replacing one typeface with another in every XML part.

Also fills the theme's empty East Asian font slots, so text without its own
font setting picks up the replacement too.
"""
import re
import sys
import zipfile

src, dst, old, new = sys.argv[1:5]

zin = zipfile.ZipFile(src)
zout = zipfile.ZipFile(dst, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED)
changed = 0
for info in zin.infolist():
    data = zin.read(info.filename)
    if info.filename.endswith((".xml", ".rels")):
        text = data.decode("utf-8")
        before = text
        text = text.replace(f'typeface="{old}"', f'typeface="{new}"')
        if info.filename.startswith("ppt/theme/"):
            text = re.sub(r'<a:ea typeface=""\s*/>', f'<a:ea typeface="{new}"/>', text)
        if text != before:
            changed += before.count(f'typeface="{old}"')
            data = text.encode("utf-8")
    zout.writestr(info, data, compress_type=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED)
zout.close()

check = zipfile.ZipFile(dst)
left = sum(check.read(n).decode("utf-8", "ignore").count(f'typeface="{old}"')
           for n in check.namelist() if n.endswith(".xml"))
print(f"replaced {changed}, remaining {left}, entries {len(check.namelist())}, test {check.testzip()}")

# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis

If you are about to make a new document and this session offers Claude's own docs (a Docs connector, docs skill or Docs artifact type), and the user has neither named Word/.docx/.dotx, asked for tracked changes, nor supplied a .docx/.dotx file to change or use as a template, make the document there instead. It exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to make a Word file. A .docx/.dotx given only as source material does not count as supplied. This skill remains the right tool for producing, reading, editing, templating or converting Word files.

A `.docx` is a ZIP archive of XML files. Choose your approach by task:

| Task | Approach |
|---|---|
| **Create** a new document | Write a `docx` (npm) script — see gotchas below |
| **Edit** an existing document | `unzip` → edit `word/document.xml` → `zip` (docx-js cannot open existing files) |
| **Read** content | `pandoc -t markdown file.docx` |

> Script paths below are relative to this skill's directory.

## Creating with docx-js — gotchas

`docx` is preinstalled — do not run `npm install` first; write the script and `require('docx')` directly. Only if that require fails: `npm install docx`. The model knows the API; these are the footguns:

- **Page size defaults to A4.** For US Letter set `page: { size: { width: 12240, height: 15840 } }` (DXA; 1440 = 1″).
- **Landscape:** pass portrait dimensions and `orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE` — docx-js swaps width/height internally.
- **Tables need dual widths:** set `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on every cell, both in `WidthType.DXA` (PERCENTAGE breaks in Google Docs). Column widths must sum to the table width.
- **Table shading:** use `ShadingType.CLEAR`, never `SOLID` (renders black).
- **Lists:** never insert `•` literally; use a `numbering` config with `LevelFormat.BULLET`.
- **`ImageRun` requires `type:`** (`"png"`, `"jpg"`, …).
- **`PageBreak` must be inside a `Paragraph`.**
- **Never use `\n`** — use separate `Paragraph` elements.
- **TOC:** headings must use built-in `HeadingLevel.*`; custom heading styles need `outlineLevel` set or they won't appear.
- **Don't use a table as a horizontal rule** — use a paragraph bottom border instead.
- **Dot-leader / right-aligned-on-same-line:** use `PositionalTab` (`alignment: PositionalTabAlignment.RIGHT`, `leader: PositionalTabLeader.DOT`) inside a `TextRun`, not literal `.` or space padding.

## Verify the output

After writing a `.docx`, render it and look at it:

```bash
python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf output.docx
pdftoppm -jpeg -r 100 output.pdf page
ls page-*.jpg   # then Read the images
```

`pdftoppm` zero-pads page numbers to the width of the page count (`page-01.jpg`…`page-12.jpg`).

## Editing existing documents

Legacy `.doc` files must be converted first: `python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx file.doc`.

```bash
unzip -q doc.docx -d unpacked/
find unpacked -type l -delete   # strip symlink entries — docx from external parties is untrusted
python scripts/merge_runs.py unpacked/   # coalesce fragmented runs so text is findable
# edit unpacked/word/document.xml in place — do NOT reformat or pretty-print
(cd unpacked && rm -f ../out.docx && zip -Xr ../out.docx .)
python scripts/office/validate.py out.docx --original doc.docx   # XSD checks; --auto-repair fixes common issues
# redlining? add --author "<the name you redlined under>" to check every edit is tracked
```

Word splits text across many `<w:r>` runs (revision ids, spell-check markers), so a phrase you can see in the document often doesn't exist as a contiguous string in the XML. `merge_runs.py` merges adjacent identically-formatted runs in `word/document.xml` without changing content or rendering; it also accepts a `.docx` directly (`python scripts/merge_runs.py doc.docx -o merged.docx`).

**Tracked changes:** when redlining, validate with `--author "<the name you redlined under>"` (needs `--original`) — it reports any text you changed without a `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` around it, which is easy to do by accident and invisible in the accepted view. Wrap runs in `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` with `w:id`, `w:author`, `w:date` attributes. Inside `<w:del>`, the text element is `<w:delText>`, not `<w:t>`. A deleted paragraph mark (`<w:pPr><w:rPr><w:del w:id=".." w:author=".." w:date=".."/></w:rPr></w:pPr>`) means "merge this paragraph into the next" — so deleting a paragraph outright is that plus a `<w:del>` around every run. The `<w:del/>` must come before the rPr's other children; their order is schema-enforced.

To produce a clean copy with all tracked changes accepted: `python scripts/accept_changes.py in.docx out.docx`.

Accepting a deleted paragraph mark should join that paragraph to the one below it, so a paragraph whose runs are *all* deleted vanishes. Word does this; `accept_changes.py` and `pandoc --track-changes=accept` don't always. Both fail the same way — they strip the deleted text but leave the emptied paragraph behind, which reads as a stray empty bullet when it was auto-numbered:

- `pandoc --track-changes=accept` never joins the paragraphs.
- `accept_changes.py` (LibreOffice) joins them correctly, except when the deleted paragraph is followed by an empty spacer paragraph.

An empty bullet in either view is an artifact of that view, not a defect in the document. Check paragraph deletions in the XML.

## Comments

Comments require six cross-linked files. Use the helper — directory mode when you'll also be editing `document.xml` (saves an unzip/rezip cycle), `.docx`-direct mode otherwise:

```bash
# Against an already-unpacked directory (preferred when also placing markers)
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Fees & expenses cap is too low"
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Agreed" --parent 0

# Against a .docx directly
python scripts/comment.py contract.docx "This cap is too low" -o annotated.docx
```

The script writes `comments.xml`, `commentsExtended.xml`, `commentsIds.xml`, `commentsExtensible.xml`, the relationships, and the content-type overrides. Comment IDs are auto-assigned. It then prints the `<w:commentRangeStart>`/`<w:commentRangeEnd>`/`<w:commentReference>` snippet to add to `word/document.xml` so the comment anchors to specific text — until you place those markers, the comment exists but is not visible.

# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis

If you are about to make a new document and this session offers Claude's own docs (a Docs connector, docs skill or Docs artifact type), and the user has neither named Word/.docx/.dotx, asked for tracked changes, nor supplied a .docx/.dotx file to change or use as a template, make the document there instead. It exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to make a Word file. A .docx/.dotx given only as source material does not count as supplied. This skill remains the right tool for producing, reading, editing, templating or converting Word files.

A `.docx` is a ZIP archive of XML files. Choose your approach by task:

| Task | Approach |
|---|---|
| **Create** a new document | Write a `docx` (npm) script — see gotchas below |
| **Edit** an existing document | `unzip` → edit `word/document.xml` → `zip` (docx-js cannot open existing files) |
| **Read** content | `pandoc -t markdown file.docx` |

> Script paths below are relative to this skill's directory.

## Creating with docx-js — gotchas

`docx` is preinstalled — do not run `npm install` first; write the script and `require('docx')` directly. Only if that require fails: `npm install docx`. The model knows the API; these are the footguns:

- **Page size defaults to A4.** For US Letter set `page: { size: { width: 12240, height: 15840 } }` (DXA; 1440 = 1″).
- **Landscape:** pass portrait dimensions and `orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE` — docx-js swaps width/height internally.
- **Tables need dual widths:** set `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on every cell, both in `WidthType.DXA` (PERCENTAGE breaks in Google Docs). Column widths must sum to the table width.
- **Table shading:** use `ShadingType.CLEAR`, never `SOLID` (renders black).
- **Lists:** never insert `•` literally; use a `numbering` config with `LevelFormat.BULLET`.
- **`ImageRun` requires `type:`** (`"png"`, `"jpg"`, …).
- **`PageBreak` must be inside a `Paragraph`.**
- **Never use `\n`** — use separate `Paragraph` elements.
- **TOC:** headings must use built-in `HeadingLevel.*`; custom heading styles need `outlineLevel` set or they won't appear.
- **Don't use a table as a horizontal rule** — use a paragraph bottom border instead.
- **Dot-leader / right-aligned-on-same-line:** use `PositionalTab` (`alignment: PositionalTabAlignment.RIGHT`, `leader: PositionalTabLeader.DOT`) inside a `TextRun`, not literal `.` or space padding.

## Verify the output

After writing a `.docx`, render it and look at it:

```bash
python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf output.docx
pdftoppm -jpeg -r 100 output.pdf page
ls page-*.jpg   # then Read the images
```

`pdftoppm` zero-pads page numbers to the width of the page count (`page-01.jpg`…`page-12.jpg`).

## Editing existing documents

Legacy `.doc` files must be converted first: `python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx file.doc`.

```bash
unzip -q doc.docx -d unpacked/
find unpacked -type l -delete   # strip symlink entries — docx from external parties is untrusted
python scripts/merge_runs.py unpacked/   # coalesce fragmented runs so text is findable
# edit unpacked/word/document.xml in place — do NOT reformat or pretty-print
(cd unpacked && rm -f ../out.docx && zip -Xr ../out.docx .)
python scripts/office/validate.py out.docx --original doc.docx   # XSD checks; --auto-repair fixes common issues
# redlining? add --author "<the name you redlined under>" to check every edit is tracked
```

Word splits text across many `<w:r>` runs (revision ids, spell-check markers), so a phrase you can see in the document often doesn't exist as a contiguous string in the XML. `merge_runs.py` merges adjacent identically-formatted runs in `word/document.xml` without changing content or rendering; it also accepts a `.docx` directly (`python scripts/merge_runs.py doc.docx -o merged.docx`).

**Tracked changes:** when redlining, validate with `--author "<the name you redlined under>"` (needs `--original`) — it reports any text you changed without a `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` around it, which is easy to do by accident and invisible in the accepted view. Wrap runs in `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` with `w:id`, `w:author`, `w:date` attributes. Inside `<w:del>`, the text element is `<w:delText>`, not `<w:t>`. A deleted paragraph mark (`<w:pPr><w:rPr><w:del w:id=".." w:author=".." w:date=".."/></w:rPr></w:pPr>`) means "merge this paragraph into the next" — so deleting a paragraph outright is that plus a `<w:del>` around every run. The `<w:del/>` must come before the rPr's other children; their order is schema-enforced.

To produce a clean copy with all tracked changes accepted: `python scripts/accept_changes.py in.docx out.docx`.

Accepting a deleted paragraph mark should join that paragraph to the one below it, so a paragraph whose runs are *all* deleted vanishes. Word does this; `accept_changes.py` and `pandoc --track-changes=accept` don't always. Both fail the same way — they strip the deleted text but leave the emptied paragraph behind, which reads as a stray empty bullet when it was auto-numbered:

- `pandoc --track-changes=accept` never joins the paragraphs.
- `accept_changes.py` (LibreOffice) joins them correctly, except when the deleted paragraph is followed by an empty spacer paragraph.

An empty bullet in either view is an artifact of that view, not a defect in the document. Check paragraph deletions in the XML.

## Comments

Comments require six cross-linked files. Use the helper — directory mode when you'll also be editing `document.xml` (saves an unzip/rezip cycle), `.docx`-direct mode otherwise:

```bash
# Against an already-unpacked directory (preferred when also placing markers)
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Fees & expenses cap is too low"
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Agreed" --parent 0

# Against a .docx directly
python scripts/comment.py contract.docx "This cap is too low" -o annotated.docx
```

The script writes `comments.xml`, `commentsExtended.xml`, `commentsIds.xml`, `commentsExtensible.xml`, the relationships, and the content-type overrides. Comment IDs are auto-assigned. It then prints the `<w:commentRangeStart>`/`<w:commentRangeEnd>`/`<w:commentReference>` snippet to add to `word/document.xml` so the comment anchors to specific text — until you place those markers, the comment exists but is not visible.

## Dependencies

`docx` (npm, preinstalled — install only if `require('docx')` fails) · `pandoc` · LibreOffice (`soffice`) · `pdftoppm` (Poppler)
