28	[10] P<heading 2> Abstract
29	[11] P<Normal (Web)> An ordinary timed feeder cannot tell which animal is standing at the bowl, so in a multi-pet household per-pet portioning and per-pet weight control are impossible — and per-pet portioning is the first thing a vet prescribes. VelaPaw, built on openVela (NuttX) and a Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5-C, identifies the individual pet on-device from a single camera and gates dispensing on two conditions together: the pet is recognised, and one of its meals is due today and unfed. Recognition uses open-set metric learning rather than classification — the model emits only a 128-dimensional L2-normalised embedding, so enrolling a new pet is a pure runtime operation requiring no retraining and no firmware update. Measured results: porting an INT8 operator library to Xtensa LX7, for which openVela ships none, cut inference from 6.75 s to 1.31 s; tracing a display fault with a logic analyser to panel bit-desynchronisation allowed a move to 40 MHz hardware SPI with GDMA, cutting full-screen repaint from 246 ms to 61 ms; and trimming 20 unused tools compressed the ai_agent request body from 19,391 B to fit NuttX's IOB pool, taking end-to-end latency from 150–300 s to 3.6–35.6 s. All image processing and every feeding decision happen on-device and no image ever leaves the hardware; the only networked component, ai_agent, uses a custom Skill to read the records the feeder writes to littlefs and speaks only when an appetite threshold is crossed. Unplugged from the network, the feeder behaves identically.
30	[12] P<heading 2> 3. Technical Report
31	[13] P<heading 3> 3.1 Introduction
32	[14] P<heading 4> 3.1.1 Background and problem statement
33	[15] P<Normal (Web)> In a multi-pet household, an ordinary timed feeder has a structural flaw: it does not know which animal is standing at the bowl. The lid opens on schedule, whoever arrives first eats everything, and the slower one goes hungry. Per-pet portions, per-pet weight control, per-pet appetite monitoring — none of it is possible. And per-pet portioning is precisely the first thing a vet asks for when prescribing a weight-loss, disease-management, or post-operative plan.
34	[16] P<Normal (Web)> Existing camera-equipped feeders — for instance the Xiaomi Mijia Smart Pet Feeder 2 Vision Edition, launched March 2026 at ¥449 crowdfunded / ¥549 retail — solve the problem of letting the owner see the bowl; what the camera produces is a video stream. They do not solve identifying which animal it is. Such products also bind the camera feed to a cloud account, which is the single largest source of hesitation pet owners have about a household camera.
35	[17] P<Normal (Web)> VelaPaw therefore defines its problem as:
36	[18] P<Normal> On an MCU-class device, with no network, no cloud, and no phone app, use a single camera to tell which pet is at the bowl, and dispense only the meal that pet is due right now; then keep a long-term record of each pet's intake and proactively tell the owner when appetite goes wrong. 
37	[19] P<Normal (Web)> That last "proactively tell the owner" layer is carried by openVela's ai_agent framework and is the only part of the system that needs a network. The feeder itself behaves identically offline.
38	[20] P<heading 4> 3.1.2 Technical challenges
39	[21] TABLE
40	    r0: Challenge | What it looked like
41	    r1: ① Compute for fine-grained on-device recognition | Individual pet ID is a fine-grained recognition problem requiring a MobileNet-class backbone plus a metric-learning head. Running that model on Xtensa LX7 through TFLite-Micro's reference kernels takes ≈6.75 s per inference — unusable. An early TFLM spike (docs/TFLM_SPIKE_REPORT.md, run in QEMU, not on S3) profiled a comparable INT8 CNN and found CONV_2D accounts for 84% of the clock (643,819 of 768,105 ticks): latency is almost entirely decided by the INT8 convolution kernels. Yet the openVela tree ships only cmsis-nn (ARM) and nnlib-hifi4 (HiFi DSP) — there is no operator library for LX7.
42	    r2: ② Adding a pet must not require retraining | No consumer product can ask a user to retrain a model to add a cat. N-way classification had to be abandoned in favour of open-set metric learning, with a threshold that holds up under real household lighting.
43	    r3: ③ The model does not fit the MCU's memory map | A 1.44 MB identity model cannot be memory-mapped as a const array — the ESP32-S3 DROM0 MMU window saturates well before that. It must be read from raw flash into PSRAM; but a flash read suspends the CPU cache, and PSRAM is reached through that cache, so if the loading thread's stack lives in PSRAM the whole SoC deadlocks.
44	    r4: ④ The hardware-SPI display "renders nothing" | Full-screen writes worked; any partial window (a CASET/RASET sub-rectangle followed by RAMWR) never appeared — while the identical byte sequence over bit-banged GPIO worked perfectly. This survived roughly 60 rounds of blind rebuilds.
45	    r5: ⑤ ai_agent's request body vs. the network buffer | ai_agent registers 36 tools by default, whose JSON schemas push a single LLM request body to 19,391 B, of which 9,946 B is tool schema. NuttX's IOB pool is only NBUFFERS(64) × BUFSIZE(196) = 12,544 B, leaving roughly 7,840 B usable after THROTTLE(24). The request is far larger than the available buffer; the symptom is an intermittent hang with no timeout.
46	    r6: ⑥ Agent answers that look right but are fabricated | The heartbeat replayed its own history; list_dir's prefix match plus a local-tool shortcut handed (no files found) straight to the user as a final answer; ask was truncated at the seventh word by MAX_ARGS. None of these raise an error — they simply make the answer fluent and wrong.
47	[22] P<heading 4> 3.1.3 Innovations
48	[23] P<Normal list1.0> Dual-condition "recognition × schedule" gating. Food is dispensed only when "this is that pet" and "one of its meals is due today and has not been fed" are both true — at most once per meal per day, with any meal individually skippable. Recognition alone would feed the greedy one all day; a timer alone would feed whoever happened to walk past. This AND gate is the core product logic and the precondition for per-pet portioning to mean anything.
49	[24] P<Normal list1.0> Open-set metric learning instead of a classifier. The model is only a generic pet feature extractor, mapping a 128×128 frame to an L2-normalised 128-dimensional embedding. Enrolment = store the mean embedding of a few photos; recognition = cosine similarity. Adding a pet is a pure runtime operation — no retraining, no firmware update.
50	[25] P<Normal list1.0> A bug that survived 60 rebuilds turned into a 4× speedup. A logic analyser disproved the "software problem" hypothesis and reframed it as a panel bit-synchronisation problem (§3.4.3). With that fixed, the display moved from bit-banging to 40 MHz hardware SPI + GDMA: full-screen repaint 246 ms → 61 ms.
51	[26] P<Normal list1.0> ai_agent as a silent health monitor, not a chatbot. A heartbeat task periodically reads the records the feeder itself wrote to flash and speaks only when a threshold is crossed. When everything is fine, the device says nothing. The custom Skill states explicitly that only numbers from those files may be used, and nothing may be invented.
52	[27] P<Normal list1.0> A clear "offline-first, network-optional" boundary. Every feeding decision and all image processing happen on-device; no image ever leaves the device. Unplug the network and the feeder behaves identically — only the Agent layer stops. This is both a privacy claim and a reliability claim.
53	[28] P<Normal list1.0> Pocket-by-pocket mechanical dosing. A continuously rotating paddle rotor replaces a flap: a flap's dose drifts with hopper level, whereas each rotor pocket has fixed volume, so grams = pockets × grams-per-pocket — making per-pet portioning true at the mechanical level too.

83	[58] P<heading 4> 3.2.2 Design decisions and rationale
84	[59] TABLE
85	    r0: Decision | Chosen | Rationale / rejected alternative
86	    r1: Recognition paradigm | Open-set metric learning (cosine match) | Rejected N-way classification: every new pet would require retraining and an OTA — unacceptable in a consumer product. Metric learning reduces "add a pet" to writing one flash record. The cost is inherently weaker rejection of non-pet objects, so the lever is placed on enrolment quality (close, well-lit, front-facing) rather than on the threshold.
87	    r2: Inference runtime | TFLite-Micro + ESP-NN | An early spike using the in-tree tflm_benchmark in a simulator confirmed integration works, all operators are covered, and the tensor arena is only 84,420 B (negligible against 8 MB PSRAM), and located the bottleneck in CONV_2D (84%). That determined the project would not be viable without LX7 SIMD kernels (ESP-NN).
88	    r3: Model storage | Raw flash partition, read into PSRAM at boot | Rejected memory-mapped const arrays: 1.44 MB far exceeds the DROM0 MMU window. Uses spi_flash_read instead; because a flash read suspends the cache, the reading thread's stack must live in internal SRAM (.bss), not PSRAM.
89	    r4: Dispenser mechanism | 28BYJ-48 stepper + paddle rotor | Rejected an MG90S servo + flap: a servo can only oscillate, and with the inlet and outlet 180° apart a zero-net-rotation wobble can never carry a pocket across — it dispenses the initial charge and then spins uselessly. A flap's dose also drifts with hopper level, which would destroy the per-pet portioning claim outright. A stepper's continuous unidirectional rotation makes grams = pockets × grams-per-pocket strictly true, and its gearbox gives the low-speed torque needed to resist jamming.
90	    r5: Carrier board | Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5-C | Same SoC as the official ESP32-S3-EYE, so the openVela port and all inference work carry over unchanged. But the product needs a capacitive touchscreen (enrolment, schedule editing, trends) and a hardware RTC (schedules stay correct across power loss) — the EYE has neither. Same platform, better carrier.
91	    r6: On-board networking | USB CDC-NCM composite device | Rejected RNDIS: Windows' rndismp6.sys hard-requires RNDIS on interface 0, which collides with the CDC-ACM console; the resulting Code-10 proved unavoidable. CDC-NCM makes the console (COM port) and the network interface (eth0) usable simultaneously over one USB cable. Rejected on-board Wi-Fi as the demo link: Wi-Fi works and remains in the configuration, but the USB composite link is far more reproducible in a demo setting.
92	    r7: Agent data bridge | Feeder writes Markdown; Agent reads it with read_file | Rejected custom tools / IPC / shared memory. After each feed the VelaPaw C application writes plain Markdown to /data/ai_agent/velapaw/{status,feed_log}.md, and the Agent reads it with the framework's own read_file. Zero new tools, zero new protocol, zero coupling: to the Agent it is an ordinary file; to the C application it is an fprintf.
93	    r8: Agent persistence | littlefs at 0x180000 mounted as /data | Rejected tmpfs: the API key, session history, and Skill files would have to be re-provisioned on every reboot. The littlefs partition starts at 0x180000 while write-flash 0x0 nuttx.bin writes only up to about 0x17ec80, so /data survives both reboots and firmware reflashes.
94	    r9: Cloud model | DeepSeek deepseek-chat | OpenAI-compatible API with native function-calling support in the framework; directly reachable domestically, with controllable latency and cost.

106	[63] P<Normal (Web)> Degraded networks are handled at three layers. (1) Transport — vela_tls keeps and reuses a connection pool to api.deepseek.com:443 (visible as [vela_tls] Reusing pooled connection). When the server closes an idle keep-alive the result is a zero-byte response, which the framework recovers from in-band; measured 3/3 recoveries. This behaviour is not a defect. (2) Timeouts — tuned to real MCU round-trips: AGENT_LLM_TIMEOUT_SEC raised to 420 s and the socket timeout to 480 s; the previous 60 s default discarded a 62.6 s answer that had in fact succeeded. (3) Request size — the tool cut described in §3.3.3, which brings the body within what the IOB pool can carry, and is by far the most effective of the three on a weak link.

130	[69] P<Normal (Web)> ESP-NN integration and compliance. The 1.3 s figure depends on Espressif's ESP-NN (Apache-2.0) SIMD kernels, and that integration modifies the public repository apps/mlearning/tflite-micro. Per contest rules, changes to public repositories are submitted as a fork plus a PR against dev-ai-contest-2026 and are not merged into the team repository. Consequently this repository runs reference kernels out of the box (≈6.75 s), and ≈1.3 s once the ESP-NN fork is applied. The integration has three parts: (1) the library itself under apps/mlearning/esp-nn/; (2) seven kernel wrappers (conv, depthwise_conv, fully_connected, pooling, add, mul, softmax) placed in .../micro/kernels/esp_nn/; (3) a Makefile block compiling with -DESP_NN=1 -DCONFIG_NN_OPTIMIZED -mlongcalls that filters out the matching reference kernels to avoid duplicate symbols. Full wrapper source and reproduction steps are in docs/esp-nn/.

142	[73] P<Normal (Web)> (1) The recognition-gated feeding state machine.
143	[74] P<HTML Preformatted> 
144	[75] P<HTML Preformatted> if  match score >= 0.45  and  the match is pet P
145	[76] P<HTML Preformatted> and there exists a meal M of P that is due, unfed today, and not skipped
146	[77] P<HTML Preformatted> and P's grams so far today + M's grams <= P's daily cap
147	[78] P<HTML Preformatted> then dispense (grams / grams-per-pocket) pockets
148	[79] P<HTML Preformatted>      -> record a feed event -> update status.md / feed_log.md

150	[81] P<Normal (Web)> (2) Trimming the tool registry — the single highest-yield change in the project. The quantified form of the problem is in §3.1.2⑤. The fix excludes 20 tools irrelevant to a feeder via s_excluded_tools in tool_registry.c (4 wearable + 6 Feishu + 8 music + 2 quick-app), taking the tool count from 36 to 16 and the tool JSON to 4,706 B. Reliability went from intermittent to 8/8, and end-to-end latency from 150–300 s down to 3.6–35.6 s.
151	[82] P<Normal> The associated defect — an engineering lesson worth recording: cutting a tool leaves its callers behind. This cut orphaned five natural-language fast-path rows, a hand-written music_search branch, and Feishu copy in every system prompt. Because handle_nl_fast_path() runs before the LLM, a fast path pointing at an unregistered tool returns a blank or wrong result as the final answer. The standing check is now: after any change to s_excluded_tools, grep for the removed tool names and require zero hits.
152	[83] P<Normal (Web)> (3) Three classes of silent error. What they share is that the answer reads fluently but did not come from the data:
153	[84] P<Normal list2.0> The heartbeat replayed its own history — persisted session history survives reboots, so every firing after the first was reciting. history_json is calloc'd once outside the loop, so it needs an explicit '\0'.
154	[85] P<Normal list2.0> list_dir prefix matching plus the local-tool shortcut — the prefix was matched against an absolute path while the model passed a relative one, and because the tool sits in the local shortcut set, (no files found) was delivered to the owner as the answer. The fix accepts both spellings (the model actually uses three).
155	[86] P<Normal list2.0> Stale console history suppressing tool calls — the fix is not to trim history but to insert a system message mid-array forcing a re-read. The old history stays on disk untouched, and the result is still iters=3 tools=2 with a correct answer.
156	[87] P<Normal list2.0> ask truncating at the seventh word — root cause was MAX_ARGS 8 in nsh_commands.c, raised to 32.
157	[88] P<Normal (Web)> (4) Verification methodology. This project is deliberately distrustful of "it looks like it works", and settled on three criteria. END status=ok iters=N tools=M is the only real signal — a perfect answer with iters=1 tools=0 is a history replay. [skills] Skills summary: NNN bytes is what proves a Skill loaded; Skills system ready (N built-in) is a compile-time constant and proves nothing. And to test whether a reply genuinely came from the remote model, enrol a new pet mid-run — if the next firing finds it, an in-RAM llm_cache replay is ruled out.

169	[92] P<heading 4> 3.3.5 Suggested improvements to openVela
170	[93] P<Normal (Web)> All six come from real hardware experience on this project, ordered by value to the next developer:
171	[94] P<Normal list3.0> Provide an official optimised TFLM kernel path for Xtensa LX7 (ESP-NN). The tree ships cmsis-nn (ARM) and nnlib-hifi4 (HiFi DSP) but nothing for LX7 — despite the ESP32-S3 being this contest's primary chip. The gap is 6.75 s → 1.3 s (5×), which directly decides whether on-device vision AI is viable on openVela at all. It should be a Kconfig option in-tree rather than something every team forks for themselves.
172	[95] P<Normal list3.0> mallinfo() / free / memdump hang holding the heap lock on a freshly booted board and kill the whole chip. ai_agent happens to call a heap walk as the very first statement of its agent task, so every ask froze the machine (initially misdiagnosed as a PSRAM problem). Suggestion: offer a non-blocking or timed variant of the heap-walk API, or at minimum document its locking semantics.
173	[96] P<Normal list3.0> ARCH_HAVE_EXTRA_HEAPS is a selected symbol and therefore never appears in a defconfig — yet it is one of the three symbols required to keep task stacks out of PSRAM, and missing any one of them deadlocks the first ask. Suggestion: state the dependency explicitly in the XTENSA_IMEM_USE_SEPARATE_HEAP help text.
174	[97] P<Normal list3.0> The default IOB pool does not match ai_agent's default request body. 36 default tools produce a 19 KB request against roughly 7.8 KB of usable IOB — presenting as an intermittent hang with no timeout, which is the hardest failure class to diagnose. Suggestion: ship a leaner default tool set for MCU targets, or assert on request size at startup.
175	[98] P<Normal list3.0> ai_agent's local-tool shortcut should be kept consistent with the tool registry. handle_nl_fast_path() runs before the LLM, so once its target tool is excluded the wrong result is returned to the user as the final answer, with no warning. Suggestion: validate at compile time that the shortcut table is a subset of the registered tools.
176	[99] P<Normal list3.0> Several config options can silently destroy a board and deserve Kconfig warnings: CONFIG_RTC (kills the USB console on this board), CONFIG_NETINIT_THREAD (hangs the whole board), CONFIG_DEBUG_USB_INFO (wedges the console). Likewise CONFIG_NSH_LINELEN silently truncates an input line at about 80 characters, so provisioning a file with echo … >> /long/path writes corrupted content without any error.

266	[182] P<heading 4> 3.4.3 Hardware design and board bring-up
267	[183] P<Normal (Web)> Was a new hardware platform adapted / were drivers developed? Yes. The Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5-C has no existing board support in openVela. This project added a complete board implementation on top of esp32s3-devkit (board/, 1,903 lines of C plus a 205-line defconfig), driving the following four peripherals from scratch:
268	[184] TABLE
269	    r0: Peripheral | Connection | Driver highlights
270	    r1: ST7796 touch panel / 320×480 | Hardware SPI2 + GDMA at 40 MHz; CLK=GPIO5, MOSI=GPIO1, CS=GPIO4; FT5x06 touch on I²C0 (SCL=7 / SDA=8) | See "the hardest debug" below. Pixel rows must pass through an internal-SRAM bounce buffer — SPI DMA cannot read PSRAM cache-coherently. Address-window setup was batched from 11 SPI calls down to 5 (LVGL resets the window on every putarea).
271	    r2: OV5640 camera | ESP32-S3 LCD_CAM peripheral with a GDMA receive channel, configured over SCCB/I²C; brought out on a 30 cm FFC with a 1:1 coupler | The preview was initially transposed 90° and tinted violet — two independent root causes. (a) Flip/mirror: bits 1 and 2 of 0x3820/0x3821 must be cleared, and the transposition itself can only be corrected in the software resample — the registers structurally cannot do it. (b) The BLC pattern register 0x4514 must be set to 0x88. The discriminator is a reusable rule: whole-frame hue is decisive — a flip or Bayer-phase error swaps red and blue and can never lose green, so violet (R+B, no G) means 0x4514, not the flip bits.
272	    r3: PCF85063 RTC | I²C0, raw register access | Deliberately does not use CONFIG_RTC — on this board it kills the USB CDC console. The boot time seed is designed as a floor anchored to the build date rather than a "anything before 2017 is invalid" plausibility test: the latter pins the board to one date forever with no way to correct it (wall_set_min only rewrites hours and minutes, and nsh has no date).
273	    r4: 28BYJ-48 stepper feeder | ULN2003 driver board, IN1–IN4 = GPIO9 / 10 / 11 / 43; separate 5 V supply, common ground only | Full-step sequence in software. IN4 must be GPIO43 (U0TXD), not GPIO44 (U0RXD) — GPIO44 is clamped and cannot drive the coil cleanly, which was the real cause of the early "buzzes but won't turn" (a pin problem, not a phase-order problem). GPIO43 is free because the console runs over USB-Serial/JTAG rather than UART0. The stepper must never use GPIO12–16 — those are the ES8311 codec's private I²S bus (not brought out to any header) and are already claimed by the voice feature.
274	    r5: ES8311 audio | I²S0: MCLK=12, BCLK=13, DIN=14, WS=15, DOUT=16; 16 kHz | Getting microphone capture working required locating and fixing a driver-layer defect: the RX TDM slot map was never programmed — the true root cause of the stalled RX channel. A PSRAM cache trap additionally forced a two-slot stream over an 18-buffer pool, with the live slot flipping per capture.
275	[185] P<Normal (Web)> The hardest debug: the hardware-SPI display. Full-screen writes worked, any partial window never appeared, and the identical byte sequence over bit-banging worked fine. It survived roughly 60 rebuilds — framebuffer mirroring, DMA on/off, software CS, PSRAM coherency, forced pin routing all had no effect.
276	[186] P<Normal list4.0> Method — measure, don't guess. The SPI pins are not brought out to any header, so the board firmware was made to mirror FSPID_OUT and FSPICLK_OUT onto spare header pins through the GPIO matrix, plus a trigger marker, and captured with a logic analyser (sigrok/PulseView + an FX2 clone). The decisive first step was a ground-truth test: drive four known square waves on the probe pins and refuse to trust any capture until they read cleanly. That step immediately exposed a wiring/grounding fault which had been the source of all the earlier "garbage" captures — only afterwards was the real capture trustworthy.
277	[187] P<Normal list4.0> Finding. The decode showed the ESP32 emitting byte-perfect CASET 00 28 00 8B / RASET 00 28 00 8B / RAMWR / pixels, with correct DC alignment, exactly eight clean clock edges per byte, and no glitches. The peripheral was innocent all along.
278	[188] P<Normal list4.0> Root cause. This panel's chip select is hardwired low, so it can never resynchronise its bit counter on a CS edge — it just keeps counting clocks. The firmware initialised the panel by bit-banging and only then handed the pads to the SPI peripheral; that handover adds or drops a single clock edge, and from that instant the panel is off by one bit. Every subsequent command decodes to garbage, RAMWR is never recognised, no pixels reach GRAM, and the screen keeps showing whatever bit-banging drew last — which looks exactly like "hardware SPI drew nothing".
279	[189] P<Normal list4.0> Fix. Hand the pads to SPI first, then hardware-reset the panel (a software reset will not do — the reset command itself would be misread), then run the entire init sequence over SPI. Once the panel resynchronises under SPI ownership, partial windows render correctly.
280	[190] P<Normal list4.0> Payoff. With the path open, the display left bit-banging behind for 40 MHz hardware SPI2 + GDMA: a full 480×320 repaint went from ≈246 ms to ≈61 ms (4×). A bug that looked like a dead end became a performance win.
281	[191] P<Normal (Web)> Mechanical design (hardware/). Gravity hopper → paddle rotor → chute → bowl. Every part is parametric OpenSCAD source plus print-ready STL (PLA/PETG, 0.2 mm layers, 3 perimeters, no supports), with a JLC-outsourced parts list. The camera is removed from the mainboard and mounted, via a 30 cm FFC and a 1:1 coupler, inside a cam_pod on a two-legged cam_mast that straddles the chute — so the screen faces the owner while the lens faces the pet. Safety warning: a reversed FFC is fatal at first power-on — board pin N lands on camera pin 25−N, shorting a power rail straight onto data or ground pins. The camera module's ground is also not internally common, so orientation cannot be confirmed by metering "through" the camera; it must be checked against the 1/24 silkscreen and bare-copper continuity (verified pin by pin on 2026-07-30).

325	    r1: 1 | The first ask froze the entire chip | Root cause: agent_loop's pthread stack landed in PSRAM (0x3c…), and littlefs' flash read disables the cache PSRAM depends on. 327	    r3: 3 | IOB exhaustion hung requests silently | IOB_NBUFFERS / IOB_NCHAINS = 64, IOB_THROTTLE = 24 (160 chains is larger but will not boot), plus a host→board ping to prime ARP first. The 1420 vs 1514 MTU difference is real but not the cause — PKTSIZE should not be "fixed".

386	[239] P<Normal> An honest reading of this result: EER 0.291 is a lower-bound-style figure measured on 39 individuals from a public pet dataset under open-set conditions. It measures the difficulty of "given any two images, are they the same animal", not the accuracy of the deployed product. The real scenario is far easier: a household typically has 2–4 pets, enrolment photos are taken close-up and front-facing by the owner, and the match threshold is 0.45 — above the EER threshold, deliberately biased towards refusing rather than mis-feeding. The dominant factor in false accepts and false rejects is enrolment quality, not the threshold; that is a structural property of open-set metric learning, since a generic feature extractor inherently struggles to reject arbitrary non-pet objects, which is why the product puts its lever on guiding the user to take tight, well-lit, front-facing photos. Work not yet done: long-run false-accept / false-reject statistics for the three household pets under the final camera pose (cam_mast mount, current colour calibration). The current three pets' embeddings were captured on a firmware build that had the violet colour cast; after the 0x4514 fix they must be re-enrolled, and any earlier field accuracy figure is not comparable. This report therefore gives no such number rather than giving an untrustworthy one.

437	[279] P<Normal list10.0> Owners managing prescription diets or weight loss. A vet's gram-level plan has to actually be executed and recorded; VelaPaw's daily caps plus per-pet history are exactly that record of execution.

23	1. **`velapaw_meal_set_by_name(name, slot, minute)`** in
24	   `apps/examples/velapaw/identity/identity.c`. Pet ids are array indices that
25	   renumber on delete (`identity.h:52`), so a **name is the only stable handle**

28	   pet on this board is literally `bob,` with a comma from the on-screen
29	   keyboard. The model sent `"pet": "bob"` and it matched; the normaliser
30	   earned its place on the first real call. Returns 0 / -1 bad args / -2 no
31	   such pet / -3 ambiguous / -4 rejected, else the save rc. It **copies all
32	   three slots** before writing one, because `velapaw_identity_update()` writes
33	   every slot it is handed; passing 0 for portion/limit means "leave alone".

96	bytes`; hand-counting the format string twice gave 151. I trusted the count and
97	hunted an encoder bug instead of asking why the gap existed. `"Meal 2 for "` is
98	11 bytes and the diagnostic reported only 13 valid — corruption began exactly
99	at the `%s`, which names the variable.
100	
101	**Two theories falsified on the way — do not re-derive either.** (1) History
102	truncation: first failure at column 8230 against `hist=8192` looked conclusive;
103	`session_clear_all` reproduced it at column 4536 in a 10286-byte body.
104	(2) A stale over-read of `tool_output`: `cJSON_AddStringToObject` passes bytes
105	through verbatim and takes its own `strlen`, and `agent_tool_exec_streamed`
106	(`static inline` in `src/core/agent_mem.h:278`) is a clean malloc/execute/
107	memcpy with no appending — the message holds exactly our NUL-terminated bytes.
108	Also wrong: re-indexing `messages[N]` onto the assistant message. `msg[0]
109	role=user` proves the **system prompt is not in the messages array**.
110	
111	**Kept as defence:** `utf8_valid_prefix()` + `add_clean_string()` in
112	`agent_loop.c` now sanitise all four content sites (assistant `content` and
113	`reasoning_content`, single- and parallel-tool results), logging `[agent]
114	UTF-8: trimmed N of M byte(s) from "<key>"`. That warning is what localised
115	this bug; a malformed string no longer hard-fails a turn. The companion
116	`msg[N] role=… len=… utf8ok=…` dump (the 25-line `DIAGNOSTIC (velapaw
117	2026-10-11)` block) was **removed 2026-10-13**: `agent_loop.c` `c1c8ebf1…` →
118	`1474c400505aa4e472d7a77bf3bbe73e`, image `0e51e11b5c61786c966ebe072015f04a`
119	(1,564,608 B, fix10 + this only), gates `grep -ac "utf8ok="` = 0 and
120	`grep -ac "UTF-8: trimmed"` = 1. Flashed on COM3 and hardware-verified
121	2026-10-13: `ask change bob's dinner to 18:20` → `END status=ok iters=3
122	tools=2` in 5 s, saved to flash, and no `msg[N]` lines printed. About 10 min
123	later, `ask set bob's launch to 12` (a typo and a bare hour) set slot 2 to
124	12:00. It took the same 3 iterations, 2 tools and 5 s, after the agent
125	reconnected on its own (`Pooled connection stale, reconnecting`). Rollback:
126	the fix10 golden's `app-sources.tar.gz` has the old `agent_loop.c`.
127	
128	## Verification discipline that worked
129	
130	- `grep -ac "set_meal_schedule" nuttx/nuttx.bin` + `grep -ac "scheduled meals"`
131	  + `nm nuttx/nuttx | grep -E "velapaw_meal_set_by_name|tool_meal_set_execute"`
132	  as flash gates.
133	- `cat /data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md` **before** any LLM call proves the
134	  VelaPaw half independently of the agent.
135	- The agent's reply text is never the discriminator — only `status.md` is. The
136	  model will happily narrate a write it never performed.
137	- `cat` does not exist at the `vela>` prompt; `quit` back to `nsh>` first.
138	- There is **no direct tool-invoke command** in the agent CLI (`help` lists
139	  none), so tool verification always costs an LLM round trip.
140	- **An ask that hangs after `REQ written` is the USB network, not this
141	  tool** — the CDC-NCM TX wedge, fixed by fix10 on 2026-10-13; see
142	  [[velapaw-ncm-tx-wedge]].

38	## Why it "hung" / stopped recognizing (ranked)
39	1. **`recog_done` latch** — after one match or 2 misses, Recognize waited for a tab re-entry; looks exactly like "fails to recognize". stab1 re-arms on a tap, on a scene change (4×4 brightness signature), and once a minute while a meal is due (its first 30 min); gap 30 s after a hit, 3 s doubling to 20 s after misses.
40	2. **Console jam** — `uart_write` takes `xmit.lock` BEFORE it checks O_NONBLOCK, so one blocking writer + a host that stopped draining COM8 (PuTTY closed, PC asleep) jams every writer, UI thread included. stab1: `uprintf` (UI) and `vp_say` (store) ask FIONSPACE first (answered under a spinlock) and drop the line instead (counted as `drop`). Rejected: a pipe relay (CONFIG_PIPES off) and a dup2 mute.
41	3. Midnight: `today_total` wasn't reconciled for a board running past midnight → a day that ended at the cap refused the next day's meals. Fix: `velapaw_store_sync_day()` on the UI's day change.
42	4. Skips survived midnight. 5. BCS ran outside `g_tflm_lock` (raced KWS). 6. The preview ran at 150 ms forever after a match. 7. The worker could stick in state 2. 8. The camera HAL hides failures: `velapaw_camera_get_frame` always returns 0 and keeps the old frame, so watch `same`, not `err`. 9. After a reset the UI booted on Enroll (pauses after 30 s). 10. Fed/skip flags were RAM-only → a reset could re-serve an eaten meal. 11. `g_last_fed` was never read → no gap between two due meals. 12. The limit-hit path left stale `fed_min`/`fed_g`.

44	## Design decisions worth keeping
45	- **At-most-once feeding:** `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/fed.bin` (magic `VPF1`, via `velapaw_store_put/get`) is saved BEFORE the dispense; `FEED_GAP_MIN` 20; a slot closed by the daily limit shows "skipped"; skips restore only on the same day.
46	- **Stall monitor:** a prio+10 thread (2 KB stack) watches the UI heartbeat (2 min; 10 min while the tag is `feed`) and the recognition worker (1 min). A prio+5 note thread (6 KB) writes `STALL <kind> at <tag> <age>s | <health line>` to flash, then `up_systemreset()` (reset code 0x03); it waits at most 3 s for the note. Started right before the main loop. **Not a HW watchdog** — an interrupts-off hang isn't caught.
47	- **health.log** = `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/health.log`, rotates at 4 KB into `health.old`. Boot line `HH:MM boot rst 0xNN`; every 10 min `HH:MM up Nm tab T cap N max Nms slow N same N err N embed N hit N miss N inf S drop N`. `velapaw voice` (read-only probe) prints the live line + the boot code.
48	- **There is NO software-reset command in this build:** `reboot` → `nsh: reboot: command not found` (2026-10-18), probably because `CONFIG_BOARDCTL_RESET` is off. **Don't suggest ai_agent's `restart`**: without BOARDCTL_RESET it prints "Restarting..." and sleeps forever, which parks the agent CLI. The RESET button gives 0x01, so the 0x03 → start-on-Recognize path can only be exercised by a real stall.
49	- Reset codes (`esp32s3_reset_reasons(0)`): 0x01 power-on/brown-out/RESET button, **0x03 CORE_SW = the stall monitor's `up_systemreset()`**, 0x07/0x08 MWDT, 0x09 RTC WDT, 0x0f brown-out, 0x15/0x16 USB UART/JTAG (esptool). Any other code than 0x01/0x15/0x16, with pets enrolled, boots on Recognize.
50	- Never patch `ui_i18n.c` — stab1 reuses `S_POINT_AT_PET`, `S_NEXT_MEAL_FMT`, `S_SKIPPED`.
51	
52	## Gotchas
53	- All velapaw sources are **LF** — an in-session note that said CRLF was wrong.
54	- No LVGL heap metric (`CONFIG_LV_USE_CLIB_MALLOC=y`) and a heap walk kills the board ([[velapaw-heap-walk-kills-board]]).
55	- Thread stacks come from IMEM (~64 KB headroom before stab1's 8 KB).
56	- Pre-existing VM warnings outside the patched files — ignore: `ui_i18n.c:245` `f14` set but not used; `agent_loop.c:740` `-Wformat-truncation`.
57	- Local compile check: `cc_check.sh <a|b> <file>` = arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.4 after `source /d/openVela/vela-env.sh`, flags from `compile_commands.json`, item8/b headers (`identity.h` 564256ad, `ui_i18n.h` 778b1a32). The VM is xtensa GCC 12.2, so the VM warning gate is the real check.
58	- Still-ungated prints (feeder, TFLM, BCS lazy init, identity, boot init, camera + LVGL syslog): a jam there now ends in a stall reset + a log line instead of a silent hang.
59	- A stall reset re-enumerates USB: reopen COM8, redo `ifconfig eth0 …`, ping to prime ARP ([[velapaw-cdcncm-networking]]).
60	
61	Offered, not done: HW watchdog (`CONFIG_WATCHDOG` + automonitor), `CONFIG_BOARD_RESET_ON_ASSERT`, syslog hardening, auto-ifconfig after a reset, idle return to Recognize, a camera HAL that returns -1 / re-inits. Related: [[velapaw-agent-on-lcd]] (the open `llm_cache` fix), [[velapaw-scheduled-feeding]], [[velapaw-recognize-tuning]].

11	**Verdict.** Code read in the stab1b `b/` sources; the board image is `50a701e8`.
12	
13	**The counting is right:**
14	- feeds land in the right day;
15	- the window rolls at midnight and on every clock-lost boot;
16	- history survives resets;
17	- today's grams, the meal count, the week total and the 60 g hard cap are all correct.
18	
19	**The scoring is wrong.**
20	
21	**Screen (My Pets, the Trends line, the bell)**
22	- `pet_appetite_pct` = today ÷ `daily_limit_g`, capped at 100 (`ui_lvgl.c:1365-1377`).
23	- `pet_alert_drop` fires when yesterday < half the limit.
24	- With Bob's numbers (13 g portion × 3 meals = 39 g, 60 g limit):
25	  - a perfect day = 65%, shown amber (green needs ≥70%);
26	  - 09:54 after breakfast = 21%, shown red;
27	  - the alert fires on any day under 30 g, so **missing one meal of three** is enough.
28	- My Pets then reads "⚠ Appetite drop (21%)": yesterday's flag next to today's running %.
29	
30	**status.md (what the agent reads, `store_stub.c:582-623`)**
31	- The baseline is the sum of the 29 prior days ÷ 29 **always**, but the window was wiped on 2026-10-11.
32	  - 10-18 read 13/29 = 0 g/day, then a hard-coded "100% of baseline".
33	  - Once it fills a little, e.g. 117/29 = 4, a normal 39 g day reads 975%.
34	- Its alert (yesterday < half the ÷28 average) fires only on a near-zero day.
35	- The "Avg: X g/day" on My Pets and Trends is the same deflated number.
36	- **So the bell and the agent can disagree.**
37	
38	**No battery, so a "day" is really a power-on session (stab1b)**
39	- The last short session becomes "yesterday" at the next plug-in, which turns the bell red.
40	- This is the most likely cause of the red bell in the 09:54 photo.
41	- To confirm it on the device:
42	  - tap the bell: a "bob: sudden appetite drop…" line means the rule above; a line with a time stamp means the agent heartbeat (`g_ag_alert`);
43	  - on Trends, tap the second-to-last bar to see yesterday's grams.

46	- It turns red only on `pet_alert_drop()` for any pet, or on `g_ag_alert`.
47	- The BCS under/over lines appear in the popup but do NOT turn it red.
48	- Colours: `COL_FED` 0x57d977 green, `COL_COOL` 0xf0b24a amber, `COL_UNK` 0xe06464 red.

51	- The cold boot makes the last session before the slot (e.g. a venue check) "yesterday", so the bell goes red unless Bob got ≥30 g in it.
52	- A RESET keeps the clock (USB power stays), so only an unplug starts a new day.
53	- A boot at 08:00 only serves breakfast; lunch at 12:15 is 4 h 15 min later.

38	## Why it "hung" / stopped recognizing (ranked)
39	1. **`recog_done` latch** — after one match or 2 misses, Recognize waited for a tab re-entry; looks exactly like "fails to recognize". stab1 re-arms on a tap, on a scene change (4×4 brightness signature), and once a minute while a meal is due (its first 30 min); gap 30 s after a hit, 3 s doubling to 20 s after misses.

Rejected: a pipe relay (CONFIG_PIPES off) and a dup2 mute.
41	3. Midnight: `today_total` wasn't reconciled for a board running past midnight → a day that ended at the cap refused the next day's meals. Fix: `velapaw_store_sync_day()` on the UI's day change.

The camera HAL hides failures: `velapaw_camera_get_frame` always returns 0 and keeps the old frame, so watch `same`, not `err`. 9. After a reset the UI booted on Enroll (pauses after 30 s). 10. Fed/skip flags were RAM-only → a reset could re-serve an eaten meal. 11. `g_last_fed` was never read → no gap between two due meals. 12. The limit-hit path left stale `fed_min`/`fed_g`.

44	## Design decisions worth keeping
45	- **At-most-once feeding:** `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/fed.bin` (magic `VPF1`, via `velapaw_store_put/get`) is saved BEFORE the dispense; `FEED_GAP_MIN` 20; a slot closed by the daily limit shows "skipped"; skips restore only on the same day.
46	- **Stall monitor:** a prio+10 thread (2 KB stack) watches the UI heartbeat (2 min; 10 min while the tag is `feed`) and the recognition worker (1 min). A prio+5 note thread (6 KB) writes `STALL <kind> at <tag> <age>s | <health line>` to flash, then `up_systemreset()` (reset code 0x03); it waits at most 3 s for the note. Started right before the main loop. **Not a HW watchdog** — an interrupts-off hang isn't caught.
47	- **health.log** = `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/health.log`, rotates at 4 KB into `health.old`. Boot line `HH:MM boot rst 0xNN`; every 10 min `HH:MM up Nm tab T cap N max Nms slow N same N err N embed N hit N miss N inf S drop N`. `velapaw voice` (read-only probe) prints the live line + the boot code.
48	- **There is NO software-reset command in this build:** `reboot` → `nsh: reboot: command not found` (2026-10-18), probably because `CONFIG_BOARDCTL_RESET` is off. **Don't suggest ai_agent's `restart`**: without BOARDCTL_RESET it prints "Restarting..." and sleeps forever, which parks the agent CLI. The RESET button gives 0x01, so the 0x03 → start-on-Recognize path can only be exercised by a real stall.
49	- Reset codes (`esp32s3_reset_reasons(0)`): 0x01 power-on/brown-out/RESET button, **0x03 CORE_SW = the stall monitor's `up_systemreset()`**, 0x07/0x08 MWDT, 0x09 RTC WDT, 0x0f brown-out, 0x15/0x16 USB UART/JTAG (esptool). Any other code than 0x01/0x15/0x16, with pets enrolled, boots on Recognize.
50	- Never patch `ui_i18n.c` — stab1 reuses `S_POINT_AT_PET`, `S_NEXT_MEAL_FMT`, `S_SKIPPED`.

28	[10] P<heading 2> Abstract
29	[11] P<Normal (Web)> An ordinary timed feeder cannot tell which animal is standing at the bowl, so in a multi-pet household per-pet portioning and per-pet weight control are impossible — and per-pet portioning is the first thing a vet prescribes. VelaPaw, built on openVela (NuttX) and a Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5-C, identifies the individual pet on-device from a single camera and gates dispensing on two conditions together: the pet is recognised, and one of its meals is due today and unfed. Recognition uses open-set metric learning rather than classification — the model emits only a 128-dimensional L2-normalised embedding, so enrolling a new pet is a pure runtime operation requiring no retraining and no firmware update. Measured results: porting an INT8 operator library to Xtensa LX7, for which openVela ships none, cut inference from 6.75 s to 1.31 s; tracing a display fault with a logic analyser to panel bit-desynchronisation allowed a move to 40 MHz hardware SPI with GDMA, cutting full-screen repaint from 246 ms to 61 ms; and trimming 20 unused tools compressed the ai_agent request body from 19,391 B to fit NuttX's IOB pool, taking end-to-end latency from 150–300 s to 3.6–35.6 s. All image processing and every feeding decision happen on-device and no image ever leaves the hardware; the only networked component, ai_agent, uses a custom Skill to read the records the feeder writes to littlefs and speaks only when an appetite threshold is crossed. Unplugged from the network, the feeder behaves identically.

31	[13] P<heading 3> 3.1 Introduction
32	[14] P<heading 4> 3.1.1 Background and problem statement
33	[15] P<Normal (Web)> In a multi-pet household, an ordinary timed feeder has a structural flaw: it does not know which animal is standing at the bowl. The lid opens on schedule, whoever arrives first eats everything, and the slower one goes hungry. Per-pet portions, per-pet weight control, per-pet appetite monitoring — none of it is possible. And per-pet portioning is precisely the first thing a vet asks for when prescribing a weight-loss, disease-management, or post-operative plan.
34	[16] P<Normal (Web)> Existing camera-equipped feeders — for instance the Xiaomi Mijia Smart Pet Feeder 2 Vision Edition, launched March 2026 at ¥449 crowdfunded / ¥549 retail — solve the problem of letting the owner see the bowl; what the camera produces is a video stream. They do not solve identifying which animal it is. Such products also bind the camera feed to a cloud account, which is the single largest source of hesitation pet owners have about a household camera.
35	[17] P<Normal (Web)> VelaPaw therefore defines its problem as:
36	[18] P<Normal> On an MCU-class device, with no network, no cloud, and no phone app, use a single camera to tell which pet is at the bowl, and dispense only the meal that pet is due right now; then keep a long-term record of each pet's intake and proactively tell the owner when appetite goes wrong. 
37	[19] P<Normal (Web)> That last "proactively tell the owner" layer is carried by openVela's ai_agent framework and is the only part of the system that needs a network. The feeder itself behaves identically offline.
38	[20] P<heading 4> 3.1.2 Technical challenges
39	[21] TABLE
40	    r0: Challenge | What it looked like
41	    r1: ① Compute for fine-grained on-device recognition | Individual pet ID is a fine-grained recognition problem requiring a MobileNet-class backbone plus a metric-learning head. Running that model on Xtensa LX7 through TFLite-Micro's reference kernels takes ≈6.75 s per inference — unusable. An early TFLM spike (docs/TFLM_SPIKE_REPORT.md, run in QEMU, not on S3) profiled a comparable INT8 CNN and found CONV_2D accounts for 84% of the clock (643,819 of 768,105 ticks): latency is almost entirely decided by the INT8 convolution kernels. Yet the openVela tree ships only cmsis-nn (ARM) and nnlib-hifi4 (HiFi DSP) — there is no operator library for LX7.
42	    r2: ② Adding a pet must not require retraining | No consumer product can ask a user to retrain a model to add a cat. N-way classification had to be abandoned in favour of open-set metric learning, with a threshold that holds up under real household lighting.
43	    r3: ③ The model does not fit the MCU's memory map | A 1.44 MB identity model cannot be memory-mapped as a const array — the ESP32-S3 DROM0 MMU window saturates well before that. It must be read from raw flash into PSRAM; but a flash read suspends the CPU cache, and PSRAM is reached through that cache, so if the loading thread's stack lives in PSRAM the whole SoC deadlocks.
44	    r4: ④ The hardware-SPI display "renders nothing" | Full-screen writes worked; any partial window (a CASET/RASET sub-rectangle followed by RAMWR) never appeared — while the identical byte sequence over bit-banged GPIO worked perfectly. This survived roughly 60 rounds of blind rebuilds.
45	    r5: ⑤ ai_agent's request body vs. the network buffer | ai_agent registers 36 tools by default, whose JSON schemas push a single LLM request body to 19,391 B, of which 9,946 B is tool schema. NuttX's IOB pool is only NBUFFERS(64) × BUFSIZE(196) = 12,544 B, leaving roughly 7,840 B usable after THROTTLE(24). The request is far larger than the available buffer; the symptom is an intermittent hang with no timeout.
46	    r6: ⑥ Agent answers that look right but are fabricated | The heartbeat replayed its own history; list_dir's prefix match plus a local-tool shortcut handed (no files found) straight to the user as a final answer; ask was truncated at the seventh word by MAX_ARGS. None of these raise an error — they simply make the answer fluent and wrong.
47	[22] P<heading 4> 3.1.3 Innovations
48	[23] P<Normal list1.0> Dual-condition "recognition × schedule" gating. Food is dispensed only when "this is that pet" and "one of its meals is due today and has not been fed" are both true — at most once per meal per day, with any meal individually skippable. Recognition alone would feed the greedy one all day; a timer alone would feed whoever happened to walk past. This AND gate is the core product logic and the precondition for per-pet portioning to mean anything.
49	[24] P<Normal list1.0> Open-set metric learning instead of a classifier. The model is only a generic pet feature extractor, mapping a 128×128 frame to an L2-normalised 128-dimensional embedding. Enrolment = store the mean embedding of a few photos; recognition = cosine similarity. Adding a pet is a pure runtime operation — no retraining, no firmware update.
50	[25] P<Normal list1.0> A bug that survived 60 rebuilds turned into a 4× speedup. A logic analyser disproved the "software problem" hypothesis and reframed it as a panel bit-synchronisation problem (§3.4.3). With that fixed, the display moved from bit-banging to 40 MHz hardware SPI + GDMA: full-screen repaint 246 ms → 61 ms.
51	[26] P<Normal list1.0> ai_agent as a silent health monitor, not a chatbot. A heartbeat task periodically reads the records the feeder itself wrote to flash and speaks only when a threshold is crossed. When everything is fine, the device says nothing. The custom Skill states explicitly that only numbers from those files may be used, and nothing may be invented.
52	[27] P<Normal list1.0> A clear "offline-first, network-optional" boundary. Every feeding decision and all image processing happen on-device; no image ever leaves the device. Unplug the network and the feeder behaves identically — only the Agent layer stops. This is both a privacy claim and a reliability claim.
53	[28] P<Normal list1.0> Pocket-by-pocket mechanical dosing. A continuously rotating paddle rotor replaces a flap: a flap's dose drifts with hopper level, whereas each rotor pocket has fixed volume, so grams = pockets × grams-per-pocket — making per-pet portioning true at the mechanical level too.

83	[58] P<heading 4> 3.2.2 Design decisions and rationale
84	[59] TABLE
85	    r0: Decision | Chosen | Rationale / rejected alternative
86	    r1: Recognition paradigm | Open-set metric learning (cosine match) | Rejected N-way classification: every new pet would require retraining and an OTA — unacceptable in a consumer product. Metric learning reduces "add a pet" to writing one flash record. The cost is inherently weaker rejection of non-pet objects, so the lever is placed on enrolment quality (close, well-lit, front-facing) rather than on the threshold.
87	    r2: Inference runtime | TFLite-Micro + ESP-NN | An early spike using the in-tree tflm_benchmark in a simulator confirmed integration works, all operators are covered, and the tensor arena is only 84,420 B (negligible against 8 MB PSRAM), and located the bottleneck in CONV_2D (84%). That determined the project would not be viable without LX7 SIMD kernels (ESP-NN).
88	    r3: Model storage | Raw flash partition, read into PSRAM at boot | Rejected memory-mapped const arrays: 1.44 MB far exceeds the DROM0 MMU window. Uses spi_flash_read instead; because a flash read suspends the cache, the reading thread's stack must live in internal SRAM (.bss), not PSRAM.
89	    r4: Dispenser mechanism | 28BYJ-48 stepper + paddle rotor | Rejected an MG90S servo + flap: a servo can only oscillate, and with the inlet and outlet 180° apart a zero-net-rotation wobble can never carry a pocket across — it dispenses the initial charge and then spins uselessly. A flap's dose also drifts with hopper level, which would destroy the per-pet portioning claim outright. A stepper's continuous unidirectional rotation makes grams = pockets × grams-per-pocket strictly true, and its gearbox gives the low-speed torque needed to resist jamming.
90	    r5: Carrier board | Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5-C | Same SoC as the official ESP32-S3-EYE, so the openVela port and all inference work carry over unchanged. But the product needs a capacitive touchscreen (enrolment, schedule editing, trends) and a hardware RTC (schedules stay correct across power loss) — the EYE has neither. Same platform, better carrier.
91	    r6: On-board networking | USB CDC-NCM composite device | Rejected RNDIS: Windows' rndismp6.sys hard-requires RNDIS on interface 0, which collides with the CDC-ACM console; the resulting Code-10 proved unavoidable. CDC-NCM makes the console (COM port) and the network interface (eth0) usable simultaneously over one USB cable. Rejected on-board Wi-Fi as the demo link: Wi-Fi works and remains in the configuration, but the USB composite link is far more reproducible in a demo setting.
92	    r7: Agent data bridge | Feeder writes Markdown; Agent reads it with read_file | Rejected custom tools / IPC / shared memory. After each feed the VelaPaw C application writes plain Markdown to /data/ai_agent/velapaw/{status,feed_log}.md, and the Agent reads it with the framework's own read_file. Zero new tools, zero new protocol, zero coupling: to the Agent it is an ordinary file; to the C application it is an fprintf.
93	    r8: Agent persistence | littlefs at 0x180000 mounted as /data | Rejected tmpfs: the API key, session history, and Skill files would have to be re-provisioned on every reboot. The littlefs partition starts at 0x180000 while write-flash 0x0 nuttx.bin writes only up to about 0x17ec80, so /data survives both reboots and firmware reflashes.
94	    r9: Cloud model | DeepSeek deepseek-chat | OpenAI-compatible API with native function-calling support in the framework; directly reachable domestically, with controllable latency and cost.

130	[69] P<Normal (Web)> ESP-NN integration and compliance. The 1.3 s figure depends on Espressif's ESP-NN (Apache-2.0) SIMD kernels, and that integration modifies the public repository apps/mlearning/tflite-micro. Per contest rules, changes to public repositories are submitted as a fork plus a PR against dev-ai-contest-2026 and are not merged into the team repository. Consequently this repository runs reference kernels out of the box (≈6.75 s), and ≈1.3 s once the ESP-NN fork is applied. The integration has three parts: (1) the library itself under apps/mlearning/esp-nn/; (2) seven kernel wrappers (conv, depthwise_conv, fully_connected, pooling, add, mul, softmax) placed in .../micro/kernels/esp_nn/; (3) a Makefile block compiling with -DESP_NN=1 -DCONFIG_NN_OPTIMIZED -mlongcalls that filters out the matching reference kernels to avoid duplicate symbols. 169	[92] P<heading 4> 3.3.5 Suggested improvements to openVela
170	[93] P<Normal (Web)> All six come from real hardware experience on this project, ordered by value to the next developer:
171	[94] P<Normal list3.0> Provide an official optimised TFLM kernel path for Xtensa LX7 (ESP-NN). The tree ships cmsis-nn (ARM) and nnlib-hifi4 (HiFi DSP) but nothing for LX7 — despite the ESP32-S3 being this contest's primary chip. The gap is 6.75 s → 1.3 s (5×), which directly decides whether on-device vision AI is viable on openVela at all. It should be a Kconfig option in-tree rather than something every team forks for themselves.
172	[95] P<Normal list3.0> mallinfo() / free / memdump hang holding the heap lock on a freshly booted board and kill the whole chip. ai_agent happens to call a heap walk as the very first statement of its agent task, so every ask froze the machine (initially misdiagnosed as a PSRAM problem). Suggestion: offer a non-blocking or timed variant of the heap-walk API, or at minimum document its locking semantics.
173	[96] P<Normal list3.0> ARCH_HAVE_EXTRA_HEAPS is a selected symbol and therefore never appears in a defconfig — yet it is one of the three symbols required to keep task stacks out of PSRAM, and missing any one of them deadlocks the first ask. Suggestion: state the dependency explicitly in the XTENSA_IMEM_USE_SEPARATE_HEAP help text.
174	[97] P<Normal list3.0> The default IOB pool does not match ai_agent's default request body. 36 default tools produce a 19 KB request against roughly 7.8 KB of usable IOB — presenting as an intermittent hang with no timeout, which is the hardest failure class to diagnose. Suggestion: ship a leaner default tool set for MCU targets, or assert on request size at startup.
175	[98] P<Normal list3.0> ai_agent's local-tool shortcut should be kept consistent with the tool registry. handle_nl_fast_path() runs before the LLM, so once its target tool is excluded the wrong result is returned to the user as the final answer, with no warning. Suggestion: validate at compile time that the shortcut table is a subset of the registered tools.
176	[99] P<Normal list3.0> Several config options can silently destroy a board and deserve Kconfig warnings: CONFIG_RTC (kills the USB console on this board), CONFIG_NETINIT_THREAD (hangs the whole board), CONFIG_DEBUG_USB_INFO (wedges the console). Likewise CONFIG_NSH_LINELEN silently truncates an input line at about 80 characters, so provisioning a file with echo … >> /long/path writes corrupted content without any error.

266	[182] P<heading 4> 3.4.3 Hardware design and board bring-up
267	[183] P<Normal (Web)> Was a new hardware platform adapted / were drivers developed? Yes. The Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5-C has no existing board support in openVela. This project added a complete board implementation on top of esp32s3-devkit (board/, 1,903 lines of C plus a 205-line defconfig), driving the following four peripherals from scratch:
268	[184] TABLE
269	    r0: Peripheral | Connection | Driver highlights
270	    r1: ST7796 touch panel / 320×480 | Hardware SPI2 + GDMA at 40 MHz; CLK=GPIO5, MOSI=GPIO1, CS=GPIO4; FT5x06 touch on I²C0 (SCL=7 / SDA=8) | See "the hardest debug" below. Pixel rows must pass through an internal-SRAM bounce buffer — SPI DMA cannot read PSRAM cache-coherently. Address-window setup was batched from 11 SPI calls down to 5 (LVGL resets the window on every putarea).
271	    r2: OV5640 camera | ESP32-S3 LCD_CAM peripheral with a GDMA receive channel, configured over SCCB/I²C; brought out on a 30 cm FFC with a 1:1 coupler | The preview was initially transposed 90° and tinted violet — two independent root causes. (a) Flip/mirror: bits 1 and 2 of 0x3820/0x3821 must be cleared, and the transposition itself can only be corrected in the software resample — the registers structurally cannot do it. (b) The BLC pattern register 0x4514 must be set to 0x88. The discriminator is a reusable rule: whole-frame hue is decisive — a flip or Bayer-phase error swaps red and blue and can never lose green, so violet (R+B, no G) means 0x4514, not the flip bits.
272	    r3: PCF85063 RTC | I²C0, raw register access | Deliberately does not use CONFIG_RTC — on this board it kills the USB CDC console. The boot time seed is designed as a floor anchored to the build date rather than a "anything before 2017 is invalid" plausibility test: the latter pins the board to one date forever with no way to correct it (wall_set_min only rewrites hours and minutes, and nsh has no date).
273	    r4: 28BYJ-48 stepper feeder | ULN2003 driver board, IN1–IN4 = GPIO9 / 10 / 11 / 43; separate 5 V supply, common ground only | Full-step sequence in software. IN4 must be GPIO43 (U0TXD), not GPIO44 (U0RXD) — GPIO44 is clamped and cannot drive the coil cleanly, which was the real cause of the early "buzzes but won't turn" (a pin problem, not a phase-order problem). GPIO43 is free because the console runs over USB-Serial/JTAG rather than UART0. The stepper must never use GPIO12–16 — those are the ES8311 codec's private I²S bus (not brought out to any header) and are already claimed by the voice feature.
274	    r5: ES8311 audio | I²S0: MCLK=12, BCLK=13, DIN=14, WS=15, DOUT=16; 16 kHz | Getting microphone capture working required locating and fixing a driver-layer defect: the RX TDM slot map was never programmed — the true root cause of the stalled RX channel. A PSRAM cache trap additionally forced a two-slot stream over an 18-buffer pool, with the live slot flipping per capture.
275	[185] P<Normal (Web)> The hardest debug: the hardware-SPI display. Full-screen writes worked, any partial window never appeared, and the identical byte sequence over bit-banging worked fine. It survived roughly 60 rebuilds — framebuffer mirroring, DMA on/off, software CS, PSRAM coherency, forced pin routing all had no effect.
276	[186] P<Normal list4.0> Method — measure, don't guess. The SPI pins are not brought out to any header, so the board firmware was made to mirror FSPID_OUT and FSPICLK_OUT onto spare header pins through the GPIO matrix, plus a trigger marker, and captured with a logic analyser (sigrok/PulseView + an FX2 clone). The decisive first step was a ground-truth test: drive four known square waves on the probe pins and refuse to trust any capture until they read cleanly. That step immediately exposed a wiring/grounding fault which had been the source of all the earlier "garbage" captures — only afterwards was the real capture trustworthy.
277	[187] P<Normal list4.0> Finding. The decode showed the ESP32 emitting byte-perfect CASET 00 28 00 8B / RASET 00 28 00 8B / RAMWR / pixels, with correct DC alignment, exactly eight clean clock edges per byte, and no glitches. The peripheral was innocent all along.
278	[188] P<Normal list4.0> Root cause. This panel's chip select is hardwired low, so it can never resynchronise its bit counter on a CS edge — it just keeps counting clocks. The firmware initialised the panel by bit-banging and only then handed the pads to the SPI peripheral; that handover adds or drops a single clock edge, and from that instant the panel is off by one bit. Every subsequent command decodes to garbage, RAMWR is never recognised, no pixels reach GRAM, and the screen keeps showing whatever bit-banging drew last — which looks exactly like "hardware SPI drew nothing".
279	[189] P<Normal list4.0> Fix. Hand the pads to SPI first, then hardware-reset the panel (a software reset will not do — the reset command itself would be misread), then run the entire init sequence over SPI. Once the panel resynchronises under SPI ownership, partial windows render correctly.
280	[190] P<Normal list4.0> Payoff. With the path open, the display left bit-banging behind for 40 MHz hardware SPI2 + GDMA: a full 480×320 repaint went from ≈246 ms to ≈61 ms (4×). A bug that looked like a dead end became a performance win.
281	[191] P<Normal (Web)> Mechanical design (hardware/). Gravity hopper → paddle rotor → chute → bowl. Every part is parametric OpenSCAD source plus print-ready STL (PLA/PETG, 0.2 mm layers, 3 perimeters, no supports), with a JLC-outsourced parts list. The camera is removed from the mainboard and mounted, via a 30 cm FFC and a 1:1 coupler, inside a cam_pod on a two-legged cam_mast that straddles the chute — so the screen faces the owner while the lens faces the pet. Safety warning: a reversed FFC is fatal at first power-on — board pin N lands on camera pin 25−N, shorting a power rail straight onto data or ground pins. The camera module's ground is also not internally common, so orientation cannot be confirmed by metering "through" the camera; it must be checked against the 1/24 silkscreen and bare-copper continuity (verified pin by pin on 2026-07-30).

386	[239] P<Normal> An honest reading of this result: EER 0.291 is a lower-bound-style figure measured on 39 individuals from a public pet dataset under open-set conditions. It measures the difficulty of "given any two images, are they the same animal", not the accuracy of the deployed product. The real scenario is far easier: a household typically has 2–4 pets, enrolment photos are taken close-up and front-facing by the owner, and the match threshold is 0.45 — above the EER threshold, deliberately biased towards refusing rather than mis-feeding. The dominant factor in false accepts and false rejects is enrolment quality, not the threshold; that is a structural property of open-set metric learning, since a generic feature extractor inherently struggles to reject arbitrary non-pet objects, which is why the product puts its lever on guiding the user to take tight, well-lit, front-facing photos. Work not yet done: long-run false-accept / false-reject statistics for the three household pets under the final camera pose (cam_mast mount, current colour calibration). The current three pets' embeddings were captured on a firmware build that had the violet colour cast; after the 0x4514 fix they must be re-enrolled, and any earlier field accuracy figure is not comparable. This report therefore gives no such number rather than giving an untrustworthy one.

395	[243] P<Normal list6.0> Power loss: the hardware RTC preserves time, and littlefs preserves pets, schedules, avatars, intake history, Agent sessions, and the API key. /data starts at 0x180000 while the firmware image ends around 0x17ec80, so even reflashing the firmware does not lose data.
396	[244] P<Normal list6.0> Network faults: see the degradation table in §3.2.3. An LLM failure prints an explicit [llm] API error NNN: and never produces a fabricated answer.
397	[245] P<Normal list6.0> Memory variation: this project deliberately reports no runtime heap-free figures — for the reason in fix #2 of §3.4.5: on this board the heap-walk APIs hang holding the lock and kill the chip, and the fix was to report status without walking the heap. The heap numbers the firmware prints are therefore assumed values, not measurements, and quoting them as a metric would be misleading. The real memory constraint is the compile-time XTENSA_IMEM_REGION_SIZE: at 0x30000, pthread_create returns ENOMEM; at 0x48000 the board reliably carries the ai_agent task, six pthreads, and velapaw's 48 KB stack. That binary can/cannot-create-a-thread result carries more information than an untrustworthy free-bytes number.
398	[246] P<Normal list6.0> Continuous run time: the longest controlled observation to date is the 600 s unattended window during demo recording (sleep 600), through which the heartbeat fired on schedule, the console stayed clean, and the Agent answered normally. Longer soak testing (24 h / 7 d) has not been performed; it is listed in §3.7.3 and no extrapolation is made here.
399	[247] P<Normal list6.0> Power consumption: not yet measured per-mode with a power analyser, so no figures are given. The design basis for low power is that recognition is triggered on demand rather than run continuously (avoiding a 1.3 s inference occupying both cores back-to-back) and that the stepper is driven only briefly when the gate passes; the stepper's ≈240 mA per phase is carried by the separate 5 V supply and does not pass through the mainboard. Quantitative measurement is listed as future work.

433	[275] P<heading 4> 3.7.2 Market outlook and commercial value
434	[276] P<Normal (Web)> Market signal. In March 2026 Xiaomi launched the Mijia Smart Pet Feeder 2 Vision Edition (¥449 crowdfunded / ¥549 retail) — a mass-market product built specifically to bring a camera into the feeding scenario. That is the company with the best read on what pet owners will pay for, independently validating VelaPaw's founding judgement with real money: the camera belongs on the feeder. VelaPaw takes the same judgement one step further — from "see the bowl" to "know which one it is", entirely on-device.
435	[277] P<Normal (Web)> Target users, in order of willingness to pay:
436	[278] P<Normal list10.0> Multi-pet households (core). The sharpest pain: portion management simply does not work with more than one animal. This is the one group whose problem cannot be solved without individual recognition.
437	[279] P<Normal list10.0> Owners managing prescription diets or weight loss. A vet's gram-level plan has to actually be executed and recorded; VelaPaw's daily caps plus per-pet history are exactly that record of execution.
438	[280] P<Normal list10.0> Privacy-sensitive owners. People unwilling to have household camera footage enter any cloud account. "Images never leave the device" is a hard property here, not a privacy-policy clause.

27	[9] P<heading 2> 摘要
28	[10] P<Normal (Web)> 多宠家庭的定时喂食器分不清食盆前站着的是哪一只，按只定量、按只控重因而无从谈起。VelaPaw 基于 openVela（NuttX）与 Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5-C，用单摄像头在端侧识别宠物个体，并以"识别 × 排程"双条件门控投喂：仅当认出该宠物、且它当天有一餐到点未喂时才出粮。识别采用开集度量学习而非分类器，模型只输出 128 维 L2 归一化嵌入，新增宠物为纯运行时操作，无需重训练、无需升级固件。实测成果：为 openVela 原本缺失的 Xtensa LX7 移植 INT8 算子库，单次推理由 6.75 s 降至 1.31 s；以逻辑分析仪定位屏幕位同步故障后改用 40 MHz 硬件 SPI + GDMA，全屏重绘由 246 ms 降至 61 ms；裁剪 20 个未用工具后，ai_agent 单轮请求体由 19 391 B 压入 NuttX IOB 池，端到端时延由 150–300 s 降至 3.6–35.6 s。图像处理与投喂决策全部在端侧完成，任何图像都不离开设备；唯一联网的 ai_agent 以自定义 Skill 读取喂食器写入 littlefs 的记录，仅在食欲越过阈值时才主动发声。断网后喂食器行为完全不变。
29	[11] P<heading 2> 三、技术报告
30	[12] P<heading 3> 3.1 绪论
31	[13] P<heading 4> 3.1.1 背景与问题定义
32	[14] P<Normal (Web)> 多宠家庭里，普通定时喂食器有一个结构性缺陷：它不知道站在食盆前的是哪一只宠物。到点开盖，先到的那只把所有粮都吃掉，慢的那只挨饿——按只定量、按只控重、按只观察食欲，全部无从谈起。而"按只定量"恰恰是宠物医生给出减重、控病、术后恢复方案时的第一条要求。
33	[15] P<Normal (Web)> 市面上已有的"视觉款"喂食器（例如 2026 年 3 月上市的小米米家智能宠物喂食器 2 视觉版，众筹 ¥449 / 零售 ¥549）解决的是"让主人看得见食盆"，摄像头的产物是一路视频流；它并不解决"认出是哪一只"。这类产品同时把摄像头画面与账号绑定上云——这是宠物主人对家庭摄像头最主要的顾虑来源。
34	[16] P<Normal (Web)> 因此 VelaPaw 定义的问题是：
35	[17] P<Normal> 在一台 MCU 级设备上，不联网、不上云、不用手机 App，仅凭一颗摄像头就分辨出食盆前是哪一只宠物，并只投喂"这一只、此时此刻该吃的那一餐"；同时把每只宠物的进食量长期记录下来，在食欲异常时主动告知主人。 
36	[18] P<Normal (Web)> "主动告知"这一层由 openVela 的 ai_agent 框架承担，是全系统唯一需要联网的部分；喂食器本体在断网状态下功能完全不变。
37	[19] P<heading 4> 3.1.2 技术难点
38	[20] TABLE
39	    r0: 难点 | 具体表现
40	    r1: ①端侧细粒度识别的算力** | 宠物个体识别属于细粒度识别，需要 MobileNet 级主干 + 度量学习头。在 Xtensa LX7 上用 TFLite-Micro 参考算子跑该模型需 ≈6.75 s/次，完全不可用。前期 TFLM 摸底（docs/TFLM_SPIKE_REPORT.md，在 QEMU 模拟器上进行，非 S3 实测）用 profiler 定量确认了同类 INT8 CNN 的时间分布：CONV_2D 占单次推理 84% 的时钟（643 819 / 768 105 ticks），即延迟几乎完全由 INT8 卷积核决定，而 openVela 树内只有 cmsis-nn(ARM) 与 nnlib-hifi4(HiFi DSP)，没有面向 LX7 的算子库。
41	    r2: ②"新增一只宠物"不能重训 | 消费产品不可能让用户为了加一只猫去训练模型。必须放弃 N 分类，改用开集度量学习，且阈值要在真实光照下站得住。
42	    r3: ③大模型放不进 MCU 的内存映射 | 1.44 MB 的身份模型无法作为 const 数组内存映射——ESP32-S3 的 DROM0 MMU 窗口远在此之前就饱和。必须从裸 Flash 读入 PSRAM；而 Flash 读会挂起 CPU cache，而 PSRAM 正是经该 cache 访问的，读模型的线程栈若落在 PSRAM 会直接死锁整颗 SoC。
43	    r4: ④硬件 SPI 屏幕"渲染不出来" | 全屏写正常，任何局部窗口（CASET/RASET 子矩形 + RAMWR）永不出图，而同样的字节序列走 GPIO 位翻转完全正常。该问题历经约 60 轮盲目编译未能解决。
44	    r5: ⑤ai_agent 在 MCU 上的请求体 vs. 网络缓冲 | ai_agent 默认注册 36 个工具，其 JSON schema 使单次 LLM 请求体达 19 391 B，其中 9 946 B 是工具 schema；而 NuttX 的 IOB 池仅 NBUFFERS(64) × BUFSIZE(196) = 12 544 B，扣除 THROTTLE(24) 后可用约 7 840 B。请求体远大于可用缓冲，表现为"时好时坏"的挂死，且无超时返回。
45	    r6: ⑥Agent 答案"看起来对"但其实是假的 | 心跳任务会重放自己的历史、list_dir 的前缀匹配与本地工具短路会把 (no files found) 直接当成最终答案交给用户、ask 在第 7 个词处被 MAX_ARGS 截断。这些缺陷都不会报错，只会让回答变得流畅而错误。
46	[21] P<heading 4> 3.1.3 创新点
47	[22] P<Normal list1.0> "识别 × 排程"双条件门控投喂——只有"认出的是这只宠物"且"它的某一餐已到点且今天未投"两个条件同时成立才投料，每餐每天至多一次，且每餐可单独跳过。只靠识别会把贪吃的那只喂一整天；只靠定时又会喂到碰巧路过的那只。这个"与"门是整个产品的核心逻辑，也是"按只定量"能成立的前提。
48	[23] P<Normal list1.0> 开集度量学习替代分类器——模型只做"通用宠物特征提取器"，把 128×128 帧映射成 L2 归一化的 128 维嵌入；登记 = 存若干张照片的平均嵌入；识别 = 余弦相似度匹配。新增宠物是纯运行时操作，无需重训、无需固件更新。
49	[24] P<Normal list1.0> 把一个卡了 60 轮的 bug 变成 4× 提速——用逻辑分析仪把"软件问题"证伪为"面板位同步问题"（详见 3.4.3），修复后顺势把显示从位翻转升级为 40 MHz 硬件 SPI + GDMA，全屏重绘 246 ms → 61 ms。
50	[25] P<Normal list1.0> ai_agent 作为"沉默的健康监护"，而不是聊天机器人——心跳任务定期读取喂食器自己写在 Flash 上的记录，只在越过阈值时才开口；一切正常时设备完全沉默。自定义 Skill 明确规定"只能使用文件里的数字，绝不臆造"。
51	[26] P<Normal list1.0> "离线为主、联网为辅"的清晰边界——所有投喂决策与全部图像处理都在端侧完成，没有任何图像离开设备；拔掉网线，喂食器行为完全不变，只是 Agent 层停止工作。这既是隐私主张，也是可靠性主张。
52	[27] P<Normal list1.0> 逐"兜"定量的机械设计——用连续单向旋转的叶轮转子取代翻板：翻板的投放量随料斗余量漂移，而转子每格容积固定，克数 = 格数 × 每格克数，使"按只定量"在机械层面也成立。

81	[56] P<heading 4> 3.2.2 方案论证与选型
82	[57] TABLE
83	    r0: 决策点 | 最终选型 | 论证 / 被否方案
84	    r1: 识别范式 | 开集度量学习（余弦匹配） | 否决 N 分类：每加一只宠物都要重训并 OTA，消费产品不可接受。度量学习把"加宠物"降级为写一条 Flash 记录。代价是对"非宠物物体"的拒识天然较弱，因此把杠杆放在登记质量（近距、光照良好的正脸）而非阈值本身。
85	    r2: 推理运行时 | TFLite-Micro + ESP-NN | 前期用树内 tflm_benchmark 在模拟器上摸底，确认 集成可行、算子全覆盖、张量竞技场仅 84 420 B（8 MB PSRAM 下可忽略），并定位延迟瓶颈在 CONV_2D（84%）。据此判定必须引入 LX7 SIMD 算子（ESP-NN），否则方案不成立。

166	[89] P<heading 4> 3.3.5 对 openVela 的改进建议
167	[90] P<Normal (Web)> 以下 6 条均来自本项目真机踩坑，按"对下一位开发者的价值"排序：
168	[91] P<Normal list3.0> 为 Xtensa LX7 提供官方的 TFLM 优化算子路径（ESP-NN）。树内现有 cmsis-nn（ARM）与 nnlib-hifi4（HiFi DSP），唯独缺少 LX7；而 ESP32-S3 是本届大赛的主力芯片。差距是 6.75 s → 1.3 s（5×），直接决定"端侧视觉 AI 在 openVela 上是否可用"。建议以 Kconfig 开关的形式内置，而非让每支队伍各自 fork。
169	[92] P<Normal list3.0> mallinfo() / free / memdump 在刚启动的板子上会持锁挂死整颗芯片。本项目中 ai_agent 恰好把堆遍历放在 agent 任务的第一条语句，于是每一次 ask 都冻结全机（曾一度被误判为 PSRAM 问题）。建议：堆遍历接口增加非阻塞/超时形态，或至少在文档中标注其持锁语义。
170	[93] P<Normal list3.0> ARCH_HAVE_EXTRA_HEAPS 是 select 符号，永远不出现在 defconfig 中。而它恰恰是"任务栈不落在 PSRAM"的三个必要符号之一，缺一个就在首次 ask 时死锁。建议在 XTENSA_IMEM_USE_SEPARATE_HEAP 的帮助文本中显式提示这一依赖。
171	[94] P<Normal list3.0> IOB 池默认容量与 ai_agent 的默认请求体不匹配。默认 36 个工具产生 19 KB 请求体，而默认 IOB 可用约 7.8 KB，症状是无超时的间歇挂死——最难排查的一类故障。建议：ai_agent 默认精简工具集，或在 MCU 目标上对请求体大小做启动期断言。

261	[177] P<Normal (Web)> 是否完成全新硬件平台适配 / 驱动开发：是。Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5-C 在 openVela 中没有现成板级支持。本项目在 esp32s3-devkit 基础上新增了一份完整的板级实现（board/，共 1 903 行 C 代码 + 205 行 defconfig），从零驱动了以下四类外设：
262	[178] TABLE
263	    r0: 外设 | 接法 | 驱动实现要点
264	    r1: ST7796 触摸屏 / 320×480 | 硬件 SPI2 + GDMA，40 MHz；CLK=GPIO5, MOSI=GPIO1, CS=GPIO4；触摸 FT5x06 走 I²C0(SCL=7/SDA=8) | 见下方"最硬的一处调试"。像素行需经内部 SRAM 中转缓冲——SPI DMA 无法 cache 一致地读 PSRAM；地址窗口设置从 11 次 SPI 调用合并为 5 次（LVGL 每次 putarea 都会重设窗口）。
265	    r2: OV5640 摄像头 | ESP32-S3 LCD_CAM 外设 + GDMA 接收通道，SCCB/I²C 配置；经 30 cm FFC + 1:1 转接板外引 | 预览曾出现90° 转置 + 紫色偏色，两个独立根因：（a）翻转/镜像位——须清除 0x3820/0x3821 的 bit1+bit2，转置本身只能在软件重采样中修正，寄存器结构上做不到；（b）BLC pattern 寄存器 0x4514 须置 0x88。判别方法是一条可复用的规律：整帧色相是决定性判据——翻转/Bayer 相位错误只会红蓝互换、绝不可能丢掉绿色，因此"紫色（R+B 无 G）"必然是 0x4514，不是翻转位。
266	    r3: PCF85063 RTC | I²C0，裸寄存器读写 | 刻意不使用 CONFIG_RTC——在本板上它会杀死 USB-CDC 控制台。开机时间种子设计为以构建日期为下限的地板值而非"早于 2017 即视为无效"的合理性判断：后者会把板子永久钉在某一天且无法纠正（wall_set_min 只改时分，nsh 没有 date）。
267	    r4: 28BYJ-48 步进投料 | ULN2003 驱动板，IN1–IN4 = GPIO9 / 10 / 11 / 43；5 V 独立供电，仅共地 | 软件走全步序列。IN4 必须用 GPIO43（U0TXD）而不是 GPIO44（U0RXD）——GPIO44 被钳位，线圈驱动不干净，这正是早期"电机嗡嗡响但不转"的根因（是引脚问题，不是相序问题）。GPIO43 可用是因为控制台走 USB-Serial/JTAG 而非 UART0。严禁把步进放在 GPIO12–16——那是 ES8311 编解码器独占的 I²S 总线（未引到任何排针），已被语音功能占用。
268	    r5: ES8311 音频 | I²S0：MCLK=12, BCLK=13, DIN=14, WS=15, DOUT=16；16 kHz | 为打通麦克风采集，定位并修复了驱动层缺陷：从未编程 RX 的 TDM slot map（RX 通道卡死的真正根因）。另有 PSRAM cache 陷阱迫使采用 18 缓冲池的双 slot 流（活动 slot 每次采集翻转）。
269	[179] P<Normal (Web)> 最硬的一处调试：硬件 SPI 屏幕。症状是全屏写正常、任何局部窗口永不出图，而完全相同的字节序列走位翻转却正常；该问题熬过了约 60 轮编译（帧缓冲镜像、DMA 开关、软件 CS、PSRAM 一致性、引脚强制路由等全部无效）。
270	[180] P<Normal list4.0> 方法——测量，而不是猜。SPI 引脚没有引到排针，无法直接探测，于是让板级固件通过 GPIO 矩阵把 FSPID_OUT/FSPICLK_OUT 镜像到空闲排针，另加一路触发标记，用逻辑分析仪（sigrok/PulseView + FX2）抓取。决定性的第一步是"地面真值"测试：先在探针脚上输出 4 路已知方波，读不干净就绝不相信任何采集——这一步立刻暴露了一个接线/接地问题，此前的"乱码"全部源于此；只有在此之后，真正的采集才是可信的。
271	[181] P<Normal list4.0> 发现。解码结果显示 ESP32 发出的是逐字节完全正确的 CASET 00 28 00 8B / RASET 00 28 00 8B / RAMWR / pixels，DC 对齐正确、每字节恰好 8 个干净时钟沿、零毛刺。外设自始至终是清白的。
272	[182] P<Normal list4.0> 根因。该面板的片选被硬件拉低，因此它永远无法借助 CS 边沿重新同步位计数器——它只会一直数时钟沿。固件先用位翻转完成面板初始化，之后才把引脚交给 SPI 外设；这次引脚交接会让时钟多出/少掉一个沿，从那一刻起面板就错开了一位。此后每条命令都被解码成垃圾，RAMWR 永不被识别，没有像素进入 GRAM，屏幕就一直显示位翻转最后画上去的内容——看起来正好像"硬件 SPI 什么都没画"。
273	[183] P<Normal list4.0> 修复。先把引脚交给 SPI 外设，再硬件复位面板（软件复位不行——复位命令自己就会被读错），然后整套初始化全部走 SPI。面板在 SPI 所有权下重新同步之后，局部窗口即正常渲染。
274	[184] P<Normal list4.0> 收益。路径打通后，显示彻底脱离位翻转，改用 40 MHz 硬件 SPI2 + GDMA：全屏 480×320 重绘 ≈246 ms → ≈61 ms（4×）。一个看似死路的 bug 变成了性能提升。
275	[185] P<Normal (Web)> 机械设计（hardware/）。重力料斗 → 叶轮转子 → 落料槽 → 食盆。全部零件为参数化 OpenSCAD 源码 + 可直接打印的 STL（PLA/PETG，0.2 mm 层高，3 圈外壁，无支撑），含 JLC 代打件清单。摄像头从主板拔下，经 30 cm FFC + 1:1 转接板装在跨过落料槽的 cam_mast 双腿支架上的 cam_pod 内，使屏幕朝向主人、镜头朝向宠物。安全警示：FFC 反插在上电瞬间是致命的——板端第 N 脚会对上相机第 25−N 脚，把电源轨直接短到数据/地脚；且该相机模组内部地未共通，无法"穿过相机"用万用表确认方向，只能依据丝印 1/24 与裸铜连通性核对（已在 2026-07-30 逐点验证）。

11	**Improvement item 8, SHIPPED 2026-10-13.** The user's goal: judges should see
12	the agent on the LCD instead of in a terminal — "watch the feeder change",
13	not "read the terminal".

16	**How to apply:** demo with fresh sentences (see the cache note), judge success
17	by the `set_meal_schedule` trace line or `status.md`, never by the reply text,
18	and expect the toast within about a second of `ask`.

20	## What is on the screen (item-8 patch, 6 files)
21	
22	Rollback copy: `~/velapaw-golden/pre-item8-agent-lcd/`.
23	
24	- **Toast under the bell for every `ask`:** "You: <question>" → "Agent
25	  working… N s" counting up → the reply. It stays 30 s; a tap dismisses it.
26	- **Heartbeat:** an all-clear is a green toast for 10 s. A warning is a red
27	  toast that stays, turns the bell red and is listed in the bell panel until
28	  the next all-clear. A *failed* heartbeat shows nothing, so a dead network at
29	  the offline defense doesn't clutter the screen.
30	- **Live My Pets:** an identity generation counter makes the card redraw on
31	  whatever tab is showing. An open Edit dialog picks up the change too, so
32	  pressing Save can't write the old time back. Before this, My Pets only
33	  redrew when you entered the tab.
34	- Bilingual; the Chinese strings use only glyphs already in the font subset
35	  ([[velapaw-i18n]]).
36	
37	## fix9 — why "the toast works but the times don't change"
38	
39	6 files: `store.h`, `store_stub.c`, `identity.c`, `ui_lvgl.c`,
40	`tool_registry.c`, `nsh_commands.c`. Rollback:
41	`~/velapaw-golden/pre-fix9-status-refresh/`. Image
42	`148bf5d5eff85947a89e00eaafd538c3`.
43	
44	- `status.md` is the agent's only source of meal times, and it was rewritten
45	  only at boot and after a feed — one turn after moving breakfast, the agent
46	  read the old time back. It is now also rewritten after an agent change, an
47	  Edit or voice-dialog save, and a pet delete.
48	- The model answered "Done" without calling `set_meal_schedule`. The tool
49	  description now says a meal changes only when the tool succeeds.
50	- `ask` text carried raw backspace/arrow-key bytes from the terminal; they are
51	  now applied or dropped before the message is sent.
52	- **Still open, not in fix9. SEEN ON HARDWARE 2026-10-13:** sending
53	  `ask change bob's dinner to 18:20` twice in a row gave `Cache hit, skipping
54	  LLM call` and `END status=ok iters=1 tools=0 … elapsed=0s`. It replayed
55	  "Done — … 18:20" without calling `set_meal_schedule`. That time it was
56	  harmless, since the meal already was 18:20. After an Edit-dialog change it
57	  would be a false "Done".
58	- **How the cache works** (`src/llm/llm_cache.c` and `include/llm/llm_cache.h`;
59	  values read from the D: checkout, which is upstream code we never modified):
60	  - It is RAM-only, with 8 slots.
61	  - Entries expire after 300 s, but **every hit re-stores the entry and
62	    restarts the 300 s**.
63	  - The key is a djb2 hash of the prompt's first 64 characters, with no string
64	    compare. Long asks that differ only after character 64 therefore collide.
65	  - The store is at `agent_loop.c` `send_reply:` (~line 1451). It is gated
66	    only on `LLM_COMPLEXITY_SIMPLE` and the non-heartbeat `cacheable` flag.
67	- **Fix** = add `&& trace.total_tool_calls == 0` to that store condition. That
68	  counter is what the END line prints as `tools=`. Not applied yet. Until then,
69	  use a fresh sentence, wait 5 minutes, or restart `ai_agent`.
70
